data/adventures/countries.json:
{
  "about": "Authored countries a generated world may hold, each where its requirements fit: beyond a march on the side named, of a country of one of the terrains named. The first march a company reaches where one fits leads into it instead of a country drawn from the seed; each is placed once in a world (src/world/frontier.ts). Of the countries among one kind (the independent adventures), the first region's marches lead into only the one its seed chooses; the rest lie further out, each beyond a country drawn from the seed (Countries.plan), so that a world holds them all. Each says what the folk of the first region say of it (rumour, with {keeper} whoever keeps travellers in the town it is asked in), what it is asked about (topic), what the company knows of it once told (heard), what is said of it a country further off (far: \"where ...\"), what is seen of it from somewhere high in the country next to it, over the march (skyline: the builder's, from what its folk say of it, for its authors to rewrite), and, for one whose news is posted, the notice every town of the first region has nailed up (notice); and, for one that says when it is seen through, how the talk goes there after and what whoever keeps travellers says to the company come back from it (after).",
  "countries": [
    {
      "id": "longman",
      "bundle": "the-long-man/placed.json",
      "entry": "road_end",
      "marker": "long_man",
      "side": "north",
      "beside": [
        "mountain",
        "forest",
        "marsh",
        "frost",
        "desert"
      ],
      "name": "Merrowdale",
      "topic": "the forty crowns in Merrowdale",
      "terrain": "mountain",
      "rumour": "'Up the north road there is Merrowdale,' says {keeper}. 'There is a long ridge across the head of the dale, and they say a giant king is buried under it. Something tall walks the crest at night. The steward has posted forty crowns to have it laid.'",
      "heard": "Up the north road lies Merrowdale, where a giant king is said to be buried under the long ridge, and something tall walks its crest at night.",
      "skyline": "a long ridge laid straight across the head of a dale, too straight for a hill",
      "far": "a giant king is buried under a long ridge, and something tall walks its crest at night",
      "notice": {
        "name": "a notice from Merrowdale",
        "text": "A notice in a clerk's hand, carried down from Merrowdale and nailed up where travellers will see it: WHOEVER LAYS THE MOWER THAT WALKS THE LONG MAN SHALL HAVE FORTY CROWNS OF THE STEWARD. A. VENN, FOR THE LORD. Under it someone has written: up the north road, over the march, three days at most.",
        "talk": "A notice from Merrowdale is nailed up where travellers will see it, and half the talk is of the forty crowns it offers and the other half of why nobody has gone."
      },
      "after": {
        "talk": "A notice from Merrowdale still hangs where travellers will see it, curling at the corners. Nobody talks of the forty crowns now: the word down the north road is that the Long Man is quiet.",
        "told": "{keeper} hears you out, all of it, without a word. 'There was word of it already,' {keeper} says then. 'Off the north road: the thing on the ridge is quiet, and nobody up there talks of forty crowns any more. Nobody said who.' {keeper} looks at you a while longer, then reaches up and takes the notice from Merrowdale down, and puts it on the fire."
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "thrume",
      "bundle": "thrume/placed.json",
      "entry": "salt_road",
      "marker": "thane_ring",
      "side": "east",
      "beside": [
        "mountain",
        "frost",
        "forest"
      ],
      "name": "Thrume",
      "topic": "Saltgrave, over the march",
      "terrain": "mountain",
      "among": "independent",
      "rumour": "'East over the march, under the fells, there is a salt town, Saltgrave,' says {keeper}. 'People pay to sleep there, and some of them do not come home. And the giants have come down off the mountain, they say, for the first time anyone remembers.'",
      "heard": "East over the march lies Saltgrave, a salt town under the fells, where people pay to sleep and some do not come home, and the giants have come down off the mountain.",
      "skyline": "smoke going up from salt-pans under the fells",
      "far": "people pay to sleep in a salt town under the fells, and some of them do not come home"
    },
    {
      "id": "strewnfield",
      "bundle": "house-that-grows/placed.json",
      "entry": "rim",
      "marker": "kezu_cup",
      "side": "south",
      "beside": [
        "marsh",
        "forest",
        "desert"
      ],
      "name": "the Strewnfield",
      "topic": "the room of glass in the Strewnfield",
      "terrain": "marsh",
      "among": "independent",
      "rumour": "'South, in the Strewnfield,' says {keeper}, 'a room of glass fell into a barley field by Cobble Ring. It grows, they say, wherever nobody is watching it. They sit up with it all night on stools.'",
      "heard": "South over the march lies the Strewnfield, where a room of glass fell into a barley field by Cobble Ring, and grows wherever nobody watches it.",
      "skyline": "a flash in the fields, like a window where no house stands",
      "far": "a room of glass fell into a barley field, and grows wherever nobody is watching it"
    },
    {
      "id": "corrow",
      "bundle": "let-one-remember/placed.json",
      "entry": "eighth_bend",
      "marker": "teshen",
      "side": "west",
      "beside": [
        "forest",
        "marsh"
      ],
      "name": "the Corrow",
      "topic": "the mountain over the Corrow",
      "terrain": "mountain",
      "among": "independent",
      "rumour": "'West of here is the Corrow,' says {keeper}. 'There is a mountain hangs over it in the sky, on a chain, and they say it is drifting. And there is a well there nobody has been to the bottom of.'",
      "heard": "West over the march lies the Corrow, where a mountain hangs in the sky on a chain, drifting, over a well nobody has been to the bottom of.",
      "skyline": "a mountain hanging in the sky, with nothing under it but air",
      "far": "a mountain hangs in the sky on a chain, drifting, over a well nobody has been to the bottom of"
    },
    {
      "id": "ghessil",
      "bundle": "patient-star/placed.json",
      "entry": "square",
      "marker": "saro",
      "side": "west",
      "beside": [
        "mountain",
        "desert",
        "frost"
      ],
      "name": "the Ghessil Uplands",
      "topic": "the Ghessil Uplands",
      "terrain": "mountain",
      "among": "independent",
      "rumour": "'West, up on the Ghessil Uplands,' says {keeper}, 'there is a light lies on the glass that slows whatever drinks it. There are people standing in it, they say, that went in last autumn and are standing there yet, alive.'",
      "heard": "West over the march lie the Ghessil Uplands, where a light on the glass slows whatever drinks it, and people stand in it alive since last autumn.",
      "skyline": "a light lying on the uplands that does not move when the clouds do",
      "far": "a light lies on the glass that slows whatever drinks it, and people stand in it alive"
    },
    {
      "id": "lowwater",
      "bundle": "low-water/placed.json",
      "entry": "rim_road",
      "marker": "deep_gate",
      "side": "south",
      "beside": [
        "marsh",
        "forest",
        "frost"
      ],
      "name": "the Bowl of Ammerlin",
      "topic": "the falling water at Ammerlin",
      "terrain": "hills",
      "among": "independent",
      "rumour": "'South over the march there's a city down the inside of a crater, Ammerlin,' says {keeper}. 'Their lake's been going down three years, and nobody there will believe anybody else about why. So they've sent out for someone from outside to measure it, and put their name to the answer. The Office of Measures pays, if you can count.'",
      "heard": "South over the march lies the Bowl of Ammerlin, a city down the inside of a crater, whose lake has been falling for three years; its Office of Measures wants someone from outside to measure it and say why.",
      "skyline": "the rim of a great crater, with smoke going up out of it",
      "far": "a city down the inside of a crater is losing its lake, and nobody there believes anybody else about why"
    },
    {
      "id": "tessary",
      "bundle": "what-tessary-owes/placed.json",
      "entry": "causeway_end",
      "marker": "ossel",
      "side": "east",
      "beside": [
        "marsh"
      ],
      "name": "the Ossel delta",
      "terrain": "marsh",
      "rumour": "'Down the east road, where the marsh meets the sea, there's Tessary on the Ossel,' says {keeper}. 'Their legions came home from the war a week back, and they say some of the soldiers are getting up in the night and walking into the sea. Barefoot, in step, eyes open. An eel-wife there has put up a notice: she'll give her savings to anyone who can tell her where her boy went.'",
      "heard": "East over the march lies Tessary on the Ossel, where the legions have come home from the war and some of the soldiers walk into the sea at night; an eel-wife there offers her savings for news of her son.",
      "skyline": "the smoke of a town where the marsh meets the sea",
      "far": "the legions have come home from the war, and some of the soldiers walk into the sea at night"
    },
    {
      "id": "wrayford",
      "bundle": "wrayford/placed.json",
      "entry": "drove_road",
      "marker": "maudie",
      "side": "south",
      "beside": [
        "mountain"
      ],
      "name": "the vale of the Wray",
      "topic": "the bridge at Wrayford",
      "terrain": "hills",
      "rumour": "'Down the south road, where the drove roads come down off the fells, there's Wrayford, on the Wray,' says {keeper}, and lowers their voice. 'The carters rose against the bridge toll there a few nights back, and the lord's riders hanged three of them off the gatehouse on the bridge, and they're hanging there yet. The reeve says they stay till the lord's captain comes. Drovers coming through say the whole town goes and stands under them, and nobody will say a word.'",
      "heard": "South over the march lies Wrayford, the bridge-city on the Wray, where the lord's riders hanged three carters from the gatehouse on the bridge after a rising against the toll, and the reeve keeps them hanging until the lord's captain comes.",
      "skyline": "a town at a bridge, far down where the drove roads come off the fells",
      "far": "the lord's riders hanged three carters from the gatehouse on the bridge, and they hang there yet"
    },
    {
      "id": "calamy",
      "bundle": "parliament-of-books/placed.json",
      "entry": "causey",
      "marker": "sewing_beam",
      "side": "east",
      "beside": [
        "frost"
      ],
      "name": "Calamy",
      "topic": "the city of paper at the mouth of the Calam",
      "terrain": "marsh",
      "rumour": "'East over the march, where the cold country comes down to the sea and the river runs out through miles of reeds, there is Calamy, at the mouth of the Calam,' says {keeper}. 'A city of paper: tide-mills and binders and printers, and every house there keeps a book that knows it. They say the books have started to talk. And they burn their old almanacks at the Kindling, which is near, and this year nobody can say whether they ought.'",
      "heard": "East over the march lies Calamy, at the mouth of the Calam, where every house keeps a book that knows it, and the books have begun to talk, and the Kindling is near.",
      "skyline": "the sails of tide-mills turning along a coast of reeds",
      "far": "the books of a city of paper have begun to talk, and the Kindling is near",
      "among": "independent"
    },
    {
      "id": "pentrice",
      "bundle": "gosses-company/placed.json",
      "entry": "road_end",
      "marker": "clemency",
      "side": "west",
      "beside": [
        "forest"
      ],
      "name": "the vale of the Arle",
      "topic": "the Trial of the Wheel at Pentrice",
      "terrain": "hills",
      "rumour": "'West over the march, where the Ise falls into the Arle, there's Pentrice,' says {keeper}. 'A minster town, very grand, where they license every word said on a stage and fine you for the rest. This week it's their Trial of the Wheel: three companies of players, three nights in a round playhouse over the river, and the best of them given a house of its own for ever.' {keeper} grins. 'They say old Absalom Gosse is going back for it, after forty years. They banned him from every stage inside the walls the last time. He started a riot.'",
      "skyline": "a minster tower over a river town, where one river falls into another",
      "far": "a minster town licenses every word said on a stage, and holds its Trial of the Wheel",
      "heard": "West over the march lies Pentrice, a minster town that licenses every word said on a stage; this week it holds its Trial of the Wheel, three companies of players for three nights, and Absalom Gosse's company is going back after forty years' banishment.",
      "notice": {
        "name": "a playbill of the Trial of the Wheel",
        "text": "A bill in red and black, much handled and rained on: THE TRIAL OF THE WHEEL AT PENTRICE. THREE COMPANIES OF PLAYERS. THREE NIGHTS. THE PATENT OF THE WHEEL TO BE GIVEN BY THE BENCH. BY LEAVE OF THE OFFICE OF PLAIN SPEECH. Under it someone has written in pencil: west road, over the march, a day; and drawn a bear.",
        "talk": "A playbill of the Trial of the Wheel at Pentrice is nailed up where travellers will see it, and half the talk is of who will win the Patent and the other half of whether old Gosse will be let play at all."
      },
      "after": {
        "talk": "A playbill of the Trial of the Wheel at Pentrice still hangs where travellers will see it, curling at the corners. The Trial is over: the word off the west road is all of what happened on the last night, and nobody tells it the same way twice.",
        "told": "{keeper} hears you out, all of it, from the Westgate to the verdict, and laughs in the right places, and once does not laugh at all. 'We heard some of it,' {keeper} says then. 'Off the west road. Not the half of it.' {keeper} reaches up and takes down the playbill of the Trial of the Wheel, and folds it, and puts it behind the bar, not on the fire."
      },
      "herald": {
        "scenario": "players.scenario.json",
        "exports": [
          "joined",
          "freed",
          "seen_show",
          "lem_kept"
        ]
      }
    },
    {
      "id": "pellam",
      "bundle": "liberty-of-the-ice/placed.json",
      "entry": "north_road",
      "marker": "ursel",
      "side": "west",
      "beside": [
        "frost",
        "mountain"
      ],
      "name": "Pellam on the Lisk",
      "topic": "the Frost Fair at Pellam",
      "terrain": "hills",
      "rumour": "'West, over the march, where the North Road comes down to the Lisk, there's Pellam, the wool city,' says {keeper}. 'The river's frozen there for the first time in thirty-one winters, they say, bank to bank, and they're holding a Frost Fair on it: booths and a gin-tent and an ox roasting on the ice. And the ice has its own law while it lasts. A lie's no crime on it, and a handshake's the Court's.' {keeper} laughs. 'Half the rogues in the country will be there by now. The other half are on the way.'",
      "heard": "West over the march lies Pellam on the Lisk, a wool city whose river has frozen for the first time in thirty-one winters; they are holding a Frost Fair on the ice, under the ice's own law: a lie is no crime on it, and a handshake is the Court's.",
      "skyline": "a city on a river white with ice from bank to bank",
      "far": "a river has frozen bank to bank under a wool city, and they hold a fair on it where a lie is no crime and a handshake is the law"
    },
    {
      "id": "hessel",
      "bundle": "hessel/placed.json",
      "entry": "south_road",
      "marker": "cherrett",
      "side": "north",
      "beside": [
        "forest",
        "marsh",
        "frost"
      ],
      "name": "the Lim valley",
      "topic": "the Season at Hessel",
      "terrain": "hills",
      "rumour": "'North over the march, down in the Lim valley, there's Hessel,' says {keeper}, 'where the water comes up out of the hill hot, and the old go to be mended and the young to be married. It's the end of their Season. They say there's a rich old woman there who cooked for the navvies, buying husbands for all her family before she dies, and a house in the best street that's kept its shutters closed nine years, with the fires lit, in the warm.'",
      "heard": "North over the march lies Hessel in the Lim valley, a spa where the water comes up hot and the old go to be mended and the young to be married; its Season is ending, a rich old woman there is buying husbands for her family before she dies, and a house in its best street has kept its shutters closed nine years.",
      "skyline": "steam going up out of a green valley, where the water comes up out of the hill hot",
      "far": "the water comes up out of a hill hot, and the old go there to be mended and the young to be married"
    }
  ]
}
data/adventures/gosses-company/city.kyr:
Module pentrice "Gosse's Company" {
  Description "Pentrice, where the Ise falls into the Arle: a cathedral city become a market city become a city of guilds, licences and precedence, in the week of the Trial of the Wheel, when three companies of players play three nights at the Wheel over the river and a bench of four critics gives one of them the Patent.".

  // ── The country ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place vale "the vale of the Arle" is region.
  Place west_road "the West Road" is wilderness within vale at 0, 1.
  Place pentrice "Pentrice" is settlement within vale at 1, 1.
  Place soke "the Soke" is settlement within vale at 1, 2.

  Place road_end "the West Road above Pentrice" is room within west_road at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Observe road_end_scene at road_end when true "The road comes over the last rise and there is the vale of the Arle below you, green and brown, with a city in the bottom of it where two rivers meet: a minster with a squat grey tower, roofs, smoke, the long glint of the Arle, and on the far bank a huddle of low houses round something round and wooden, like a drum laid on its side.".
  Observe road_end_bills at road_end when week() "A board at the roadside has been pasted with bills so many times it has grown a skin: THE TRIAL OF THE WHEEL. THREE COMPANIES. THREE NIGHTS. THE PATENT TO BE GIVEN BY THE BENCH. The newest bill is for Gosse's Company, in red, and someone has written under it, in pencil, AT LAST.".
  Passage west_road_way "the West Road" is road between road_end and westgate taking 1 hour.

  // ── Pentrice, the City ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place westgate "the Westgate" is room within pentrice at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place chepe "the Chepe" is room within pentrice at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place guildhall_square "Guildhall Square" is room within pentrice at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place close "the Minster Close" is room within pentrice at 3, 1 outdoors.
  Place row "Paternoster Row" is room within pentrice at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place hill "Hill Street" is room within pentrice at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place mayor_garden "the Lord Mayor's garden" is room within pentrice at 3, 0 outdoors.
  Place gullet "the Gullet" is room within pentrice at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place water_stairs "the Water Stairs" is room within pentrice at 1, 3 outdoors.

  Passage westgate_street "Westgate Street" is path between westgate and chepe taking 5 minutes.
  Passage cheap_side "Cheap Side" is path between chepe and guildhall_square taking 5 minutes.
  Passage minster_lane "Minster Lane" is path between guildhall_square and close taking 5 minutes.
  Passage row_lane "Bookbinders' Alley" is path between chepe and row taking 5 minutes.
  Passage hill_steps "the Hill Steps" is steps between guildhall_square and hill.
  Passage garden_gate "the Lord Mayor's garden gate" is gate between hill and mayor_garden.
  Passage fish_lane "Fish Lane" is path between chepe and gullet taking 5 minutes.
  Passage stairs_lane "the lane to the Stairs" is path between gullet and water_stairs taking 5 minutes.

  Observe westgate_scene at westgate when true "The Westgate is a squat old gate-tower with a toll-board on it, so thick with the Trial's bills that the tolls are covered and nobody pays any. Carters, a goose-girl, a man selling hot pies out of a box. Under the arch a clerk in grey sits at a folding desk with a ledger and a jar of notched sticks.".
  Observe chepe_scene at chepe when true "The Chepe is the city's market: a long cobbled place with the market cross in the middle, stalls under striped awnings, and every stall with a little painted board on a pole that says what it may sell and who licensed it. A crier with a licence pinned to his hat is crying the Trial: 'The Siege of Arle, by the Lord Mayor's Servants! The Patient Daughter, by the Children of the Close! And Gosse's Company, God help us, from nowhere!'".
  Observe guildhall_scene at guildhall_square when not fountainRuns(pentrice) "Guildhall Square: the Guildhall's long front with its clock, the Office of Plain Speech in the old corn exchange beside it with its doors standing open like a mouth, and in the middle of the square the Fountain of Concord, a great stone basin with four bronze river-gods round a column, every one of them holding an urn, and every urn dry. There is a dead pigeon in the basin.".
  Observe guildhall_scene_wet at guildhall_square when fountainRuns(pentrice) "Guildhall Square, and in the middle of it the Fountain of Concord running: four bronze river-gods pouring the Ise out of their urns into the basin, splashing the cobbles, and children wading in it to the knee, and an alderman in his chain standing at the edge with his mouth open.".
  Observe close_scene at close when true "The Close is green and quiet and very tidy: a lawn nobody walks on, the minster's grey west front, canons' houses with brass knockers, the choir school behind a high wall with broken glass along its top. A sign on the lawn says, in the Office's lettering, SILENCE IS LICENSED HERE.".
  Observe row_scene at row when true "Paternoster Row is booksellers and binders and printers, shoulder to shoulder, with their wares out on trestles under the eaves: almanacs, sermons, ballads, plays in quarto with the licence printed on the title-page. Halfway down hangs a painted owl, and under it a door from which comes the smell of coffee and the sound of people disagreeing.".
  Observe hill_scene at hill when true "Hill Street climbs above the Chepe in tall houses with gardens running down behind them toward the Ise. The houses have railings and the railings have spikes.".
  Observe hill_garden at hill when not fountainRuns(pentrice) "At the top of the street a gate in a high wall stands a little open on a garden with a fountain in it, running.".
  Observe hill_garden_dry at hill when fountainRuns(pentrice) "At the top of the street a gardener is standing in the Lord Mayor's gateway, looking down the hill toward the Chepe, from which comes the sound of water and children.".
  Observe mayor_garden_scene at mayor_garden when not fountainRuns(pentrice) "The Lord Mayor's garden: gravel walks, clipped yews, roses, and in the middle of it all a fountain shaped like a stone shell held up by three fat stone children, running clear and full and splashing over into a pool with carp in it. A gardener is raking the gravel and does not look at you.".
  Observe mayor_garden_dry at mayor_garden when fountainRuns(pentrice) "The Lord Mayor's garden, and the shell fountain dry, its three fat stone children holding up nothing. In the pool the carp are crowded together in a hand's depth of water, gasping. A gardener stands looking at them with his rake.".
  Observe gullet_scene at gullet when true "The Gullet is the fish market, under a long tiled roof on stone posts, and it smells as a fish market smells on a warm day. Fishwives cry pike and eel and Arle salmon in voices that need no licence. At the near end, by a post, a woman keeps a honey stall in a cloud of bees; at the far end the fishmongers' hall has a tall chimney, and a stall papered with ballad-sheets is doing a brisk trade.".
  Observe water_stairs_scene at water_stairs when true "Wide stone stairs go down into the brown Arle, slippery with weed at the bottom. Across the water, low and wooden, the Wheel.".
  Observe water_stairs_oars at water_stairs when not watermenStrike(pentrice) "Watermen sit along the steps in their red caps beside their boats, smoking, shouting 'Oars! Oars! Over to the Soke!' at anyone who looks at them.".
  Observe water_stairs_strike at water_stairs when watermenStrike(pentrice) "A board has been propped against the bottom step: NO BOATS TONIGHT. THE BRIDGE WARDENS KNOW WHY.".

  // ── The Painted Moon, by the Westgate ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place moon "the Painted Moon" is building within pentrice.
  Place moon_upper "the stable loft" is level within moon.
  Place moon_yard "the yard of the Painted Moon" is room within moon at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place moon_taproom "the Painted Moon's taproom" is room within moon at 1, 0.
  Place moon_loft "the loft over the Moon's stables" is room within moon_upper at 0, 0.
  Passage moon_arch "the Moon's archway" is arch between westgate and moon_yard.
  Passage moon_door "the Moon's back door" is door between moon_yard and moon_taproom.
  Passage loft_stair "the loft stair" is stair between moon_yard and moon_loft.
  Observe moon_yard_scene at moon_yard when true "A cobbled coaching-yard with galleries on three sides and the stables along the fourth. A tall wagon painted with a sun and a moon stands in the corner, its shafts down, and the loft over the stables has a door at the top of an outside stair.".
  Observe moon_yard_voices at moon_yard when at(gosse, moon_loft) "From the loft over the stables come voices declaiming, and somebody hammering.".
  Observe moon_yard_bear at moon_yard when at(the_bear, moon_yard) "In a stall at the end of the stables, on clean straw, an old brown bear lies with her chin on her paws, watching the yard with small kind eyes.".
  Observe moon_taproom_scene at moon_taproom when true "A low taproom, black-beamed, with the Moon's own sign hung inside over the fire: a full moon with a woman's face painted on it, winking. On the wall by the door, in a frame, the house's ale-licence with the Office's seal on it, signed in a small upright hand.".
  Observe moon_loft_scene at moon_loft when true "The loft runs the length of the stables, with the floor swept and chalk marks on it for where the stage will be, a wooden throne, a property chest with brass corners, and a long trestle.".
  Observe moon_loft_hampers at moon_loft when not costumesInSoke(pentrice) and not costumesTaken(pentrice) "Along one wall stand the costume hampers, and a rack of swords that bend.".
  Observe moon_loft_hepzibah at moon_loft when at(hepzibah, moon_loft) "At the trestle a grey woman sits with a fat book open in front of her and a pencil behind her ear.".

  Person bascombe "Mistress Bascombe" at moon_taproom {
    Role "who keeps the Painted Moon". Ancestry human. Profession innkeeper. Peaceable. Pronouns she. Manner jovial.
    Greets "Mistress Bascombe is a big woman with her sleeves rolled up and a ring of keys at her belt the size of a horse-collar. 'Players or Trial?' she says. 'Either way it's three coin a night and you don't bring the bear in here.'".
    Sells rations for 2 coin from 10.
  }
  Topic bascombe_trial with bascombe "Ask Mistress Bascombe about the Trial of the Wheel" when true once {
    Says "'Three companies, three nights, over the river at the Wheel,' says Mistress Bascombe, 'and the Bench of four to give one of them the Patent, which is a licensed house and the Office off their backs for ever, near enough. Corin Fallow's had it eleven years, the Lord Mayor's Servants. The Children of the Close every year come second and are very good about it.' She jerks her head at the yard. 'And this year Absalom Gosse, God save us. He was banned from the City's stages, you know. The night of the riot. The Office was made for him.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, riot_rumour). }
  }
  Discovery riot_rumour "Forty years ago there was a riot at the Wheel during a performance by Gosse's Company, and the City banned Absalom Gosse; the Office of Plain Speech was founded after it." { Known by bascombe. }
  Topic bascombe_bear with bascombe "Ask Mistress Bascombe about the bear" when at(the_bear, moon_yard) once {
    Says "'She's no trouble,' says Mistress Bascombe, 'except to the ostlers, the horses, the honey-woman in the Gullet and the Court of Aldermen, who passed a bye-law against her in the year twelve. She's eaten nobody. She's very fond of Jem Pudding, who's no better than he should be.' She looks out of the window at the stall. 'She gets out, mind. She knows the way to the honey.'".
  }
  // A member of Gosse's Company sleeps in the loft for nothing, among the hampers: the players' pallets are kept.
  Rule loft_pallet when inCompany(party) and at(party, moon_loft) and not onTheHouse(hepzibah, party) { Assert onTheHouse(hepzibah, party). }

  // ── The Office of Plain Speech, Guildhall Square ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place office "the Office of Plain Speech" is building within pentrice.
  Place office_hall "the Office's hall" is room within office at 0, 0.
  Place master_room "the Master's room" is room within office at 1, 0.
  Passage office_doors "the Office's doors" is doorway between guildhall_square and office_hall.
  Passage master_door "the Master's door" is door between office_hall and master_room.
  Observe office_hall_scene at office_hall when true "The old corn exchange, high and cold and full of desks. At each desk a clerk in grey reads with a pen in one hand and a ruler in the other, and every so often the ruler comes down and the pen goes through a line with a sound like a small door shutting. Along the walls, shelves of bound licences, and a lectern with a chained book as big as a tombstone: THE ORDINANCES OF PLAIN SPEECH. Over the Master's door at the far end is painted the Office's motto: WHAT IS SAID IS DONE.".
  Observe master_room_scene at master_room when true "A small square room with a window onto the square and the Fountain. Everything in it is very plain and very good: a desk, two chairs, a shelf of plays in quarto, the Office's seal on a silver stand, a jug of ink. On the wall, alone, a portrait of a heavy, cheerful man in an alderman's chain, painted badly and with love.".

  // ── The Close: the minster, the choir school, the canon's house ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place minster "the minster" is building within pentrice.
  Place minster_tower "the minster tower" is level within minster.
  Place nave "the minster nave" is room within minster at 0, 0.
  Place bell_loft "the minster bell-loft" is room within minster_tower at 0, 0.
  Passage west_door "the minster's west door" is doorway between close and nave.
  Passage tower_stair "the tower stair" is stair between nave and bell_loft.
  Observe nave_scene at nave when true "The nave is long and grey and cool, and smells of stone and candles. Down the north aisle the Book of Precedence lies open on a brass eagle, four hundred pages of who walks before whom, with a verger standing over it. From high in the tower comes the sound of two men arguing about bells.".
  Observe bell_loft_scene at bell_loft when true "The ringing chamber, under the bells: a square room with eight ropes coming down through holes in the ceiling, each with a red-and-white woollen grip, and painted boards on the walls recording great peals rung, with the names of the ringers in gold. It is very dusty, and full of jackdaws' noise.".
  Place choir_school "the choir school" is building within pentrice.
  Place school_yard "the choir school yard" is room within choir_school at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Passage school_gate "the choir school gate" is gate between close and school_yard.
  Observe school_yard_scene at school_yard when true "A gravelled yard inside a high wall, with a pump and a lime tree. Small boys in white surplices over muddy stockings are rehearsing a procession round the pump, holding cardboard wings, while a man with a stick beats time.".
  Place canonry "Canon Mallory's house" is building within pentrice.
  Place canon_study "Canon Mallory's study" is room within canonry at 0, 0.
  Passage canon_door "Canon Mallory's door" is door between close and canon_study.
  Observe canon_study_scene at canon_study when true "A comfortable study smelling of tobacco and old paper, with a fire in all weathers, a harpsichord with music open on it, and shelves of sermons, every one of which has been read.".

  // ── Paternoster Row: the Owl and Inchbald's ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place owl "the Owl" is building within pentrice.
  Place owl_room "the Owl's long room" is room within owl at 0, 0.
  Passage owl_door "the Owl's door" is door between row and owl_room.
  Observe owl_room_scene at owl_room when true "The Owl is one long room full of coffee-smoke, newsprint and opinions. Men and a few women sit at long tables with papers, and at the end table, under a window, sit two men who are plainly critics, because nobody sits near them.".
  Place inchbalds "Inchbald's printing-house" is building within pentrice.
  Place press_room "Inchbald's press-room" is room within inchbalds at 0, 0.
  Passage press_door "Inchbald's door" is door between row and press_room.
  Observe press_room_scene at press_room when true "A low room with a great wooden press in the middle of it like a gallows, cases of type on sloping desks, quires of damp paper hung on lines across the ceiling, and the smell of ink and lye. On the imposing-stone a forme of type is locked up ready, and pinned to the wall are title-pages: THE SIEGE OF ARLE, AS IT WAS PLAYED; THE PATIENT DAUGHTER; SERMONS FOR ALL SEASONS.".

  // ── The Hill: the Orde house, and the conduit house ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place orde_house "the Orde house" is building within pentrice.
  Place orde_parlour "the Orde house's parlour" is room within orde_house at 0, 0.
  Place orde_area "the area of the Orde house" is room within orde_house at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Passage area_steps "the area steps" is steps between hill and orde_area.
  Passage orde_door "the Orde house's door" is door between hill and orde_parlour.
  Observe orde_area_scene at orde_area when true "Down the area steps, below the railings, a scrubbed flagged space before the kitchen door, with a pump and a row of geraniums in pots and a bench where a maid could sit out of sight of the street.".
  Observe orde_parlour_scene at orde_parlour when true "A tall cool parlour, very orderly, with a harp nobody plays and a writing-desk somebody does: its pigeonholes stuffed with paper, its blotter black with years of the same small upright hand reversed. On the mantel a child's drawing in a frame, a man in a fool's cap, very old, in brown crayon.".
  Place conduit_house "the conduit house" is building within pentrice.
  Place conduit_room "inside the conduit house" is room within conduit_house at 0, 0.
  Passage conduit_door "the conduit house door" is door between hill and conduit_room.
  Thing conduit_lock "the conduit house lock" on conduit_door {
    State locked blocking "A little round stone house at the top of Hill Street, over the City's water. Its door has a lock the size of a loaf, with the arms of the Guildhall on it.".
    State open "The conduit house door stands open, and from inside comes the sound of running water.".
    Change pick "Pick the conduit house lock" from locked to open needing lockwork.
    Change key "Open the conduit house with Wat Cundy's master's key" from locked to open needing cundy_key.
  }
  Observe conduit_room_scene at conduit_room when true "Inside it is dim and cold and roaring: the City's water comes in under the floor in a stone channel as wide as a man is tall and goes out again by two culverts, one large, one small. Over each culvert hangs an iron sluice on a screw with a wheel to turn it. The large culvert's sluice is down. The small one, painted fresh green, is up.".

  // ── The Mayor's Room, Fallow's house ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place mayors_room "the Mayor's Room" is building within pentrice.
  Place mayors_hall "the Mayor's Room" is room within mayors_room at 0, 0.
  Passage mayors_door "the Mayor's Room's doors" is doorway between chepe and mayors_hall.
  Observe mayors_hall_scene at mayors_hall when true "The City's licensed playhouse: a handsome indoor hall off the Chepe, with candle-branches and a painted ceiling of the virtues, every seat with a number on it, and a stage with a proper proscenium and a curtain of green baize. On every pillar is framed the house's licence, and on the curtain, in gold, BY LEAVE OF THE OFFICE.".

  // ── The Soke, over the Arle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place soke_landing "the Soke landing" is room within soke at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place soke_lane "Soke Lane" is room within soke at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Passage landing_lane "the landing lane" is path between soke_landing and soke_lane taking 5 minutes.
  Observe soke_landing_scene at soke_landing when true "A wooden landing-stage on piles, and beyond it the Soke: low houses leaning on each other, tavern signs, washing, a smell of beer and bears. A painted post at the top of the landing says THE LIBERTY OF THE SOKE: THE CITY'S WRIT RUNS NOT HERE, and someone has hung a garland of dead flowers on it.".
  Observe soke_lane_scene at soke_lane when true "Soke Lane runs along the bank between taverns, cookshops and a building with a red lamp. At its end, round, wooden, enormous, stands the Wheel, with its pennant on a pole above it; and behind a fence of split palings, the bear-garden, from which come the sounds of dogs.".
  Place wheel_house "the Wheel" is building within soke.
  Place wheel_below "the cellarage under the stage" is level within wheel_house.
  Place wheel "the Wheel" is room within wheel_house at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place tiring_house "the Wheel's tiring-house" is room within wheel_house at 1, 0.
  Place under_stage "under the stage" is room within wheel_below at 0, 0.
  Passage wheel_gate "the Wheel's gate" is gate between soke_lane and wheel.
  Passage tiring_door "the tiring-house door" is door between wheel and tiring_house.
  Passage trap_ladder "the ladder under the stage" is ladder between tiring_house and under_stage.
  Observe wheel_scene at wheel when not playingTonight(pentrice) and not (playEnded(pentrice) and tday(pentrice) == 4) "The Wheel is a wooden O, three galleries high, open to the sky in the middle: a beaten-earth yard where the groundlings stand, a stage thrust out into the yard on trestles, with two doors at the back of it and a balcony above, and a painted roof over the stage, the heavens, with stars on it. Below the stage, at the front, is a bench painted grey: the Office's bench, where the tallymen sit in Trial week.".
  Observe tiring_scene at tiring_house when true "Behind the stage: a long room full of hampers, ropes, a ladder going down through a hatch, a rack of old costumes left by companies long gone, and a wall of names scratched into the plaster, players who have played here, hundreds of them, going back two hundred years. Halfway up, very deep, cut by someone with a knife and a great deal of time: A. GOSSE.".
  Observe under_stage_scene at under_stage when true "Under the stage it is dark and close and smells of earth and old beer. Light comes down in stripes through the boards. In the middle a square trap is cut in the stage above, with a counterweighted platform under it, and a stiff lever; beside it a lead tank on a frame, with a pump and a pipe going up through the boards.".
  Person wilmot "Old Wilmot" at tiring_house {
    Role "who keeps the Wheel". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner grim.
    Greets "Old Wilmot is a bent old man with a broom and a ring of keys, who has kept the Wheel for fifty years and has seen, he will tell you, everything, twice.".
    Offers lodging "a bench in the tiring-house and a blanket that smells of other people's plays" for 1 coin.
  }
  Topic wilmot_names with wilmot "Ask Old Wilmot about the names on the tiring-house wall" when true once {
    Says "'Every company that ever played the Wheel,' says Wilmot, 'scratches its names on that wall the night it plays, for luck. Some of them have been here two hundred years.' He puts his thumb on one, very deep, half way up: A. GOSSE. 'Forty years. He did that with a property dagger the night of the riot, with the City banging on the gate, and the Watch coming over the river. Took him an hour. I held the lantern.' He shrugs. 'He said if they were going to put him out of the City, they'd not put him off the wall.'".
  }
  Place bear_garden "the bear-garden" is building within soke.
  Place bear_pen "the bear-garden" is room within bear_garden at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Passage garden_palings "the bear-garden gate" is gate between soke_lane and bear_pen.
  Observe bear_pen_scene at bear_pen when true "A ring of trampled sand inside a fence of palings, with benches round it going up in tiers, and a stake in the middle with a chain. Along one side, pens: dogs, mastiffs, a great many, who hate you on sight. It smells of blood and sawdust.".

  // The river: by boat, while the watermen row; at low water in the evening, by the old weir, for those who know it.
  Passage ferry "the watermen's boats" is ferry between water_stairs and soke_landing taking 10 minutes
    opening when not watermenStrike(pentrice) "The watermen sit on the Stairs with their oars across their knees and their caps on the back of their heads, and do not shout. Their boats are drawn up and chained.".
  Discovery weir_known "Below the Water Stairs there is an old weir across the Arle, and at low water in the evening you can walk it to the Soke on the stones, if you know where they are and keep your feet." { Known by garlick, tolly. }
  // The weir is two walks with the stones in the middle, where the mill-race comes in and something lives under it.
  Place weir_stones "the weir stones" is room within pentrice at 1, 4 outdoors.
  Passage weir_path "the weir's last stones" is path between water_stairs and weir_stones taking 15 minutes hidden until weir_known
    opening when hour(clock) >= 16 or hour(clock) < 2 "The weir is under a yard of brown water, running fast. At low water, from the evening until the small hours, the stones come up.".
  Passage weir_soke "the old weir" is path between weir_stones and soke_lane taking 15 minutes hidden until weir_known
    opening when hour(clock) >= 16 or hour(clock) < 2 "The weir is under a yard of brown water, running fast. At low water, from the evening until the small hours, the stones come up.".
  Observe weir_stones_scene at weir_stones when true "Halfway over, the weir widens into a ledge of old dressed stone, slimed green, where the mill-race of the drowned Bishop's Mill comes in under an arch and the water stands in a black pool before it goes over. The City's lamps are behind you, the Soke's in front, and both look a long way off. The moss is where the footing is. There are bones on the ledge, small ones, fish and fowl, and the end of somebody's fire.".
  Initially Assert cityRoom(weir_stones).

  Relation fountainRuns(place). Relation watermenStrike(place). Relation playingTonight(place).

  Initially Assert cityRoom(westgate). Initially Assert cityRoom(chepe). Initially Assert cityRoom(guildhall_square).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(close). Initially Assert cityRoom(row). Initially Assert cityRoom(hill). Initially Assert cityRoom(mayor_garden).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(gullet). Initially Assert cityRoom(water_stairs). Initially Assert cityRoom(moon_yard).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(moon_taproom). Initially Assert cityRoom(moon_loft). Initially Assert cityRoom(office_hall).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(master_room). Initially Assert cityRoom(nave). Initially Assert cityRoom(bell_loft).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(school_yard). Initially Assert cityRoom(canon_study). Initially Assert cityRoom(owl_room).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(press_room). Initially Assert cityRoom(orde_parlour). Initially Assert cityRoom(orde_area).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(conduit_room). Initially Assert cityRoom(mayors_hall). Initially Assert cityRoom(soke_landing).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(soke_lane). Initially Assert cityRoom(wheel). Initially Assert cityRoom(tiring_house).
  Initially Assert cityRoom(under_stage). Initially Assert cityRoom(bear_pen).
}
data/adventures/gosses-company/road/vill:
Module wending "Wending Cross" {
  // A village on the road to Pentrice, for the campaign played alone: what a generated country's town would be, and
  // where the players on the green (data/goings-on/players) are set. In a generated world the town is the world's own.
  Description "A village where the west road crosses a brook, a day's walk short of the march.".
  Place shire "the brook country" is region.
  Place wending "Wending Cross" is settlement within shire at 0, 0.
  Place cross_green "the green at Wending Cross" is room within wending at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place sheaf "the Wheatsheaf" is building within wending.
  Place sheaf_taproom "the Wheatsheaf's taproom" is room within sheaf at 0, 0.
  Place chapel "the chapel at Wending Cross" is building within wending.
  Place chapel_room "the chapel" is room within chapel at 0, 0.
  Place cobbet_shop "Cobbet's shop" is building within wending.
  Place cobbet_room "Cobbet's shop" is room within cobbet_shop at 0, 0.
  Place west_way "the west road" is wilderness within shire at 0, 1.
  Place road_out "the west road out of Wending Cross" is room within west_way at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Passage sheaf_door "the Wheatsheaf's door" is door between sheaf_taproom and cross_green.
  Passage chapel_door "the chapel door" is doorway between chapel_room and cross_green.
  Passage shop_door "Cobbet's door" is door between cobbet_room and cross_green.
  Passage west_lane "the west lane" is road between cross_green and road_out taking 1 hour.
  Observe green_day at cross_green when not dark() "A triangle of rough grass where the west road crosses a brook by a stone bridge, with a pump, a horse-trough, a chapel with a squat bell-cote, the Wheatsheaf, and Cobbet's shop, which sells everything badly.".
  Observe green_night at cross_green when dark() "The green at Wending Cross in the dark: the brook loud under the bridge, a light in the Wheatsheaf, a dog barking somewhere and then thinking better of it.".
  Observe sheaf_scene at sheaf_taproom when true "A low taproom with a sanded floor, a settle by the fire and a sheaf of last year's wheat nailed up over the door for luck.".
  Observe chapel_scene at chapel_room when true "A whitewashed chapel with six benches and a window of plain glass, very clean.".
  Observe shop_scene at cobbet_room when true "Cobbet's shop: candles, string, pots, nails, a cheese, a coffin standing on end in the corner with a price on it.".
  Observe road_out_scene at road_out when true "The west road out of Wending Cross goes on between hedges toward the march, and beyond it, the folk say, the vale of the Arle.".
  Person thackeray "Mistress Thackeray" at sheaf_taproom {
    Role "who keeps the Wheatsheaf". Ancestry human. Profession innkeeper. Peaceable. Pronouns she. Manner jovial.
    Greets "Mistress Thackeray is a square red-faced woman with flour to the elbows. 'Bed, beer or both?' she says.".
    Sells rations for 2 coin from 6.
  }
  Person ivy "Mother Ivy" at chapel_room {
    Role "who keeps the chapel". Ancestry human. Profession priest. Peaceable. Pronouns she. Manner compassionate.
    Greets "Mother Ivy is very old and very small and sits by the door of her chapel shelling peas into her apron.".
  }
  Person cobbet "Cobbet" at cobbet_room {
    Role "who keeps the shop". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner acerbic.
    Greets "Cobbet looks at you over a cheese as if you had come to steal it.".
    Sells rations for 2 coin from 4.
    Sells torch for 1 coin from 4.
  }
  Topic thackeray_road with thackeray "Ask Mistress Thackeray about the road west" when true once {
    Says "'West,' says Mistress Thackeray, 'over the march, a day, is Pentrice, where the Ise falls into the Arle. A grand minster town, where they license every word said on a stage and fine you a crown a line for the rest.' She jerks her head at the green. 'That lot on the green are going there for their Trial of the Wheel: three companies, three nights, and a house for ever to the best. If they ever get their wagon off my post.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, west_told). }
  }
  Discovery west_told "West over the march, a day's walk, lies Pentrice, where the Trial of the Wheel is played: three companies of players for three nights, and a house to the best.".
  Initially Assert leadsTo(west_told, road_out).
  Company party "You" of 1 at cross_green.
  Initially Set quantity(party, gold) to 14. Initially Set quantity(party, rations) to 2.
}

Module hessel "The Banns at Hessel" {
  Description "Hessel, a spa city on a hillside over the river Lim, in the last four days of its Season: the old come to be mended and the young to be married, and a rich old woman with a navvy's laugh means to see three people settled before she dies.".

  // ── The country ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // One hillside, so that class is height: the Old Town by the river, where the work is done; the Baths in the middle,
  // where the water comes up hot; Upper Hessel, the new stone town built to look at itself; and the downs above it,
  // over which the road goes to Orm. The road from the south comes in at the bottom, over the Lim.
  Place imbar "Imbar" is plane.
  Place hessel "the Lim valley" is region within imbar.
  Initially Assert terrain(hessel, hills).
  Place orm_way "the Orm road" is wilderness within hessel at 0, 0.
  Place downs "the downs above Hessel" is wilderness within hessel at 0, 1.
  Place hessel_town "Hessel" is settlement within hessel at 0, 2.
  Place lim_vale "the Lim vale" is wilderness within hessel at 0, 3.

  // ── Buildings ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Place carth_house "Carth House" is building within hessel_town.
  Place carth_upper "the floor above" is level within carth_house.
  Place carth_below "the rooms below stairs" is level within carth_house.
  Place wenlock_lodging "Lady Wenlock's lodgings" is building within hessel_town.
  Place cherrett_lodging "Mrs Cherrett's lodgings" is building within hessel_town.
  Place assembly "the Assembly Rooms" is building within hessel_town.
  Place twiss_house "Mr Twiss's house" is building within hessel_town.
  Place pump_house "the Pump Room" is building within hessel_town.
  Place ebbas "Saint Ebba's" is building within hessel_town.
  Place hartopp_house "Dr Hartopp's house" is building within hessel_town.
  Place apothecary_house "the apothecary's" is building within hessel_town.
  Place poles_house "the Two Poles" is building within hessel_town.
  Place hospital_house "the Hospital of the Waters" is building within hessel_town.
  Place hetty_house "Hetty Quiney's shop" is building within hessel_town.
  Place no_four_house "Number Four, Quay Lane" is building within hessel_town.
  Place hut_house "the shepherd's hut" is building within orm_way.

  // ── Rooms ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Upper Hessel
  Place carth_drawing "the drawing room at Carth House" is room within carth_upper at 0, 0 indoors.
  Place carth_study "Sir Gervase's study" is room within carth_house at 1, 0 indoors.
  Place wenlock_room "Lady Wenlock's drawing room" is room within wenlock_lodging at 3, 0 indoors.
  Place carth_hall "the hall of Carth House" is room within carth_house at 0, 1 indoors.
  Place crescent "the Crescent" is room within hessel_town at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place parade_top "the top of the Parade" is room within hessel_town at 2, 1 outdoors.

  Place cherrett_bedroom "Mrs Cherrett's bedroom" is room within cherrett_lodging at 5, 1 indoors.
  Place carth_area "the area of Carth House" is room within carth_house at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place carth_kitchen "the kitchen at Carth House" is room within carth_below at 0, 2 indoors.
  Place coal_cellar "the coal cellar under the Crescent" is room within carth_below at 0, 3 underground.
  Place twiss_parlour "Mr Twiss's parlour" is room within twiss_house at 2, 2 indoors.

  // The Baths
  Place ebba_nave "Saint Ebba's" is room within ebbas at 3, 3 indoors.
  Place vestry "the vestry of Saint Ebba's" is room within ebbas at 4, 3 indoors.
  Place abbey_yard "the Abbey Yard, at the foot of the Parade" is room within hessel_town at 3, 4 outdoors.
  Place pump_room "the Pump Room" is room within pump_house at 4, 4 indoors.

  Place beacon "the Beacon walk" is room within downs at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place sham_castle "the Sham Castle" is room within downs at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place stile "the stile on the down" is room within orm_way at 1, 3 outdoors.

  Initially Assert townRoom(carth_hall). Initially Assert townRoom(crescent). Initially Assert townRoom(parade_top).

  // ── Ways ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Passage lim_bridge "Lim Bridge" is bridge between south_road and bridge_foot taking 10 minutes.
  Passage quay_way "Quay Lane" is path between bridge_foot and quay_lane taking 2 minutes.
  Passage stall_way "Stall Street" is path between quay_lane and stall_street taking 5 minutes.
  Passage hetty_door "Hetty Quiney's door" is door between quay_lane and hetty_shop
    opening when hour(clock) >= 8 and hour(clock) < 20 "The milliner's shutters are up, and the bonnets in the window are only shapes.".
  Passage no_four_door "the door of Number Four" is door between quay_lane and no_four
    opening when hour(clock) >= 9 and hour(clock) < 18 and not mopsaHouse(mopsa) or mopsaHouse(mopsa) and hour(clock) >= 7 and hour(clock) < 23 "Number Four is locked, with a card in the window: TO LET, A GOOD LODGING-HOUSE, APPLY MR GILMOUR, DAYTIMES.".
  Passage laundry_way "the laundry lane" is path between quay_lane and laundry_yard taking 5 minutes.
  Passage poles_door "the Two Poles' door" is door between stall_street and two_poles.
  Passage hospital_door "the Hospital door" is door between stall_street and hospital.
  Passage baths_way "Stall Street, up to the Baths" is path between stall_street and abbey_yard taking 5 minutes.
  Passage cross_way "Bath Street" is path between abbey_yard and cross_bath taking 5 minutes.
  Passage wash_way "the steps down to the laundries" is steps between cross_bath and laundry_yard.
  Passage pump_door "the Pump Room door" is door between abbey_yard and pump_room
    opening when hour(clock) >= 7 and hour(clock) < 18 "The Pump Room's doors are shut, and through the glass the great room stands empty, with its chairs on its tables.".
  Passage gallery_arch "the arch to the gallery" is arch between pump_room and kings_bath.
  Passage ebba_door "the west door of Saint Ebba's" is door between abbey_yard and ebba_nave
    opening when hour(clock) >= 7 and hour(clock) < 20 "Saint Ebba's is locked for the night.".
  Passage vestry_door "the vestry door" is door between ebba_nave and vestry.
  Passage walk_way "Doctors' Walk" is path between abbey_yard and doctors_walk taking 3 minutes.
  Passage hartopp_door "Dr Hartopp's door" is door between doctors_walk and hartopp_room
    opening when hour(clock) >= 9 and hour(clock) < 17 "Dr Hartopp's brass plate is polished; his door is shut. CONSULTATIONS NINE TILL FIVE.".
  Passage apothecary_door "the apothecary's door" is door between doctors_walk and apothecary
    opening when hour(clock) >= 8 and hour(clock) < 20 "The apothecary's is shut, its great glass jars dark in the window.".
  Passage parade "the Parade" is path between abbey_yard and parade_top taking 15 minutes.
  Passage circus_way "Gay Street" is path between parade_top and circus taking 5 minutes.
  Passage crescent_way "Brock Street" is path between parade_top and crescent taking 5 minutes.
  Passage cherrett_door "Mrs Cherrett's door" is door between circus and cherrett_parlour
    opening when hour(clock) >= 7 and hour(clock) < 23 or legs(party) "Mrs Cherrett's door is shut for the night, and the knocker is muffled in a stocking.".
  Passage bedroom_door "the bedroom door" is door between cherrett_parlour and cherrett_bedroom
    opening when legs(party) or bedbound(cherrett) "Mrs Cherrett's bedroom door is shut, and her maid sits on a chair in front of it with her knitting, and looks at you over it.".
  Passage twiss_door "Mr Twiss's door" is door between circus and twiss_parlour
    opening when hour(clock) >= 10 and hour(clock) < 18 "Mr Twiss's door bears a card, beautifully lettered: THE MASTER OF THE CEREMONIES RECEIVES BETWEEN TEN AND SIX.".
  Passage rooms_door "the door of the Assembly Rooms" is door between circus and vestibule
    opening when hour(clock) >= 10 and hour(clock) < 24 "The Assembly Rooms are dark, and their great door is shut.".
  Passage ballroom_door "the ballroom doors" is door between vestibule and ballroom
    opening when evening() and admitted(party) or at(party, ballroom) or at(party, card_room) or ballNight() and admitted(party) "The ballroom doors are open, and through them the light and the music; a footman in the Rooms' blue stands across them, and does not move for you.".
  Passage card_door "the card-room door" is door between ballroom and card_room.
  Passage wenlock_door "Lady Wenlock's door" is door between crescent and wenlock_room
    opening when hour(clock) >= 10 and hour(clock) < 18 "Lady Wenlock is not at home. Lady Wenlock is never at home before ten, nor after six.".
  Passage carth_front "the front door of Carth House" is door between crescent and carth_hall.
  Passage area_steps "the area steps" is steps between crescent and carth_area.
  Passage kitchen_door "the kitchen door" is door between carth_area and carth_kitchen.
  Passage coal_hole "the coal-hole" is crawl between carth_area and coal_cellar hidden until coal_hole_known needing lockwork or brawn.
  Passage cellar_door "the cellar door" is door between coal_cellar and carth_kitchen.
  Passage back_stair "the back stair" is stair between carth_kitchen and carth_hall.
  Passage study_door "the study door" is door between carth_hall and carth_study.
  Passage great_stair "the great stair" is stair between carth_hall and carth_drawing.
  // The drawing-room window, over the area railings: a climber's way, and only while it is open.
  Passage carth_window "the drawing-room window" is ladder between crescent and carth_drawing needing climbing
    opening when state(drawing_window, ajar).
  Passage beacon_path "the path up to the Beacon" is path between parade_top and beacon taking 20 minutes.
  Passage castle_path "the walk to the Sham Castle" is path between beacon and sham_castle taking 10 minutes.
  Passage orm_road "the Orm road" is road between beacon and stile taking 1 hour.
  Passage hut_path "the sheep-track to the hut" is path between stile and hut_yard taking 20 minutes.
  Passage hut_door "the hut door" is door between hut_yard and hut.
  Passage down_road "the Orm road over the high down" is road between stile and crossways taking 90 minutes.
  Passage drove_track "the drove track" is track between hut_yard and crossways taking 90 minutes.
  // A shepherd's way across the down, straight where the road goes round: for someone who can read sheep-walks.
  Passage sheep_path "the sheep-path across the down" is path between hut_yard and crossways taking 40 minutes needing woodcraft or wayfinding.
  Passage orm_last "the last of the Orm road" is road between crossways and orm_gate taking 1 hour.

  // ── How the places look ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Observe south_road_scene at south_road when not visitedBefore(south_road) "The south road comes down out of the green country to a river, and on the far side of the river is Hessel, all of it at once, going up its hill: first the Old Town's roofs, wet and close, with steam coming out of them as if the whole place were a kettle; then a great dark church and a long pale pillared building in a haze of more steam; then terraces, honey-coloured, curving round the hill like the rings of a sawn log; and on the top of the hill, against the sky, a castle that is, when you look at it properly, only a wall with holes in it. The air smells of warm iron.".
  Observe south_road_again at south_road when visitedBefore(south_road) "The south road, at Lim Bridge, with Hessel going up its hill on the other side of the water.".
  Observe bridge_foot_scene at bridge_foot when true "The foot of Lim Bridge: fish-baskets, a tar-pot, washing strung between upper windows, and the river going by, brown and quick. A board on the toll-house says WELCOME TO HESSEL, THE QUEEN OF HEALING, and somebody has added in chalk AND OF HEALERS.".
  Observe quay_scene at quay_lane when not dark() and not visitedBefore(quay_lane) "Quay Lane: narrow houses, a milliner's with three bonnets in the window on wooden heads, a lodging-house with a card in its window, and at the end the steam of the laundries rolling across the lane like weather.".
  Observe quay_again at quay_lane when not dark() and visitedBefore(quay_lane) "Quay Lane: the milliner's bonnets, the card in the lodging-house window, the laundries' steam.".
  Observe quay_night at quay_lane when dark() "Quay Lane at night: shutters, a dog, the laundries' steam lit from below.".
  Observe stall_scene at stall_street when not dark() and not strike(chairmen) and not visitedBefore(stall_street) "Stall Street: the chairmen's stand, a long bench under a penthouse roof, and the chairs themselves, black, glossy, like great beetles with their poles laid by them; men in blue coats sitting on the bench with their arms folded, every one of them broad enough to stop the Parade.".
  Observe stall_again at stall_street when not dark() and not strike(chairmen) and visitedBefore(stall_street) "Stall Street: the chairmen's stand, the black chairs, the blue coats on the bench.".
  Observe stall_strike at stall_street when not dark() and strike(chairmen) "Stall Street: the chairmen's stand, and every chair on it with its poles out and laid crossways on the bench, which in Hessel means NO. The chairmen sit behind them with their arms folded.".
  Observe stall_night at stall_street when dark() "Stall Street at night: the chairs chained to their bench, and the lamp of the Two Poles.".
  Observe poles_scene at two_poles when not visitedBefore(two_poles) "The Two Poles: a low room, a fire, a long table polished by blue sleeves, and over the chimney a pair of crossed chair-poles with a laurel wreath, very dusty, won by somebody in a race in the year of a comet.".
  Observe poles_again at two_poles when visitedBefore(two_poles) "The Two Poles: the fire, the long table, the crossed poles over the chimney.".
  Observe hospital_scene at hospital when not visitedBefore(hospital) "The Hospital of the Waters: a long whitewashed ward, twenty beds, twenty patients, a smell of vinegar and the river. The poor of three counties come to Hessel for the waters, the same as the rich, and here is where they lie. A bench by the door has a doctor's bag on it, packed.".
  Observe hospital_again at hospital when visitedBefore(hospital) "The Hospital of the Waters: the long ward, the twenty beds, the vinegar.".
  Observe laundry_scene at laundry_yard when not dark() and not visitedBefore(laundry_yard) "The laundry yard: coppers, mangles, steam, a dozen women with their sleeves up and arms red to the elbow, and lines and lines of white linen, the Season's sheets and bathing-gowns, rising and falling in the warm wind off the coppers like a fleet.".
  Observe laundry_again at laundry_yard when not dark() and visitedBefore(laundry_yard) "The laundry yard: coppers, steam, red arms, and the Season's linen on the lines.".
  Observe laundry_night at laundry_yard when dark() and not at(nan, laundry_yard) "The laundry yard at night: the coppers banked, the linen taken in, and in one window over the yard a candle.".
  Observe laundry_night_nan at laundry_yard when dark() and at(nan, laundry_yard) "The laundry yard at night: the coppers banked, the linen taken in, and on the step under the stair, in the light of one candle in the window over the yard, a woman sitting with her red hands folded, awake.".
  Observe cross_scene at cross_bath when true "The Cross Bath: the old one, open to the sky, a stone cross in the middle of a square of hot green water. The poor bathe here free, in their shifts, and the laundresses come up from below to fill their buckets. It is noisier and much happier than the King's Bath.".
  Observe abbey_scene at abbey_yard when not dark() and not visitedBefore(abbey_yard) "The Abbey Yard, at the foot of the Parade: on one side the great dark front of Saint Ebba's, carved all over with angels climbing ladders; on another the colonnade of the Pump Room; and between them the Parade going up the hill so steeply that the paving is cut into ridges for the chairmen's feet. Everyone here is either ill, or with someone who is, or selling something to both.".
  Observe abbey_again at abbey_yard when not dark() and visitedBefore(abbey_yard) "The Abbey Yard: the church, the Pump Room, the Parade going up the hill, and everybody looking at everybody.".
  Observe abbey_night at abbey_yard when dark() "The Abbey Yard at night, lit by the Pump Room's lamps; the angels on the church front climbing their ladders into the dark.".
  Observe pump_scene at pump_room when not visitedBefore(pump_room) "The Pump Room: a long cool room of pale stone, with tall windows, a gallery for musicians, and at one end a marble urn from which a man in a waistcoat dispenses the hot waters of Hessel by the glass, threepence. Over the urn, in gold letters, WATER IS BEST. Everyone in Hessel comes here at eight in the morning to drink a glass, and grimace, and look at everybody else, and write their names in the great book by the door.".
  Observe pump_again at pump_room when visitedBefore(pump_room) "The Pump Room: the urn, the gold letters, the book by the door, the glasses.".
  Observe bath_scene at kings_bath when true "From the gallery you look down into the King's Bath: a great steaming square of brown water, and standing in it up to their necks, in canvas gowns and canvas hats, thirty of the best people in three counties, bobbing slightly, with little floating trays in front of them for their handkerchiefs and their snuff. Along the gallery rail the rest of the best people watch them, and comment.".
  Observe ebba_scene at ebba_nave when true "Saint Ebba's: a high pale nave full of memorial tablets, put up by the Season to its dead. SACRED TO THE MEMORY of a colonel, a widow, a child, a bishop, all of whom came to Hessel for the waters and are in Hessel still. One tablet only says, HE CAME TOO LATE.".
  Observe vestry_scene at vestry when true "The vestry: surplices on pegs, a table, an inkstand, and the register of banns, which is a thin book, as most people in Hessel marry elsewhere.".
  Observe walk_scene at doctors_walk when not visitedBefore(doctors_walk) "Doctors' Walk: eleven brass plates on eleven doors, eleven physicians to the Season, each of whom will prescribe you the waters, in a different quantity, at a different hour, at a different price.".
  Observe walk_again at doctors_walk when visitedBefore(doctors_walk) "Doctors' Walk: eleven brass plates.".
  Observe hartopp_scene at hartopp_room when true "Dr Hartopp's consulting room: Turkey carpet, a bust of somebody wise, books with uncut pages, and a large chair for the patient that tips back so that the patient is lying down before they know it.".
  Observe apothecary_scene at apothecary when not visitedBefore(apothecary) "The apothecary's: rows of blue and white jars, a pestle as big as a child, scales, and on the counter a row of little brown bottles with handwritten labels waiting to be sent up the hill.".
  Observe apothecary_again at apothecary when visitedBefore(apothecary) "The apothecary's: the jars, the scales, the little brown bottles waiting to go up the hill.".
  Observe parade_scene at parade_top when not dark() and not visitedBefore(parade_top) "The top of the Parade, where the hill levels: you can see the whole of Hessel below you from here, the Baths smoking and the Old Town smoking and the river. Two terraces go off from here, the Crescent to the left and the Circus to the right, and a path goes on up to the downs and the Beacon.".
  Observe parade_again at parade_top when not dark() and visitedBefore(parade_top) "The top of the Parade: the Crescent one way, the Circus the other, the Beacon path going up.".
  Observe parade_night at parade_top when dark() "The top of the Parade at night: the whole town below you in lamps, going down to the black river.".
  Observe circus_scene at circus when not dark() and not visitedBefore(circus) "The Circus: a ring of tall houses round a round lawn, every one alike, columns on columns, so that wherever you stand you are looking at the same house. On one side, the Assembly Rooms; on another, a door with a brass plate, MR S. TWISS, M.C.; on another, the lodgings Mrs Cherrett has taken for the Season.".
  Observe circus_again at circus when not dark() and visitedBefore(circus) "The Circus: the ring of houses, the round lawn, the Rooms on one side and Mrs Cherrett's door on another.".
  Observe circus_night at circus when dark() "The Circus at night: the ring of houses with lamps at every door, and the Rooms lit like a ship.".
  Observe crescent_scene at crescent when not dark() and not visitedBefore(crescent) "The Crescent: thirty houses in one sweep of honey-coloured stone, built all of a piece to be looked at from the lawn below, and full of lodgers looking at one another. At the far end the last house is different. Every shutter of every window of it is closed, and smoke is coming out of all its chimneys, in the warm afternoon.".
  Observe crescent_again at crescent when not dark() and visitedBefore(crescent) "The Crescent: the pale sweep of houses, the lawn, the lodgers, and at the far end, shuttered and smoking, Carth House.".
  Observe crescent_night at crescent when dark() "The Crescent at night: lit windows the whole length of it, and then, at the end, nothing; only Carth House's chimneys against the stars, smoking.".
  Observe beacon_scene at beacon when true "The Beacon walk: turf, sheep, wind, and the whole valley below. This is where Hessel comes to walk in pairs at noon, slowly, to be seen walking in pairs. A road goes off north-west across the down, to Orm.".
  Observe castle_scene at sham_castle when true "The Sham Castle: a castle front, two towers and a gateway and battlements, all very fine from the Crescent, and from up here a single wall one stone thick, propped from behind with timbers, with sheep lying in its shade. Lovers carve their names in the back of it, where nobody in the Crescent can see.".
  Observe wenlock_scene at wenlock_room when true "Lady Wenlock's drawing room: the best lodgings in the Crescent, and too many chairs in them, all of them hard.".
  Observe twiss_scene at twiss_parlour when not visitedBefore(twiss_parlour) "Mr Twiss's parlour: a portrait of Mr Twiss, younger, dancing; a portrait of Mr Twiss, older, not; a framed copy of the Rules of the Rooms; and a great many letters, each tied with ribbon of a colour that means something to Mr Twiss.".
  Observe twiss_again at twiss_parlour when visitedBefore(twiss_parlour) "Mr Twiss's parlour: the two portraits, the Rules, the beribboned letters.".
  Observe vestibule_scene at vestibule when true "The vestibule of the Assembly Rooms: marble, mirrors, a footman, and by the ballroom doors, framed in gold, THE RULES OF THE ROOMS. No boots after six. No lady to dance two dances running with one gentleman, unless betrothed. No introductions but by the Master. No dancing after eleven, though the King himself should ask it. No companion, governess or paid attendant to stand up in the dances. Signed, Septimus Twiss, M.C.".
  Observe ballroom_scene at ballroom when not evening() and not ballNight() "The ballroom, empty: five chandeliers in holland bags, a floor chalked for dancing, the musicians' gallery with its chairs on end.".
  Observe card_scene at card_room when true "The card room: green tables, the old at whist, and the talk under the play, which is all of who is dancing with whom.".
  Observe hut_yard_scene at hut_yard when true "A hurdle fold on the open down, a dog asleep in it with one eye open, and a shepherd's hut on iron wheels with smoke coming out of its pipe. Beyond it the drove track goes off over the turf, and a fainter line, a sheep-walk, goes straight across the down toward the crossways.".
  Observe stile_scene at stile when true "A stile in a hedge on the high down, where the Orm road climbs out of the valley. Hessel is gone behind the brow; there is only grass and sky and larks, and the road going on. A sheep-track goes off sideways to a hut.".
  Observe hut_scene at hut when true "A shepherd's hut: one room, a fire, a bed, a dog under it, a woman at the fire, and in the bed a little girl, flushed, with her eyes open and too bright.".
  Observe crossways_scene at crossways when true "The crossways on the high down, where the Orm road meets the drove road. A gibbet stands at the crossing, empty, its chain creaking. Somebody has hung a garland on it.".
  Observe orm_scene at orm_gate when true "The south gate of Orm: a grey wall, a grey gate, a grey town behind it with a grey tower, and over the gate, in letters the College of Physicians paid for, MEDICUS CURAT, NATURA SANAT.".

  // ── The weather of the Season ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // No month is named. It is warm, as Hessel always is in the Season, because the hill is hot from inside.
  Observe steam_dusk at abbey_yard when hour(clock) >= 18 and hour(clock) < 21 "In the evening the steam stands up off the Baths in a pillar, gold, and the bells of Saint Ebba's ring for nothing in particular.".
}

  Milestone m_kit_kept "kept Kit Danby on the poles" worth 50 when kitDefended(kit).

  Milestone m_rooms "got Mrs Cherrett back into the Rooms" worth 150 when householdAdmitted(cherrett).
  Milestone m_brocca "got Signor Brocca up the hill in time" worth 150 when broccaDone(brocca) and twissOwes(party) or broccaDone(brocca) and twissFavour(twiss) >= 2 and broccaSober(brocca).

  Milestone m_stood "stood with the chairmen" worth 100 when stoodWith(party).

  Milestone m_rupert "found out Rupert Wenlock's secret" worth 100 when knows(party, rupert_married).
  Milestone m_family "put Jack in Lady Wenlock's arms" worth 250 when grandmother(lady_wenlock).
  Milestone m_banns "stopped the banns" worth 150 when bannsStopped(ebbas).
  Milestone m_kit_ismay "brought Ismay and Kit to the Sham Castle" worth 200 when kitEngaged(kit).
  Milestone m_blessing "got Mrs Cherrett's blessing on a chairman" worth 200 when cherrettBlessesKit(cherrett).
  Milestone m_poem "made a poem of what was seen" worth 150 when poemGood(rob) and celiaHasPoem(celia).
  Milestone m_knocker "found out who knocks at Carth House" worth 150 when knows(party, nan_is_lady).
  Milestone m_gervase "sat up with Sir Gervase" worth 150 when gervaseTold(gervase).
  Milestone m_celia_out "brought Celia Carth out into the Season" worth 200 when celiaOut(celia).
  Milestone m_mother "brought Celia to her mother" worth 200 when celiaMetMother(celia).
  Milestone m_door "saw the door of Carth House opened" worth 400 when carthReunited(carth).
  Milestone m_ottery "walked Dr Ottery to Orm" worth 150 when ottTurned(party).
  Milestone m_child "stayed while Ottery saw to the shepherd's child" worth 100 when childTreated(party).
  Milestone m_witness "stood witness for Dr Ottery" worth 150 when otteryLicensed(ottery).
  Milestone m_lease "got Mopsa Gedge her house" worth 200 when mopsaHouse(mopsa).
