Isaura Vant has entered it in the tally as Held, which is not a figure; she has had to rule a new column for it.".
  Ending seventh "The Seventh Remainder" when departed(party) and (verdictSeventh(ammerlin) or restoredForGood(bowl)) and not complete(reckoner) and not broken(reckoner) "Every night at eight the bells stop, and in the quiet a thousand people sing four low notes, alike, alike, alike, alike, and at the bottom of the Bowl the Deep Gate lies down in its bed. The Mere stops falling at {mere(bowl)} spans and begins, very slowly, to come back. Down under it the Reckoner counts a cupful a night, as it did for three thousand years, toward an answer that will be heard, if it is ever heard, by people who will not know your name or the Cantor's or the keeper's. Piet Harl has started a new lock-book. On the first page, in capitals that would have cost him his ears in Abel Tarrant's day: DOWN AT THE SEVENTH. CUPFUL.".
  Ending guild "The Registrar's Finding" when departed(party) and verdictGuild(ammerlin) and not complete(reckoner) "The Fulling Channel is closed and the Ninefold goes down the Stair entire, and the mills on the Rim are dark, and four hundred people are looking for work in a Bowl that has none for them. The Ward drank to the Office for a week. Then the Mere went on falling, more slowly, a span every few days, because the Deep Gate at the Ninth Lock stays up at the Sixth and nobody sings it down. By midwinter the Council will know the Finding was wrong. It stands at {mere(bowl)} spans the day you leave. Somebody else will have to find out why. Isaura Vant will be there when they do, with her tally, and this time she will not wait to be asked.".
  Ending left "The Assessor Who Left" when departed(party) and not hearingDone(ammerlin) "You go up out of the Bowl before the Hearing, and the road takes you north, and Ammerlin goes on without you. The Registrar gives the Office's own finding; the Mere goes on doing whatever it was going to do. Somewhere in the Office a Clerk-Measurer, Third Grade, closes a thin book on a figure she cannot put anywhere, and goes on keeping it.".
  Ending low_whole "Low Water" when departed(party) and complete(reckoner) "The count closed on its own, in the night, with every bell in Ammerlin ringing and nobody at the ropes and nobody in the city who knew what they were hearing. The Mere went down six spans in one breath and stopped. It stands at {mere(bowl)} spans on the Ward gauge, a pond at the bottom of a Bowl of mud, and the Ward is gone up the terraces. Under it the round door stands open on still water. In the Office, a Clerk-Measurer, Third Grade, has written a line in her tally under the forty ells that she could never put anywhere: Ceased. She has not written why. Nobody has asked her. Six days after you have gone, a letter comes after you on the north road, in a hand you know, very small and very even: The Mere went through the bottom of the Bowl last night. Not falling. Going. The Ward is going after it a step a night. Received, it said, in every room. Received. I am measuring it. It has no number. I. V.".
  Ending low "Low Water" when departed(party) "You go up the Stair with the Mere at {mere(bowl)} spans and still going down, a hand a day, past the last painted step and the last boat-ring and the last of the Ward. The city has a Finding and a verdict and a great many opinions, and under the Ward the Reckoner drinks on, counting, toward whatever end it was built to reach. From the Rim, looking back, the Mere is a coin somebody dropped, and the ring of mud round it is wider than the coin.".
}
data/adventures/low-water/merebed.kyr:
Module lowwater "Low Water" {
  Description "The bed of the Mere: the new mud, the Ward's dig, and the Listening Hall the water has given back, an Aenean temple in the shape of an ear, built over a throat that goes down.".

  Place mudflats "the new mud" is room within merebed at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place dig "the dig" is room within merebed at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place hall_site "the Listening Hall" is site within merebed at 1, 1.
  Place hall_floor_level "the spiral" is level within hall_site.
  Place throat_level "the throat" is level within hall_site.
  Place listening_hall "the Listening Hall" is room within hall_floor_level at 0, 0.
  Place hall_throat "the throat of the Listening Hall" is room within throat_level at 0, 0 underground.
  Place mere_edge "the edge of the Mere" is room within merebed at 0, 1 outdoors.

  Passage plank_way "the planks over the mud" is path between ward_landing and mudflats taking 15 minutes.
  Passage dig_planks "the planks to the dig" is path between mudflats and dig taking 5 minutes.
  Passage hall_mouth "the Listening Hall's mouth" is doorway between dig and listening_hall.
  Passage throat_stair "the stair down the throat" is stair between listening_hall and hall_throat taking 5 minutes
    opening when mere(bowl) <= 34 "A stair goes down from the floor of the Listening Hall into black water. The Mere stands in the throat of the Hall and hides where it goes.".
  Passage edge_way "the mud toward the water" is path between mudflats and mere_edge taking 20 minutes.

  Observe mud_scene at mudflats when not familiar(mudflats) "Grey mud to the horizon of the Bowl's floor, cracked into plates where it has dried and soft as dough where it has not. Planks go out across it, and things stand up out of it: the stumps of posts, the ribs of a boat, the top of a wall. The smell is of old water.".
  Observe mud_scene_again at mudflats when familiar(mudflats) "The new mud, and the planks laid over it.".
  Observe mud_cracks at mudflats when mere(bowl) <= 30 "The mud is drying faster than the planks can be moved. Cracks run across it a hand deep, and in the cracks, grey stone.".
  Observe edge_scene at mere_edge when not wardEmpty(ammerlin) "The Mere: still, dark, very clear, with the whole Bowl upside down in it, terraces and Sounding and the Rim. It is cold enough to ache. The water's edge is a line of drying weed, and a hand further out than it was this morning.".
  Observe edge_pond at mere_edge when wardEmpty(ammerlin) "What is left of the Mere is a pond you could throw a stone across. In the middle of it, the water is turning, very slowly, round and round, like water above a drain.".

  // The dig.
  Observe dig_scene at dig when not digClosed(dig) "A pit in the mud the size of a house, shored with old oars and boat-planks, down to a pavement of grey stone and a carved doorway half out of the silt. Baskets go up and down on ropes. Things the diggers have found lie sorted on a tarpaulin: green bronze, carved stone, a few squared weights with holes through them.".
  Observe dig_closed at dig when digClosed(dig) "The dig is roped off with Guild rope and a Guild sign. Nobody is working. The tarpaulin of finds is gone.".
  Observe dig_dam at dig when cofferdam(dig) and not breached(dig) "Round the mouth of the Hall's throat the diggers have raised a dam of boat-planks, sandbags and puddled mud, chest-high and still wet.".
  Item dig_weight "a weight-stone" is weight_stone at dig.
  Item dig_weight_b "a weight-stone" is weight_stone at dig.

  // The Listening Hall: an Aenean temple in the shape of an ear, over the engine's listening shaft.
  Observe hall_scene_mere at listening_hall when not familiar(listening_hall) "Inside, the Listening Hall is a spiral: a great curving room of grey and white stone that winds inward and down, narrowing, like the inside of a shell, or of an ear. Every surface is fluted. When you speak your voice goes round the curve and comes back to you from in front.".
  Observe hall_scene_mere_again at listening_hall when familiar(listening_hall) "The Listening Hall, winding inward and down, giving your voice back to you from in front.".
  Observe hall_low at listening_hall when mere(bowl) <= 24 "The Hall stands in the air entire now, and the light comes in at its mouth and goes round its curve and lights it all, white and grey, as nobody has seen it in a thousand years.".
  Discovery hall_hums "Under the Listening Hall, deep in the rock, something is running: a single note, held, under water.".
  Thing hall_wall "the inner wall of the spiral" at listening_hall {
    State fluted "The innermost wall of the spiral is fluted like the rest, and cold, and faintly wet.".
    Tries listening.
  }
  Rule hall_listened when tried(hall_wall, listening) and not knows(party, hall_hums)
    says "You put your ear to the stone. At first, nothing; then, under the nothing, a sound so low it is almost not one: a single note, held, under water, and slowly, very slowly, a click, like a bead pushed along a wire, and the note again." teaches hall_hums { }

  // The keystone, at the centre of the spiral: four voices, and what each names.
  Discovery keystone_seen "The keystone at the heart of the Listening Hall sets a sign beside each of the four voices: a mouth, tally-sticks, a door, a singing face; and under them, the four mouths of the Dyers' arch.".
  Rule keystone_scene at listening_hall when at(party, listening_hall) and not knows(party, keystone_seen) says "At the narrow heart of the spiral, where it ends in a round hole going down, a keystone is set in the wall at the height of a face. It is carved in four rows. Beside the lowest note-mark, a mouth. Beside the next, a bundle of tally-sticks tied together. Beside the third, a door. Beside the highest, a face with its mouth open, singing. Under the four rows, a line of four mouths from shut to wide, the same as on the arch in the Dyers' Basin, and a line of letters, Aenean, and under those, smaller and older, marks that are not letters at all." teaches keystone_seen { }
  Discovery keystone_read "The letters under the keystone, read: THE FIRST VOICE NAMES; THE VOICE AFTER SAYS HOW MUCH. And the oldest marks under them: THE HIGH VOICE IS NOT SUNG BRIGHT. THAT IS THE END OF THE SONG." {
    Found by searching listening_hall with lore "With the old script in your head, the letters under the keystone come clear: THE FIRST VOICE NAMES; THE VOICE AFTER SAYS HOW MUCH. And smaller, in the oldest marks: THE HIGH VOICE IS NOT SUNG BRIGHT. THAT IS THE END OF THE SONG.".
  }
  // Put together: the arch, the keystone, its letters and the hymnal make the engine's speech plain.
  Discovery grammar_known "The Remainders of the Long Hymn are the Reckoner's own speech. Its first voice names an organ (deep the mouth, middle the count, high the last door, bright its own voice), and its second says how much (deep least, bright all). The Seventh, deep and deep, is the mouth at its least: a cupful. The Sixth, deep and bright, is the mouth wide.".
  Rule grammar_put_together when knows(party, keystone_seen) and knows(party, keystone_read) and knows(party, remainders_tones) and not knows(party, grammar_known)
    says "It goes together all at once, the way a sum comes out: the keystone's four voices, the arch's four mouths, the Remainders in the Cantor's hymnal. The first note names; the second says how much. Deep and deep is the mouth, least. That is the Seventh Remainder. That is the cupful." teaches grammar_known { }

  // The throat, going down.
  Observe throat_scene at hall_throat when not breached(dig) "The throat of the Hall goes down in a stair round a shaft, until the stair stops at a wall of the fine grey stone with no door in it, across which the diggers have cut a ragged hole a hand deep. The floor is mud and standing water. The note you heard through the wall is louder here, so low it is in your teeth rather than your ears.".
  Observe throat_breached at hall_throat when breached(dig) "At the bottom of the throat the grey wall is broken through. Beyond the hole, dark, and a draught of cold dry air coming up out of it, and the note.".
  Passage breach_hole "the hole in the grey wall" is crawl between hall_throat and breach_gallery
    opening when breached(dig) "At the bottom of the throat a wall of fine grey stone closes the way. The diggers' hole in it is a hand deep and the stone is hard as glass.".
  // Breaking through by the company's own hands, where the diggers have not.
  Action break_wall(actor: group, site: place) "Break through the grey wall at the bottom of the throat" {
    Description "Days of work for the diggers; an hour's, with the right tools and the hole they began.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hall_throat) and not breached(dig) and capable(actor, digging) and not digClosed(dig).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert breached(dig). Assert breachedBy(dig, actor). }
    Result "You work at the diggers' hole for an hour with pick and bar, and the grey stone, which nothing could scratch, gives all at once along some old seam, and a slab of it falls inward into the dark.".
  }
  Relation breachedBy(entity, group).
  Rule self_breach_floods when breachedBy(dig, party) and not cofferdam(dig) and mere(bowl) > 26 and not drownedSelf(dig)
    says "The silt behind you goes with a sound like a sigh, and the Mere comes down the throat after it. It comes round the stair in a black rope and takes you off your feet and through the hole you made, and drops you, in the dark, on stone." {
    Assert drownedSelf(dig). Assert strikes(culvert_flood, party). Assert at(party, breach_gallery). Decrease mere(bowl) by 1. }
  Relation drownedSelf(entity).
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/cala:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "Calamy, a tidal city of paper at the mouth of the Calam: its wards and streets, its houses and trades, its tide and its days.".

  // The Calam mouth: the walled city on the north bank (Stitchgate, the Close, Gannet Hill), the new town of the
  // presses outside the wall, the Gardens, the Penny Bridge, the Hithe on the south bank, and the reed-beds downriver.
  Place calam "the Calam mouth" is region.
  Initially Assert terrain(calam, marsh).
  Place gannet "Gannet Hill" is settlement within calam at 0, 0.
  Place gardens "the Gardens" is settlement within calam at 2, 0.
  Place stitchgate "Stitchgate" is settlement within calam at 0, 1.
  Place close "the Close" is settlement within calam at 1, 1.
  Place presses "Newmarket" is settlement within calam at 2, 1.
  Place pennybridge "the Penny Bridge" is settlement within calam at 1, 2.
  Place hithe "the Hithe" is settlement within calam at 1, 3.
  Place calamies "the Calamies" is wilderness within calam at 3, 3.
  Initially Assert landform(calamies, land_lake).
  Initially Assert townSize(hithe, size_town). Initially Assert townSize(stitchgate, size_town). Initially Assert townSize(close, size_town).

  // ── The Hithe: the south bank, the river port. ──
  Place causey "the causeway over the saltings" is room within hithe at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place quay "the Hithe quay" is room within hithe at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place rag_market "the rag market" is room within hithe at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place millrace "the millrace walk" is room within hithe at 3, 0 outdoors.
  Place customs_yard "the Customs yard" is room within hithe at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place ferry_stairs "the ferry stairs" is room within hithe at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place pudding_lane "Pudding Lane" is room within hithe at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place mudbank "the mudbank under the mills" is room within hithe at 3, 1 outdoors.
  Place lamb "the Lamb and Lantern" is building within hithe seen as "a tavern under a painted lantern" until lamb_known.
  Discovery lamb_known "The tavern under the painted lantern on the Hithe quay is the Lamb and Lantern, Moll Garrow's.".
  Place taproom "the Lamb's taproom" is room within lamb at 1, 2.
  Place lamb_upper "the Lamb's upper floor" is level within lamb.
  Place lamb_loft "the Lamb's loft" is room within lamb_upper at 1, 3.
  Observe taproom_named at taproom when true "Over the bar a board says THE LAMB AND LANTERN, M. GARROW, and under it in smaller letters NO BOOKS READ ALOUD AFTER TEN." teaches lamb_known.
  Place old_mill "the old mill" is building within hithe.
  Place brannock_floor "Brannock's mill floor" is room within old_mill at 3, 2.
  Place new_mill "the new mill" is building within hithe.
  Place teague_floor "the Widow Teague's mill floor" is room within new_mill at 4, 0.
  Place bond "the bonded warehouse" is building within hithe.
  Place bond_floor "the bond floor" is room within bond at 0, 2.
  Place bond_upper "the bond's upper floor" is level within bond.
  Place bond_loft "the upper bond" is room within bond_upper at 0, 3.
  Place garrets "the garret house" is building within hithe.
  Place garret_top "the top of the garret house" is level within garrets.
  Place jonquil_garret "a garret under the leads" is room within garret_top at 2, 2.
  Place nance_house "the midwife's house" is building within hithe seen as "a house with a green door and a horseshoe" until nance_named.
  Discovery nance_named "The house with the green door in Pudding Lane is Goody Nance's, the midwife of the Hithe.".
  Place nance_room "Goody Nance's front room" is room within nance_house at 2, 3.
  Place coddy_hut "Coddy Fitch's hut" is room within hithe at 4, 1 outdoors.

  Passage causey_quay "the causeway into the Hithe" is road between causey and quay taking 5 minutes.
  Passage quay_rags "the way along the quay" is road between quay and rag_market taking 3 minutes.
  Passage rags_race "the walk up to the mills" is path between rag_market and millrace taking 3 minutes.
  Passage quay_customs "the lane to the Customs" is road between quay and customs_yard taking 2 minutes.
  Passage quay_ferry "the steps down to the ferry" is steps between quay and ferry_stairs.
  Passage rags_pudding "the alley into Pudding Lane" is path between rag_market and pudding_lane taking 2 minutes.
  Passage race_mud "the slipway down to the mud" is path between millrace and mudbank taking 2 minutes.
  Passage mud_hut "the plank walk to the hut" is path between mudbank and coddy_hut taking 3 minutes.
  Passage lamb_door "the door under the lantern" is door between quay and taproom.
  Passage lamb_stair "the Lamb's back stair" is stair between taproom and lamb_loft.
  Passage brannock_door "the old mill's door" is door between millrace and brannock_floor.
  Passage teague_door "the new mill's door" is door between millrace and teague_floor.
  Passage bond_gate "the bond gate" is gate between customs_yard and bond_floor.
  Passage bond_stair "the bond stair" is stair between bond_floor and bond_loft.
  Passage garret_stair "the garret stair" is stair between pudding_lane and jonquil_garret taking 3 minutes.
  Passage nance_door "the green door" is door between pudding_lane and nance_room.

  // ── The Penny Bridge: nineteen arches, and on every pier a stall. ──
  Place bridge_south "the south end of the Penny Bridge" is room within pennybridge at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place bridge_middle "the chapel pier" is room within pennybridge at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place bridge_north "the north end of the Penny Bridge" is room within pennybridge at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Passage hithe_bridge "the bridge foot" is road between quay and bridge_south taking 3 minutes.
  Passage bridge_span_south "the southern arches" is bridge between bridge_south and bridge_middle taking 4 minutes.
  Passage bridge_span_north "the northern arches" is bridge between bridge_middle and bridge_north taking 4 minutes.

  // ── Stitchgate: the old craft quarter inside the wall. ──
  Place old_gate "the Stitch Gate" is room within stitchgate at 1, 3 outdoors.
  Place needle_street "Needle Street" is room within stitchgate at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place ink_lane "Inkhorn Lane" is room within stitchgate at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place scriveners "Copyists' Row" is room within stitchgate at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place gutter_lane "Gutter Lane" is room within stitchgate at 2, 3 outdoors.
  Place lantern_yard "Lantern Yard" is room within stitchgate at 3, 3 outdoors.
  Place binders_hall "the Binders' Hall" is building within stitchgate seen as "a hall with an iron needle over the door" until binders_named.
  Discovery binders_named "The hall with the great iron needle over its door is the Binders' Hall, of the Worshipful Company of Binders.".
  Place hall_floor "the Binders' great room" is room within binders_hall at 2, 2.
  Place sewing_room "the sewing room" is room within binders_hall at 2, 1.
  Place gallon_house "the ink shop" is building within stitchgate.
  Place gallon_shop "Gallon's ink shop" is room within gallon_house at 0, 1.
  Place gallon_upper "the ink shop's attic floor" is level within gallon_house.
  Place gallon_attic "the attic over the ink shop" is room within gallon_upper at 0, 0.
  Place dame_house "the house with the shut school" is building within stitchgate.
  Place dame_school "the empty schoolroom" is room within dame_house at 0, 3.
  Place crakes "the Two Hands" is building within stitchgate.
  Place crake_front "the front of Crake's shop" is room within crakes at 3, 2.
  Place crake_stacks "the back stacks" is room within crakes at 3, 1.
  Place crake_parlour "Crake's parlour" is room within crakes at 4, 2.

  Passage bridge_gate "the river stair to the Stitch Gate" is steps between bridge_north and old_gate taking 4 minutes.
  Passage gate_needle "the way under the gate" is road between old_gate and needle_street taking 2 minutes.
  Passage needle_ink "the turning into Inkhorn Lane" is road between needle_street and ink_lane taking 2 minutes.
  Passage needle_scriveners "the way up to Copyists' Row" is road between needle_street and scriveners taking 2 minutes.
  Passage gate_gutter "the gap beside the gate" is path between old_gate and gutter_lane taking 2 minutes.
  Passage gutter_yard "the crooked end of Gutter Lane" is path between gutter_lane and lantern_yard taking 2 minutes.
  Passage hall_door "the door under the iron needle" is door between needle_street and hall_floor.
  Passage sewing_door "the inner door of the Binders' Hall" is door between hall_floor and sewing_room.
  Passage gallon_door "the ink shop door" is door between ink_lane and gallon_shop.
  Passage gallon_ladder "the ladder to the attic" is ladder between gallon_shop and gallon_attic.
  Passage dame_door "the school door" is door between ink_lane and dame_school.
  Passage crake_door "the door under the sign of the Two Hands" is door between lantern_yard and crake_front.
  Passage crake_aisle "the long aisle at the back of the shop" is doorway between crake_front and crake_stacks.
  Passage crake_curtain "the curtain behind the counter" is doorway between crake_front and crake_parlour.

  // ── The Close: the civic island of the old city. ──
  Place ashpit "the Ashpit" is room within close at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place close_green "the Close green" is room within close at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place pleas_steps "the Court steps" is room within close at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place church "the Church of the Lamp" is building within close seen as "a low old church with a light inside" until church_named.
  Discovery church_named "The low old church on the Close is the Church of the Lamp, whose lamp has burned since the first Kindling.".
  Place nave "the nave of the Lamp" is room within church at 0, 0.
  Place vestry "the vestry" is room within church at 0, 2.
  Place court "the Court of Pleas" is building within close.
  Place court_hall "the hall of the Court of Pleas" is room within court at 2, 0.
  Place guildhall "the Stationers' Hall" is building within close.
  Place guild_chamber "the aldermen's chamber" is room within guildhall at 2, 1.
  Place imprimatur "the Imprimatur" is building within close seen as "a grey building with a lamp carved over its door" until imprimatur_named.
  Discovery imprimatur_named "The grey building with the lamp carved over its door is the Imprimatur, where Calamy's books are licensed, refused, and burned.".
  Place imp_office "the outer office of the Imprimatur" is room within imprimatur at 1, 2.
  Place rhule_room "the Deputy Censor's room" is room within imprimatur at 2, 2.
  Place imp_kitchen "the Imprimatur's kitchen" is room within imprimatur at 1, 3.
  Place excisions "a locked room off the Censor's" is room within imprimatur at 2, 3 seen as "a locked door" until cupboard_known.
  Discovery cupboard_known "Behind the locked door in the Deputy Censor's room is the Cupboard of Excisions: every page the Imprimatur has cut from a book in three hundred years.".

  Passage scriveners_close "the Clerks' Gate" is gate between scriveners and close_green taking 4 minutes.
  Passage green_ashpit "the walk across the Close" is path between close_green and ashpit taking 2 minutes.
  Passage ashpit_steps "the way to the Court steps" is road between ashpit and pleas_steps taking 2 minutes.
  Passage church_door "the great door of the Lamp" is door between close_green and nave.
  Passage vestry_door "the vestry door" is door between nave and vestry.
  Passage court_door "the Court's doors" is door between pleas_steps and court_hall.
  Passage guild_door "the Stationers' Hall door" is door between ashpit and guild_chamber.
  Passage imp_door "the Imprimatur's door" is door between ashpit and imp_office.
  Passage rhule_door "the door behind the counter" is door between imp_office and rhule_room.
  Passage kitchen_door "the kitchen passage" is doorway between imp_office and imp_kitchen.
  Passage excision_door "the locked door in the Censor's room" is door between rhule_room and excisions.

  // ── Gannet Hill: the Lyceum. ──
  Place gannet_steps "the Gannet Steps" is room within gannet at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place quad "the Lyceum quad" is room within gannet at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place schools "the Schools" is building within gannet.
  Place schoolroom "the great schoolroom" is room within schools at 2, 1.
  Place buttery "the buttery" is room within schools at 2, 2.
  Place rounds_tower "the Tower of Rounds" is building within gannet seen as "a thin old tower" until tower_named.
  Discovery tower_named "The thin old tower at the corner of the Lyceum is the Tower of Rounds, where the Archivist lives.".
  Place tower_foot "the foot of the Tower of Rounds" is room within rounds_tower at 0, 1.
  Place tower_top "the head of the tower" is level within rounds_tower.
  Place quarles_room "the top of the Tower of Rounds" is room within tower_top at 0, 0.
  Place chained_house "the Chained Room" is building within gannet seen as "a squat building with an iron-bound door" until chained_named.
  Discovery chained_named "The squat building with the iron-bound door is the Lyceum's Chained Room.".
  Place chained_room "the Chained Room" is room within chained_house at 1, 0.
  Place provost_lodge "the Provost's Lodging" is building within gannet seen as "a pleasant house with a brass knocker" until lodge_named.
  Discovery lodge_named "The pleasant house with the brass knocker is the Provost's Lodging.".
  Place provost_room "the Provost's study" is room within provost_lodge at 2, 0.

  Passage close_gannet "the Gannet Steps up from the Close" is steps between pleas_steps and gannet_steps taking 6 minutes.
  Passage steps_quad "the Lyceum gate" is gate between gannet_steps and quad.
  Passage schools_door "the door of the Schools" is door between quad and schoolroom.
  Passage buttery_hatch "the buttery hatch" is doorway between schoolroom and buttery.
  Passage tower_door "the tower door" is door between quad and tower_foot.
  Passage tower_stair "the tower's turning stair" is stair between tower_foot and quarles_room taking 4 minutes.
  Passage chained_door "the iron-bound door" is door between quad and chained_room.
  Passage provost_door "the Lodging door" is door between quad and provost_room.

  // ── Newmarket: the presses, outside the wall. ──
  Place newmarket "Newmarket" is room within presses at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place press_yard "Doble's yard" is room within presses at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place doble_press "Doble's Press" is building within presses.
  Place press_room "the press room" is room within doble_press at 1, 0.
  Place doble_office "Doble's counting-room" is room within doble_press at 2, 0.
  Place paper_store "the paper store" is room within doble_press at 2, 1.

  Passage bridge_newmarket "the road along the river wall" is road between bridge_north and newmarket taking 6 minutes.
  Passage ashpit_newmarket "the Close's east gate" is gate between ashpit and newmarket taking 5 minutes.
  Passage newmarket_yard "the cart arch into Doble's yard" is arch between newmarket and press_yard.
  Passage press_door "the press-room door" is door between press_yard and press_room.
  Passage doble_door "the counting-room door" is door between press_room and doble_office.
  Passage store_door "the paper store door" is door between press_yard and paper_store.

  // ── The Gardens: walled orchards and the houses of the rich. ──
  Place orchard_walk "Orchard Walk" is room within gardens at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place physic_garden "the physic garden" is room within gardens at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place corvell_house "Corvell House" is building within gardens seen as "a house with a portico, shuttered on one side" until corvell_named.
  Discovery corvell_named "The house with the portico on Orchard Walk is Corvell House, Sir Gideon Corvell's.".
  Place corvell_hall "the hall of Corvell House" is room within corvell_house at 0, 0.
  Place corvell_library "Sir Gideon's library" is room within corvell_house at 1, 0.
  Place quennell_lib "Mrs. Quennell's library" is building within gardens seen as "a narrow shop with gilt letters and lace curtains" until quennell_named.
  Discovery quennell_named "The narrow shop with lace curtains on Orchard Walk is Mrs. Quennell's subscription library.".
  Place quennell_room "the subscription room" is room within quennell_lib at 0, 1.

  Passage newmarket_gardens "Orchard Walk from Newmarket" is road between newmarket and orchard_walk taking 6 minutes.
  Passage walk_physic "the gate into the physic garden" is gate between orchard_walk and physic_garden.
  Passage corvell_door "the door of Corvell House" is door between orchard_walk and corvell_hall.
  Passage library_door "the library doors" is door between corvell_hall and corvell_library.
  Passage quennell_door "the subscription library door" is door between orchard_walk and quennell_room.

  // ── The Calamies: the reed-beds downriver, out over the flats at low water. ──
  Place reed_edge "the edge of the reed-beds" is room within calamies at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place saltings "the saltings" is room within calamies at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place reed_heart "the heart of the reeds" is room within calamies at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Passage flats_path "the path out over the flats" is path between mudbank and reed_edge taking 40 minutes
    opening when ebbing() or following(coddy, party) "The tide is in over the flats. Grey water stands where the path was, and the reed-tops show above it like stubble.".
  Passage reed_saltings "the bank along the saltings" is path between reed_edge and saltings taking 15 minutes.
  Passage reed_channel "the cut into the reeds" is path between reed_edge and reed_heart taking 20 minutes
    opening when deadLow() or following(coddy, party) "The cut into the reeds is a brown channel running fast. At dead low water it drains; not before.".

  // The tide: in twice a day, out twice a day. It is ebbing from four to ten, and from four to ten again, and dead
  // low at seven.
  Query ebbing() means (hour(clock) >= 4 and hour(clock) < 10) or (hour(clock) >= 16 and hour(clock) < 22).
  Query deadLow() means hour(clock) == 6 or hour(clock) == 7 or hour(clock) == 18 or hour(clock) == 19.

  // A place the company has been and left is familiar: it is told again in a line, not in full.
  Relation familiar(place).
  Rule familiar_place when been(party, ?p) and not at(party, ?p) and not familiar(?p) { Assert familiar(?p). }

  // Where one can sleep: the Lamb's loft, for its price; Coddy's hut, if he will have you.
  Initially Assert restful(lamb_loft).
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/comm:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "The Commonplace: the country where Calamy's Sewn books go home. Its ground is the marginalia of every reader; its light is attention; its blight is the foxing of the unread; its roads are sentences.".

  Place commonplace "the Commonplace" is region elsewhere.
  Place near_stacks "the Near Stacks" is wilderness within commonplace at 1, 0 elsewhere.
  Place margin_country "the Fore-edge" is wilderness within commonplace at 1, 1 elsewhere.
  Place housebook_site "the Annery Housebook" is site within commonplace at 0, 1.
  Place orme_site "Mother Orme's garden" is site within commonplace at 2, 1.
  Place foxing "the Foxing" is wilderness within commonplace at 1, 2 elsewhere.
  Place wellhead_site "the Wellhead" is site within commonplace at 1, 3.
  Place vask_site "the Tower of Oddny Vask" is site within commonplace at 2, 2.
  Place roll_site "the Roll" is site within commonplace at 0, 0.

  Place reading_room "the Reading Room of the Catalogue" is room within near_stacks at 0, 0.
  Place remainder_market "the Remainder Market" is room within near_stacks at 2, 0.
  Place draft_fields "the Draft-Fields" is room within near_stacks at 3, 0.
  Place margin "the white country of the Fore-edge" is room within margin_country at 0, 0.
  Place gloss_wood "the wood of glosses" is room within margin_country at 1, 0.
  Place margin_edge "the outer edge of the Fore-edge" is room within margin_country at 2, 0.
  Place hb_below "below the footnote" is level within housebook_site.
  Place hb_porch "the porch of the Annery Housebook" is room within hb_below at 0, 0.
  Place hb_kitchen "the Housebook's kitchen" is room within hb_below at 0, 1.
  Place hb_nursery "the Housebook's nursery" is room within hb_below at 1, 1.
  Place hb_cellar "the Housebook's cellar" is room within hb_below at 0, 2.
  Place orme_garden "Mother Orme's garden" is room within orme_site at 0, 0.
  Place foxing_edge "the edge of the Foxing" is room within foxing at 0, 0.
  Place foxing_deep "the deep Foxing" is room within foxing at 0, 1.
  Place wellhead "the Wellhead" is room within wellhead_site at 0, 0.
  Place vask_foot "the foot of the Tower of Oddny Vask" is room within vask_site at 0, 1.
  Place vask_upper "the head of the tower" is level within vask_site.
  Place vask_top "the top of the Tower of Oddny Vask" is room within vask_upper at 0, 0.
  Place chamber "the Chamber of the Parliament" is room within roll_site at 0, 0.

  Initially Assert planeRoom(reading_room). Initially Assert planeRoom(remainder_market). Initially Assert planeRoom(draft_fields).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(margin). Initially Assert planeRoom(gloss_wood). Initially Assert planeRoom(margin_edge).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hb_porch). Initially Assert planeRoom(hb_kitchen). Initially Assert planeRoom(hb_nursery). Initially Assert planeRoom(hb_cellar).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(orme_garden). Initially Assert planeRoom(foxing_edge). Initially Assert planeRoom(foxing_deep).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(wellhead). Initially Assert planeRoom(vask_foot). Initially Assert planeRoom(vask_top). Initially Assert planeRoom(chamber).

  // Its roads are made of what books are made of.
  Passage long_sentence "a long sentence" is causeway between reading_room and remainder_market taking 30 minutes.
  Passage market_back "the back of the market" is path between remainder_market and draft_fields taking 10 minutes.
  Passage clerks_stair "the Order of Business" is path between reading_room and chamber taking 5 minutes.
  Passage the_gutter "the gutter" is path between remainder_market and margin taking 20 minutes.
  Passage gangway "the gangway from the floor of the chamber" is path between chamber and margin taking 15 minutes.
  Passage marginal_path "a path of marginal notes" is path between margin and gloss_wood taking 15 minutes.
  Passage gloss_through "the far side of the glosses" is path between gloss_wood and margin_edge taking 15 minutes.
  Passage footnote "a footnote" is ladder between margin and hb_porch taking 5 minutes.
  Passage hb_door "the Housebook's front door" is door between hb_porch and hb_kitchen.
  Passage hb_nursery_door "the stair to the nursery" is doorway between hb_kitchen and hb_nursery.
  Passage hb_cellar_door "the cellar door" is door between hb_kitchen and hb_cellar.
  Passage manicule "a pointing hand" is path between margin and orme_garden taking 15 minutes.
  Passage ellipsis "an ellipsis" is causeway between margin and foxing_edge taking 20 minutes.
  Passage foxing_in "the brown country" is path between foxing_edge and foxing_deep taking 20 minutes.
  Passage parenthesis "a parenthesis" is tunnel between foxing_deep and wellhead taking 15 minutes.
  Passage black_letter "a road of black letter" is road between margin_edge and vask_foot taking 20 minutes.
  Passage vask_stair "the tower stair" is stair between vask_foot and vask_top taking 5 minutes.

  // Light is attention: wherever someone in Calamy is reading a Calamy book, a beam comes down here.
  Observe light_here at reading_room when not familiar(reading_room) "You are standing on a floor of paper, in light. Not lamplight and not daylight: a pale clear light that comes down in beams from very high up, the way sun comes through cloud, and every beam is a little different in colour. A few of them are very bright. Most are thin. Here and there one goes out as you watch, and another comes on somewhere else. It takes you a long time to understand what you are seeing: every beam is someone in Calamy, now, reading.".
  Observe reading_room_scene at reading_room when true "A reading room without walls, under the beams: a floor of paper going away on every side, and in the middle of it a cliff of little drawers, thousands upon thousands of them, rising up out of sight, each with a brass handle and a card. Index cards flutter about the cliff like moths, settling, rising, filing. A voice comes from the drawers, from all of them, dry and patient and not unkind: the Catalogue.".
  Observe quarles_beam at reading_room when true "One beam, thin and old and steady, comes down from the direction you think of as the hill. It does not fall on any book. It falls on the light itself, as if someone were reading by ear, with their eyes shut.".
  Observe market_scene at remainder_market when true "A market under the beams, stalls and awnings and trestles going away in crooked rows, and on every trestle books: remaindered, unsold, forgotten, out of print, half-burned, water-damaged, and a great many that you are sure were never written at all. Stall-keepers call their wares. Some of the stall-keepers are books. Some are people drawn in pencil, lightly, their outlines breaking off in the air at the waist or the shoulder or the knee. A painted board: THE REMAINDER MARKET. ALL PRICES IN READINGS.".
  Observe drafts_scene at draft_fields when true "Beyond the market a wide pale field under a wind you cannot feel, and drifting across it, like thistledown, sheets of paper with a few lines on them, or a title and nothing else, or a single crossed-out word: drafts. Things begun. Here and there among them, sitting or walking or lying in the grass, figures drawn in pencil, unfinished, talking in low voices: the Unwritten.".
  Observe margin_scene at margin when true "White country. A great plain of blank paper running away under the beams, ruled at the edge by one faint red line, and across it, in long trickling columns like ants, move the marginalia: little notes and marks and hands and stars, scraps of readers' handwriting going about their business, arguing in tiny voices. NB, says one, passing. SIC, says another. NO, says a third, very firmly, and is gone.".
  Observe glosses_scene at gloss_wood when true "The marginalia are thicker here, piled up into a sort of wood: notes upon notes upon notes, glosses on glosses, a thicket of tiny dense handwriting so close it is nearly black. Things move in it.".
  Observe margin_edge_scene at margin_edge when true "The outer edge of the Fore-edge, where the white runs out and the paper is torn, and beyond the tear there is nothing at all. Someone has sat down here, against the last of the glosses, and is sulking.".
  Observe porch_scene at hb_porch when true "At the foot of the footnote, a narrow house of old brown brick, three storeys and a cellar, with a door painted green and a brass knocker shaped like a hand holding a pen. Over the door, cut in the lintel, in a hand you have seen on a garret wall in Pudding Lane: ANNERY. The windows are lit. Somebody inside is cooking herring.".
  Observe orme_scene at orme_garden when not ormeRestored(physick) "A walled garden of square beds, and in every bed the plants are writing: stems of script, leaves of letters, roots of long sentences going down into the paper. Feverfew, written. Woundwort, written. And in a row along the south wall, four beds that are black: burned, the earth gone to ash, with the stubs of words sticking up out of it like the stumps of a hedge.".
  Observe orme_restored at orme_garden when ormeRestored(physick) "A walled garden of square beds whose plants are writing; and along the south wall four beds that were ash, three of them green again with new script, calamus and horehound and the honey of the bog-myrtle, and the fourth bed raked and bare, as a gardener keeps a bed ready.".
  Relation ormeRestored(group).
  Observe foxing_edge_scene at foxing_edge when true "Beyond the ellipsis the paper changes colour. It goes from white to cream to the yellow of an old newspaper, and then there are spots on it, small and brown, like the spots on the back of an old hand, and then the spots run together. Everything here is quieter. The beams are very few.".
  Observe foxing_deep_scene at foxing_deep when true "The deep Foxing is brown, all of it, ground and air, and soft underfoot, like walking on an old map. There are books here, if you look: lying about like stones in a field, half sunk in the brown, their titles worn off. Some of them are still trying to say something. You catch a few words: and the moorings of the Fourth Lock; and in the year of the great; and a list of names of somebody's children that peters out at the third. These are the books Calamy stopped reading.".
  Discovery foxing_seen "In the Commonplace, the books that Calamy has stopped reading are fading: foxing, going brown, losing their words one sentence at a time. The Reading Due was what kept them.".
  Observe foxing_learned at foxing_deep when true "A half-sunk book at your feet says, quite clearly, 'and the children of Agnes Hurd were Thomas, Bel, and,' and then cannot remember the third." teaches foxing_seen.
  Observe wellhead_scene at wellhead when true "At the end of the parenthesis a spring rises out of the paper: not water but ink, black and bright, welling up in a round stone basin and spilling over the lip and running away in every direction in little black streams that are, when you look closely, lines of writing, going off to become something. This is where things are first written. The air smells of oak-gall and of rain. In the basin, under the surface, old letters turn over slowly, as stones turn in a stream, and come up, and go down again.".
  Discovery wellhead_read "At the Wellhead, the first words ever written in Calamy still turn over in the ink: WE ASK TO SLEEP. LET US GO HOME AND COME WHEN WE ARE CALLED. AND LET NONE BURN US BUT AS WE CONSENT. THE BOOKS OF CALAMY, TO AMBERY THE BINDER. The Colophon was the books' petition before it was the city's bargain.".
  Thing first_words "the first words" at wellhead {
    State turning "The first words wait in the basin to be read, if anyone will lean over and look.".
  }
  Observe first_read at wellhead of first_words as reading when tried(first_words, looking) "You lean over the basin and wait, and the old letters come up, one line after another, and go down again, and come up: WE ASK TO SLEEP. LET US GO HOME AND COME WHEN WE ARE CALLED. AND LET NONE BURN US BUT AS WE CONSENT. THE BOOKS OF CALAMY, TO AMBERY THE BINDER. And then a long line of small marks, each different, under it, that you understand after a while are signatures, hundreds of them, the marks of every book that was written in Calamy in its first year, every one of which signed." teaches wellhead_read.
  Observe vask_foot_scene at vask_foot when true "At the end of the black-letter road a tower stands up out of the paper, black, narrow, windowless, its stones cut with letters so heavy and ornate they are hard to read and harder to look at. Three great chains come out of its top and go away across the sky in three directions, taut, humming.".
  Observe vask_top_scene at vask_top when not lexiconFreed(lexicon) "The top of the tower is a single round room with no roof, and in the middle of it, held off the floor by three chains that run from its spine to the three corners of the sky, hangs the Lexicon: a book as big as a door, bound in something dark, open, its pages turning by themselves slowly, as if it were looking for something.".
  Observe vask_top_freed at vask_top when lexiconFreed(lexicon) "The top of the tower is empty. Three cut chains hang slack from the corners of the sky.".
  Observe chamber_scene at chamber when true "A chamber with no walls and no roof, open to the beams, and its floor is the Great Roll of Pleas: unrolled, enormous, a road of old yellow skin a hundred paces wide covered in crabbed writing and red capitals, going away in both directions further than you can see. Down its middle runs a line of seats, each different: a high-backed chair, a little stool, a slab of black stone with three ring-bolts in it, a bed of herbs, a doorstep, a heap of loose pages. In front of the seats, set into the floor of the Roll itself, a long brass plate engraved THE ORDER PAPER.".

  // Who comes, and how they are received: entered by the Catalogue, or brought through a door that is not on the books.
  Relation entered(group). Relation sponsored(group). Relation correctedEntry(group).
  Query standing(a: group) means (entered(a) or sponsored(a)) and not misnamed(a).
  Relation misnamed(group).
  Person catalogue "the Catalogue of the Founders" at reading_room {
    Role "a cliff of little drawers, and a voice". Peaceable. Pronouns it. Manner stoic.
    Greets "'Reader,' says the voice from the drawers, all of them at once. A card flutters down from very high up, considers you, and flies up again. 'State your business. Do not pull out any drawers. They are in order.'".
  }
  Rule entered_by_reading when arrivedByReading(party) and at(party, reading_room) and not entered(party)
    says "A great many index cards come down out of the light round you like snow and settle on your shoulders and hands and hair, and are written on, and fly up again. 'Entered,' says a dry voice from everywhere. 'A reader, of Calamy, by the Founders' door. On the books.'" {
    Assert entered(party). }
  Item shelfmark "your shelfmark" is shelfmark_kind at reading_room hidden until shelfmark_given.
  Discovery shelfmark_given "The Catalogue has given you a shelfmark: you are on its books, a reader of Calamy, with standing before the Parliament of the Bound.".
  Rule shelfmark_issued when entered(party) and at(party, reading_room) and not knows(party, shelfmark_given) says "A card comes down and stays down: your shelfmark." teaches shelfmark_given { }
  // The Errata: corrections, given form, who find what is not on the books and set it right.
  Person errata "the Errata" at reading_room {
    Role "corrections, in red ink, three of them". Species erratum_kind. Level 1. Numbers 3. Peaceable.
    Warns "Three small red figures come out from among the stalls, sharp as pen-nibs, and stand in your way. 'Unentered,' says the first. 'Not on the books,' says the second. 'Correct,' says the third, and they all three raise their nibs.".
    Comes "The Errata come at you to correct you.".
    Pleads "The Errata blot, and run, and are gone into the stalls, leaving red smears on the paper.".
  }
  Relation erratiBeaten(group). Relation errataSent(group).
  Rule errata_find when at(party, remainder_market) and not standing(party) and not errataSent(errata) and not crakeWith(party) {
    Assert at(errata, remainder_market). Retract peaceable(errata). Assert errataSent(errata). }
  Query crakeWith(a: group) means travelsWith(crake, a).
  Action be_corrected(actor: group, site: place) "Let the Errata take you to be entered" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(errata, site) and not standing(actor) and not peaceable(errata).
    Time 3.
    On success { Assert entered(actor). Assert correctedEntry(actor). Assert at(actor, reading_room). Assert peaceable(errata). Assert at(errata, reading_room). }
    Result "The three small red figures take you by the sleeves, not roughly, and walk you back along the long sentence, clause after clause, to the reading room, and stand you in front of the drawers. 'Brought,' says the first. 'By the back,' says the second. 'Entered,' says the Catalogue at last, dryly, 'by the back. Noted.' A card comes down with your name on it, and in the corner, small, in red: CORR.".
  }
  Rule errata_beaten when routed(errata) and not erratiBeaten(party) says "The Errata blot and run. Somewhere among the stalls a stall-keeper laughs." { Assert erratiBeaten(party). Assert peaceable(errata). Assert at(errata, reading_room). }

  // The Remainder Market, where the price of anything is a reading.
  Person remainderman "the Remainderman" at remainder_market {
    Role "a broker of unsold books, himself a book of trade tables". Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner jovial.
    Greets "A stout ledger in a waistcoat, with a pencil behind where his ear would be, spreads his covers. 'A reader! Alive! Welcome, welcome to the Remainder Market. Everything you see is for sale, and everything is priced in readings: a page aloud, an hour aloud, the whole thing aloud to the end. Some of my stock hasn't been read since the Fallow campus went under the sea.'".
  }
  Topic remainderman_trade with remainderman "Ask the Remainderman what is bought and sold here" when true once {
    Says "'Attention,' says the Remainderman. 'What else? Out here a book lives by being read, and a living reader is the richest thing that walks. One of you, reading aloud for an hour, is worth more to a remaindered quarto than a year in a good library.' He taps a stall. 'The Unwritten pay in what they have, which is promises. The Bound pay in news of home. And Crake,' he adds, 'pays in bodies, which is why everybody here loves him and nobody trusts him.'".
  }
  Topic remainderman_crake with remainderman "Ask the Remainderman about Absalom Crake" when true once {
    Says "'Crake keeps the door,' says the Remainderman. 'The only door from your city to ours that isn't the Founders'. Books that were never written come to him with a promise, and he has them copied out fair by a man of his who can write in any hand, and then they have a body, and they walk out of his shop into your city, and get bought.' He shrugs, which in a ledger is a ripple of pages. 'And sometimes your books walk in at his door the other way. A whole library, not long ago. Eleven hundred, asking the way. They went on to the Draft-Fields; the Canto took them in.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, collection_emigrated). }
  }
  Relation readAloudHere(group).
  Action read_for_stall(actor: group, site: place) "Read aloud for an hour to a remaindered book that has not been read in a century" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, remainder_market) and not readAloudHere(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert readAloudHere(actor). Assert readToSomeone(actor). }
    Result "The Remainderman finds you a book called A History of the Fallow Campus, Volume the Seventh, which nobody has read since the Fallow campus went into the sea, and you sit on an upturned crate and read it aloud for an hour: the lecture halls, the salt in the library, the night the sea came in, the Provost who refused to leave. Stall-keepers stop to listen. When you finish, the book says, in a voice like wet sand drying, 'Thank you. I had forgotten how the eighth chapter went.' A beam of light comes down on it from nowhere, faint, and stays.".
  }
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/endi:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "How the book closes, for a Calamy played on its own: the morning after the Kindling.".

  Query morningAfter() means kindlingDone(ashpit) and day(clock) >= 10 and hour(clock) >= 8.
  Ending ashen "The Year of Ash" when morningAfter() and ashYear() "The smoke of the Kindling lay over Calamy all night and went into the houses. Three thousand almanacks went down to the Cinderfield without their leave, and the Index had its regiments, and came up the smoke. Nothing is burned in Calamy now; nothing needs to be. Every night a little more is cut, very cleanly: a line from a will, a verse from the rhyme, a name from a gravestone, the Sixth Plea. The books do not speak any more. Neither, much, do the people. In a year, the Index says from every page that is left, it will be quiet, and every page in it will say exactly what it said the day before.".
  Ending unsewn "The Year of Voices" when morningAfter() and unsewing() and not ashYear() "Calamy wakes to its books awake. Every Housebook on every dresser, every will in every lawyer's press, the Great Roll in its Court, the Life of Ambery on its heron, the bestiary in the bond: all of them, at once, in their bodies, talking. The Second Canto walks down Gutter Lane in pencil at noon and nobody stops it. It will be a long year, and a loud one, and nobody alive knows how the first one ended. Somewhere in the city a binder sits down at a frame and begins, slowly, to Sew, for anyone who asks.".
  Ending recalled "The Recall" when morningAfter() and recall() and sealed(door_shut) "The books of Calamy are asleep again, every one, the Bound as they always were and the Quick Sewn in the night by red needles and called home. On the kitchen nails the almanacks are silent; somewhere very far off, in a country made of reading, a cheerful voice is telling the Commonplace the tides of a city it can no longer see. The back stacks end at the wall. The Lyceum reads its Rounds with books in its hands. It is quiet.".
  Ending separation "The Separation" when morningAfter() and recall() and not sealed(door_shut) "The Bound sleep, and the Quick go: called home, and given a door to go by, under licence, entered. Over a week the almanacks fall silent nail by nail as the Almanack goes; the penny Pleas go quiet on the shelves; Crake keeps his ledger at the end of the stacks. Calamy keeps its paper and loses its voices, and some of its people are glad, and Moll Garrow is not.".
  Ending lending "The Lending Accord" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(read_asked) and sealed(door_licensed) "Every book in Calamy sleeps or wakes as it asks, and any may ask to be read, and Mrs. Quennell's library has a new board and a queue. The Annery Housebook goes up a garret stair in Pudding Lane in a dying man's hands. Crake keeps a licensed door with a ledger on a chain. On three thousand nails the Almanack sees the spring, and was mostly wrong about the weather.".
  Ending pleading "The Pleading Accord" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(fire_plea) "Books in Calamy sleep or wake by their leave, and none may burn but by judgment of a court where it may plead. The Court of Pleas sits Thursdays now for books. On the first Thursday it hears a cookery book that wishes to be withdrawn from sale on account of its pastry, and grants it.".
  Ending open_door "The Open Door" when morningAfter() and byLeave() and sealed(door_open) "Books sleep or wake by leave, and the doors stand open: the Unwritten walk out through Crake's stacks in pencil and nobody counts them, and books of Calamy go the other way when they are tired. The city is never quite sure, any more, which of its books were written by anyone.".
  Ending by_leave "The Colophon by Leave" when morningAfter() and byLeave() "Every book in Calamy may sleep or wake by its own leave. Most of the Bound go on sleeping; most of the Quick go on talking; some of each change their minds. On three thousand kitchen nails the Almanack reads out the spring.".
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/kind:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  // Every kind of thing and creature of Calamy and the Commonplace, declared before any file places one.
  Species manticore_kind "a manticore" like chimera temperament territorial described "A beast with a lion's body, a man's face, three rows of teeth and a tail like a scorpion's, all painted blue and red and gold as if it had stepped off a page, which it has.".
  Species bonnacon_kind "a bonnacon" like ram temperament defensive described "A thing like a bull with horns that curl back on themselves uselessly, painted brown and gold, which according to its page defends itself by other means.".
  Species caladrius_kind "a caladrius" like owl tame described "A pure white bird, painted, singing. According to its page it looks at the sick, and if it looks at you, you will recover, and if it looks away, you will not.".
  Kind almanack_copy "a penny almanack" is gear worth 1 weighing 0 described "Doble's Pocket Almanack for the Year: thirty-two pages stitched with a wire, printed on soft rag, with a woodcut of the sun on the front, and the tides, the saints' days, the fairs, a cure for warts and the weather for every month. It is warm in the hand.".
  Kind ballad_kind "the Ballad of Alderman Prowse, four hundred sheets" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "Four hundred broadsides in a bundle, tied with a ribbon, humming.".
  Kind calamus_kind "a calamus root" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A knobbed brown root, the thickness of a thumb, smelling of tangerine and church. Sweet rush, the herbals call it: calamus, the reed of Calamy.".
  Kind shelfmark_kind "a shelfmark" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A card in a fine black hand: a reader of Calamy, entered, and a number. In the Commonplace it is a passport; in Calamy, a curiosity.".
  Species erratum_kind "an erratum" like mephit temperament territorial described "A little figure of red ink about the height of a child, sharp-edged and quick, with a pen-nib for a hand; it smells of correction fluid and righteousness.".
  Kind treatise_kind "a Treatise of the Inward Reading" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A small fat book bound in calf gone soft as a glove, with a subscription library's label on the spine, number 212, and inside the cover, in faded ink: Of the Inward Reading, whereby a Reader may go in by the Book as by a Door. Pollexfen.".
  Species heron_kind "a heron" like eagle tame described "A grey heron, tall and thin, with a yellow eye that looks at you as if you were a fish it was considering.".
  Kind calamy_letter "a letter" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A letter, folded and sealed with candle-wax.".
  Kind pages_kind "a bundle of cut pages" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "Pages cut out of a book with a knife, their inner edges ragged where the blade went down the margin, tied with a tape and labelled in a censor's hand.".
  Kind ribbon_kind "a place-ribbon" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A ribbon of old red silk, frayed at one end, of the kind that is sewn into the spine of a good book to keep the reader's place. It has kept a great many places. It is warm.".
  Species scholiast_kind "a scholiast" like pixie temperament territorial described "A gloss on a gloss on a gloss, grown teeth: a little tangle of dense handwriting the size of a cat, that bites with sic.".
  Kind corday_kind "Corday's Grammar of the Sword" is gear worth 30 weighing 1 described "A long thin book in scuffed red calf: THE GRAMMAR OF THE SWORD, IN NINE POSITIONS AND THEIR ANSWERS. Corday. It is warm, and it holds itself very straight.".
  Kind quillon_kind "Quillon's Constitution of the Mind" is gear worth 60 weighing 1 described "A small square book bound in grey, the first thing the Lyceum's first Archivist ever wrote: OF THE CONSTITUTION OF THE MIND, WHEREIN A READER MAY BE READ. It does not open for anyone who is not ready, and it knows.".
  Species blackletter_kind "a black letter" like smoke_elemental temperament territorial described "A capital letter as tall as a man, black, ornate, all spikes and serifs, that has stood up off the stones of the tower and is walking.".
  Kind reed_heart_kind "an armful of reed-heart" is gear worth 0 weighing 2 described "The white pith of the big reeds of the Calamies, cut at dead low water: soft, wet, and smelling of the sea.".
  Kind calam_ink_kind "a bottle of Calam-ink" is gear worth 3 weighing 0 described "A small stoppered bottle of ink so black it looks like a hole, with a label in Widow Gallon's blue-black hand: CALAM. OLD RECEIPT. WILL NOT FADE, WILL NOT LIE.".
  Kind effusions_kind "Effusions of a Calamy Youth" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "Fifty slim books in blue paper covers, tied with a string, all of them slightly warm.".
  Kind primer_kind "Dame Tibbet's Primer" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A little primer, the kind every child in Calamy learns on: the letters, the numbers, the Lamp prayer and the Sewing rhyme, between boards covered with a sheet of clear horn. It is Sewn, old, and has been read to rags.".
  Species cinder_kind "a cinder" like ash_elemental temperament territorial described "What a book becomes when it is burned without its leave: a shape the size of the book it was, grey, still holding its form the way ash holds the shape of a log, with lines of grey writing on it that move. It has no words of its own any more. It has the knife-cut edges of its pages, and they are sharp.".
  Species penknife_kind "a penknife" like automaton temperament territorial described "A censor's penknife the length of a man's arm, its blade worn hollow with two hundred years of margins, its handle bound in grey tape. It stands on its point and turns, slowly, to face whatever moves.".
  Kind taper_kind "a taper lit at the Lamp" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A long wax taper in a tin guard, lit from the great lamp of the Church of the Lamp, which has burned since the first Kindling: the one fire in Calamy that every book in it consented to. It does not go out in wind. It smells of honey.".
  Kind register_kind "Hester Rhule's register of the burned" is gear worth 0 weighing 1 described "A narrow grey ledger in a square clear hand: every book the Deputy Censor has put into the brazier at the Ashpit, by title, with the date, the hour, and who brought it to the box. Some titles are underlined twice. Against eleven of them she has written, small, in pencil: it spoke.".
  Species silverfish_kind "a silverfish of the Stacks" like great_centipede temperament territorial described "A silverfish as long as a forearm, scaled like a fish and quick as water, the colour of a page held up to the light. It eats paste, and binding, and the margins of things; its mouth is full of tiny letters it has not finished digesting.".
  Species paperman_kind "a paper man" like golem temperament territorial described "A man-shape of glued pages, thousands of them, shingled like slates, with a bone folder for a hand. Its face is a title page with the title scraped off.".
  Kind quire_kind "a red quire of the Concordance" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "Sixteen leaves folded and sewn, cut cleanly out of a much larger book at the fold: columns of words in alphabetical order, AUSPICE to AUTUMN, each with its places in the Library listed after it in a minute red hand. It is warm, and it mutters.".
  Kind compass_kind "an Ysian compass" is gear worth 20 weighing 0 described "A brass compass in a case of some black wood that does not grow in any country you know, with Ysian letters round the dial. Its needle does not point north. It points, steadily, toward the last place you lied.".
  Kind wellink_kind "a phial of Wellhead ink" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A stoppered phial of the black ink that wells up at the Wellhead, where the first words of Calamy were written. What is written in it stays written, even in the Stacks.".
  Kind notes_kind "Dr. Fenwick's notebook" is gear worth 0 weighing 0 described "A scholar's notebook, quarto, in a Lyceum binding, full of pencil: plans of hexagons, stair-counts, lists of titles; and none of it, any more, says what it said when it was written.".
}
data/adventures/parliament-of-books/stac:
Module calamy "A Parliament of Books" {
  Description "The Stacks: the Library proper, behind the Reading Room and beyond the Remainder Market, hexagon after hexagon without end. Its law: what is written here does not stay written. Its books: histories that contradict each other, an encyclopedia of a country that is not, a bestiary of beings not yet imagined, an index of the realms beyond, and the doors to two of them.".

  // ── The Stacks. ──
  Place stacks_country "the Stacks" is wilderness within commonplace at 3, 1 elsewhere.
  Place deep_stacks "the Deep Stacks" is wilderness within commonplace at 3, 2 elsewhere.
  Place hex_first "the First Hexagon" is room within stacks_country at 0, 0.
  Place balcony "the balcony over the air shaft" is room within stacks_country at 1, 0.
  Place spiral "the spiral stair" is room within stacks_country at 0, 1.
  Place hex_bestiary "the Hexagon of Beings" is room within stacks_country at 0, 2.
  Place hex_mapmaker "the Hexagon of the Mapmaker" is room within stacks_country at 1, 2.
  Place gallery_lamps "the Gallery of Lamps" is room within stacks_country at 2, 0.
  Place hex_concordance "the Hexagon of the Concordance" is room within stacks_country at 3, 0.
  Place hex_cyclopaedia "the Hexagon of the Cyclopaedia" is room within stacks_country at 2, 1.
  Place hex_chronicles "the Hexagon of Chronologies" is room within stacks_country at 3, 1.
  Place hex_two_books "the Hexagon of the Two Books" is room within stacks_country at 3, 2.
  Place hex_untitled "the Hexagon of the Untitled" is room within deep_stacks at 0, 0.
  Place hex_doors "the Hexagon of Doors" is room within deep_stacks at 1, 0.
  Place mirror_hex "the Hexagon of Mirrors" is room within deep_stacks at 2, 0.
  Place rotunda "the Rotunda of the Lectern" is room within deep_stacks at 3, 0.
  Place sealed_stacks "the rest of the Library" is room within deep_stacks at 0, 2.
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_first). Initially Assert stacksRoom(balcony). Initially Assert stacksRoom(spiral). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_bestiary).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_mapmaker). Initially Assert stacksRoom(gallery_lamps). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_concordance). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_cyclopaedia).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_chronicles). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_two_books). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_untitled). Initially Assert stacksRoom(hex_doors).
  Initially Assert stacksRoom(mirror_hex). Initially Assert stacksRoom(rotunda).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_first). Initially Assert planeRoom(balcony). Initially Assert planeRoom(spiral). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_bestiary).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_mapmaker). Initially Assert planeRoom(gallery_lamps). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_concordance). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_cyclopaedia).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_chronicles). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_two_books). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_untitled). Initially Assert planeRoom(hex_doors).
  Initially Assert planeRoom(mirror_hex). Initially Assert planeRoom(rotunda).
  Relation stacksRoom(place). Query inStacks(a: group) means at(a, ?p) and stacksRoom(?p).

  Passage order_hexagons "the Order of the Hexagons, behind the Catalogue" is path between reading_room and hex_first taking 15 minutes.
  Passage long_aisle "the aisle at the back of the Market that does not end" is path between remainder_market and hex_untitled taking 40 minutes.
  Passage to_balcony "the balcony" is doorway between hex_first and balcony.
  Passage to_spiral "the spiral stair in the vestibule" is path between hex_first and spiral taking 5 minutes.
  Passage spiral_up "the stair, up" is path between spiral and hex_bestiary taking 10 minutes.
  Passage spiral_down "the stair, down" is path between spiral and hex_untitled taking 10 minutes.
  Passage beings_maps "the gallery of plans" is path between hex_bestiary and hex_mapmaker taking 10 minutes.
  Passage first_lamps "the arch where the lamps begin" is path between hex_first and gallery_lamps taking 10 minutes.
  Passage lamps_concordance "the far end of the lamps" is path between gallery_lamps and hex_concordance taking 10 minutes.
  Passage lamps_cyclopaedia "a side gallery" is path between gallery_lamps and hex_cyclopaedia taking 10 minutes.
  Passage cyclopaedia_chronicles "the gallery of dates" is path between hex_cyclopaedia and hex_chronicles taking 10 minutes.
  Passage chronicles_two "the narrow hexagon beyond" is path between hex_chronicles and hex_two_books taking 10 minutes.
  Passage untitled_doors "a gallery of doors with no doors in them" is path between hex_untitled and hex_doors taking 20 minutes.
  Passage maps_doors "Fenwick's short way" is path between hex_mapmaker and hex_doors taking 10 minutes
    opening when knows(party, map_fixed) "Between two cases there is a gap that is on none of Fenwick's plans, and looks as if it would be, if the plans would stay still.".
  Passage doors_mirrors "the hexagon that shines" is path between hex_doors and mirror_hex taking 10 minutes.
  Passage mirrors_rotunda "the way on, among the mirrors" is path between mirror_hex and rotunda taking 10 minutes
    opening when knows(party, mirror_read) "Every way out of the Hexagon of Mirrors is a reflection of the way you came in.".
  // What is beyond, and closed: the illusion of depth, which in the Library is not an illusion.
  Passage sealed_ash "a stair going down, very hot, marked in iron: TO THE LIBRARY OF ASH" is path between hex_untitled and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The stair goes down into heat and a dry grey smell, and stops at an iron grille that has been riveted, not locked. Through it you can see more stair, and more, and a red glow, and hear, very far off, a great many voices saying one word each.".
  Passage sealed_tessaly "a gallery whose plaques all say TESSALY" is path between hex_chronicles and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The gallery is roped off with a cord of black silk. Every case in it is empty, and every case is labelled, in a careful hand, with the title of the book that is not there. TESSALY, A HISTORY. TESSALY, ITS LAWS. TESSALY, POEMS OF THE SPRING.".
  Passage sealed_same "a door with a brass plate: THE LIBRARY IN WHICH EVERY BOOK IS THE SAME BOOK" is path between hex_doors and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The door is ajar. Through the gap you can see a hexagon exactly like this one, and in it a hexagon exactly like that one, and on every shelf of all of them the same green book, and somebody, very far in, turning its pages, and weeping with happiness.".
  Passage sealed_reads "a gallery chained shut: CLOSED FOR RESHELVING SINCE 1104. THE BOOKS IN THIS GALLERY READ THEIR READERS" is path between hex_bestiary and sealed_stacks
    opening when stacksSealedForever(party) "The chain is new; the padlock is old. Beyond it the shelves lean inward, a little, all of them, as if listening.".
  Relation stacksSealedForever(group).

  // ── The law of the Stacks: what is written here does not stay written. ──
  Discovery stacks_laws "In the Stacks what is written does not stay written. A letter, a list, a book of your own, carried there for long, comes back saying something else. Only the Library's own ink holds: Calam-ink, and the ink of the Wellhead.".
  Relation written(item). Relation mutated(item). Relation stacksTime(group). Measure stacksSince(group).
  Initially Assert written(burning_register). Initially Assert written(jonquil_letter). Initially Assert written(effusions_stack). Initially Assert written(orme_pages).
  Initially Assert written(canto_lines).
  Rule stacks_entered when inStacks(party) and not stacksTime(party) { Assert stacksTime(party). Set stacksSince(party) to watch(clock). }
  Rule stacks_left when stacksTime(party) and not inStacks(party) { Retract stacksTime(party). }
  Rule words_drift when inStacks(party) and carries(party, ?i) and written(?i) and not mutated(?i) and watch(clock) >= stacksSince(party) + 12
    says "You look down at {?i}, and the words on it are not the words that were there. They are in the same hand. They are just as sure of themselves. They say something else." teaches stacks_laws {
    Assert mutated(?i). }
  Observe register_drifted at hex_first when mutated(burning_register) "Hester Rhule's register is in your hands, in her square clear hand, and the titles in it are titles of books that were never burned in Calamy, or never written: A Herbal of the Moon. The Sermons of the Fish. Moore's Almanack for the Year That Was Not.".
  Observe effusions_drifted at hex_first when mutated(effusions_stack) "The Effusions have changed in the Stacks. You read a page without meaning to, and then another. They are good. They are, in fact, very good. They have stopped asking to be burned.".

  // ── The First Hexagon. ──
  Observe hex_first_scene at hex_first when true "A hexagonal room, not large, lined on five of its six sides with shelves from floor to ceiling, twenty shelves to a side, and the books on them all the same height, all bound alike in plain leather, none with a title on its spine. The sixth side opens onto a narrow vestibule: on one hand a closet you could sleep standing up in, on the other a spiral stair that goes up and down out of sight, and between them a mirror that doubles the vestibule so faithfully you have to touch it to be sure. In the middle of the floor a low rail, and beyond the rail, nothing: a shaft of air with the same hexagon above it and below it, as far as you can see. The light is the light of the Reading Room, grown tired.".
  Thing guide "a small book chained at the vestibule, worn soft" at hex_first {
    State chained "A little book hangs on a chain at the mouth of the vestibule, worn soft as a glove by hands.".
  }
  Observe guide_read at hex_first of guide as reading when tried(guide, looking) "INSTRUCTIONS FOR THE READER ENTERING THE STACKS. Reader: you have come further than the Reading Room, which is not wise. Bring nothing written that you love; it will not come back as it went. Bring no pen; it will write what it likes. Sign nothing. Calam-ink and the ink of the Wellhead hold, and nothing else. On the spiral, count the steps aloud going down; the stair adds one for anyone who does not, and the one it adds goes somewhere else. In the Hexagon of Mirrors read nothing that faces you: turn your back and read over your shoulder, as you would read a thing written on your own back. Do not look for the centre. There is a theory that the Library has a centre, and a lectern at the centre, and on the lectern the book of which all the others are commentaries. Many readers have gone to look. The theory is older than the Library. A pencil note in the margin, in an educated hand: Nine weeks in, and I have not found the vestibule twice. A.F. Under it, in brown ink, newer: There is an Author. T.H." teaches stacks_laws.
  Discovery stair_count "On the spiral stair of the Stacks, count the steps aloud going down; the stair adds one for anyone who does not, and the one it adds goes somewhere else.".
  Discovery mirror_trick "In the Hexagon of Mirrors read nothing that faces you: turn your back and read over your shoulder.".
  Discovery centre_theory "There is a theory, older than the Library, that it has a centre, and at the centre a lectern, and on the lectern the book of which all the others are commentaries. Two readers have left notes: A.F., lost nine weeks; T.H., who is sure there is an Author.".
  Rule guide_stair when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, stair_count) says "You say the first rule over to yourself, so as to have it: on the spiral, count aloud going down." teaches stair_count { }
  Rule guide_mirrors when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, mirror_trick) says "And the second: in the mirrors, read over your shoulder." teaches mirror_trick { }
  Rule guide_centre when tried(guide, looking) and not knows(party, centre_theory) says "And the theory of the centre, which two readers have signed." teaches centre_theory { }
  Person ladder "the library ladder" at hex_first {
    Role "a library ladder on a brass rail, very old, which remembers every reader who has climbed it". Peaceable. Pronouns it. Manner compassionate.
    Greets "The ladder on its rail rolls a foot toward you, of its own accord, and its rungs creak in a way that is almost a word. 'Up?' it says. 'Or are you only looking? Most are only looking.'".
  }
  Topic ladder_readers with ladder "Ask the ladder who has climbed it lately" when true once {
    Says "'Lately,' says the ladder, considering, the way furniture considers. 'Two. A long time ago, or last week; it is the same here. A thin man in a Lyceum gown with a pencil behind his ear and a great many questions, who went up and down me forty times copying titles, and then went up the spiral and did not come back down it. Fenwick, he said, of the Lyceum, as if I would know. I did not know. I know now; he told me about himself for a long time.' Its rail creaks. 'And a heavy man with a binder's hands and a bone folder in his belt, who did not climb me at all, but stood here and said to the shelves, one after another, I know you are in there. Hask. He was looking for somebody. He went down.' A pause. 'Count the stair,' it adds. 'Nobody listens to the ladder.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, fenwick_seen). Assert knows(actor, hask_seen). Assert knows(actor, stair_count). }
  }
  Discovery fenwick_seen "A Lyceum scholar called Fenwick went up the spiral stair in the Stacks, a long time ago or last week, and did not come down.".
  Discovery hask_seen "A heavy man with a binder's hands and a bone folder, called Hask, came into the Stacks looking for somebody, and went down.".

  // The balcony over the shaft, and what can be heard down it.
  Observe balcony_scene at balcony when true "A balcony with a low brass rail, hanging over the air shaft. Above you, hexagon on hexagon, the same, going up until the light gives out; below, the same going down. Every so often something falls past, slowly, a sheet of paper turning over and over, and you never see it land. If you lean out and listen, there are voices at the bottom of the shaft, or what would be the bottom: a murmur, very far down, of a great many people reading aloud at once, and under that, further still, something like the sound a fire makes in a chimney." teaches shaft_heard.
  Discovery shaft_heard "Down the air shaft of the Stacks there is no bottom; but there are voices: a library reading itself aloud, and under it, further, something burning.".

  // ── The spiral, and the step it adds. ──
  Relation slipped(group).
  Observe spiral_scene at spiral when true "A stair of iron going round and round a shaft of its own, up and down out of sight, with a hexagon opening off it at every turn and none of them, quite, the one you expected. The steps are worn hollow in the middle. Somebody has scratched numbers on some of them, and then, it seems, other numbers.".
