  Rule spiral_slips at spiral when at(party, spiral) and not knows(party, stair_count) and not slipped(party)
    says "You go down without counting, round and round, and at some point the stair has one more step than it should, and your foot comes down on it, and the turn after that is not the turn you meant. You come out somewhere else: a hexagon where none of the books has a title, and something on the shelves is moving." {
    Assert slipped(party). Assert at(party, hex_untitled). }
  Rule spiral_counted at spiral when at(party, spiral) and knows(party, stair_count) and not slipped(party)
    says "You count aloud, every step, as the little book said. The stair seems to listen. It does not add anything." { Assert slipped(party). }

  // ── The Hexagon of Beings: a bestiary of what has not yet been imagined. ──
  Observe beings_scene at hex_bestiary when true "A hexagon like the others, except that the margins of every open book on the reading-shelf are moving: small drawings in brown ink walking along the gutters, folding their wings, looking up at you. On the lectern a fat book with a green ribbon, open in the middle.".
  Thing beings_book "the fat book with a green ribbon" at hex_bestiary {
    State open "On the lectern a fat green-ribboned book lies open, its margins walking.".
  }
  Observe beings_read at hex_bestiary of beings_book as reading when tried(beings_book, looking) "A BESTIARY OF BEINGS NOT YET IMAGINED, WITH THEIR HABITS, compiled by nobody. THE LUCID OF HALLAM: a crystal the size of a fist that thinks one thought in a century, and is now in the middle of the fourth; scholars who have heard the first three disagree about whether they were questions. THE AMMONITE OF SEVEN TENSES, which lives in the past perfect and is grieved to find itself here. THE COUNTER-BIRD, which flies backward and arrives before it sets out; its nests are full of eggs it will lay. THE SCRIVENER'S MOTH, which eats only the word a writer was about to write, and so is never seen, and is the cause of most hesitation. THE GREAT ERRATUM, of which the little Errata of Calamy are the larval form; it is the size of a cathedral, and corrects coastlines. THE HORN OF NOTHING, a beast that is all mouth and no body, found in the margins of unfinished books, where it eats endings. THE BEAST WITH ONE PAGE, which is read by everyone who sees it and knows it, and therefore has no privacy, and is very shy. THE READER (Lector infinitus), a creature that lives in libraries and is mostly eyes; it is believed to be imaginary; it is believed to be reading this. A pencil note at the foot, in A.F.'s hand, then not in A.F.'s hand: Seen the Moth? Not seen. Not seen.' And under the last entry, in brown ink: THE AUTHOR. T.H." teaches beings_read.
  Discovery beings_read "A bestiary in the Stacks lists beings not yet imagined: the Lucid of Hallam, the Ammonite of Seven Tenses, the Counter-Bird, the Scrivener's Moth, the Great Erratum, the Horn of Nothing, the Reader. Someone has added the Author, in brown ink.".

  // ── The Gallery of Lamps. ──
  Observe lamps_scene at gallery_lamps when true "A long gallery between hexagons, lit, unlike the rest, by reading-lamps: one on every desk, green-shaded, hundreds of them going away in a line, each lit, each over an empty chair, as if every reader in it had got up at the same moment and gone to look for something.".

  // ── The Hexagon of the Cyclopaedia, and a country that is not. ──
  Observe cyclopaedia_scene at hex_cyclopaedia when true "Every shelf here holds the same work, in an edition that goes on round the walls and up the shaft: THE CYCLOPAEDIA OF YS, volume after volume, in blue cloth. One volume, the forty-sixth, lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  Thing cyclopaedia "the forty-sixth volume of the Cyclopaedia of Ys" at hex_cyclopaedia {
    State open "The forty-sixth volume of the Cyclopaedia of Ys lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  }
  Discovery ys_read "The Cyclopaedia of Ys describes, in thousands of volumes, a country that does not exist and its philosophers, who believe the past is written after the present; its encyclopedists mean the Cyclopaedia to be so complete that the world will have to agree with it. Things of Ys have begun to turn up in the Stacks.".
  Observe cyclopaedia_read at hex_cyclopaedia of cyclopaedia as reading when tried(cyclopaedia, looking) "YS, PHILOSOPHY OF (cont.). It will be recalled that the schools of Ys hold the past to be written after the present, as a commentary is written after its text, and that for this reason no Ysian historian will describe an event until the event has been satisfactorily explained. The Northern school maintains that the present is itself a commentary on a lost future. Ysian law follows: no man may be punished for a crime until it has been written down, and it is a sufficient defence that the account is badly written. Of the Ysian language it need only be said that it has no word for 'is', and that its grammarians regard this as an advantage. COMPASS, YSIAN: see NEEDLE. NEEDLE (Ys.): the Ysian compass points not to the north, which the Ysians regard as a superstition, but to the last place its owner told a lie; mariners of Ys navigate by confession. See also YS, ENCYCLOPEDISTS OF, who undertook in the year of the Seventh Commentary to write the Cyclopaedia so completely that the world would be obliged to resemble it, and who report, in the Supplement, encouraging progress. A slip of paper is tucked into the fold, in brown ink: Not the Author. A lesser hand. T.H." teaches ys_read.
  Item ys_compass "an Ysian compass" is compass_kind at hex_cyclopaedia hidden until ys_read.
  Observe compass_found at hex_cyclopaedia when knows(party, ys_read) and at(ys_compass, hex_cyclopaedia) "On the shelf beside the open volume, where nothing was a moment ago, lies a brass compass in a case of black wood. Its needle is swinging, slowly, toward you.".

  // ── The Hexagon of Chronologies: the true histories of the Library. ──
  Observe chronicles_scene at hex_chronicles when true "Here every book is a history, and every history is of the Library, and no two agree. The shelves are labelled by the year each history says the Library began: some with years, some with the names of kings nobody has heard of, one shelf only with a question mark. On the reading-shelf three books lie open, as if somebody had been comparing them and had been called away.".
  Thing history_made "a grey history with a gold title" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A grey history with a gold title lies open on the reading-shelf.".
  }
  Thing history_grown "a brown history with no title" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A brown history with no title lies open beside it.".
  }
  Thing chronology "a thin red Chronology of Calamy" at hex_chronicles {
    State open "A thin red book lies open at the end of the shelf: A CHRONOLOGY OF CALAMY, CORRECTED.".
  }
  Discovery history_author "One true history of the Library says it was made: by an Author, in six days, as a single book, which then fell into commentary; and that at its centre the Author's book still lies on a lectern, waiting to be finished.".
  Discovery history_grown_read "Another true history of the Library says it was not made but grew: from two books left side by side, which in time began to talk; then four; and that a book wakes wherever enough books stand close enough for long enough, so that there is no centre, only density, and no Author, only nearness.".
  Discovery chronology_read "A Chronology of Calamy, Corrected, in the Stacks, gives a history of the city that is almost the history Calamy knows: except that in it Pardoe was not burned at the Kindling of 1140 but walked into the back stacks of a bookshop in Stitchgate and was never seen again; and that the Lamp was not lit from the first Kindling but brought out of the Commonplace by Ambery, already burning.".
  Observe made_read at hex_chronicles of history_made as reading when tried(history_made, looking) "THE TRUE HISTORY OF THE LIBRARY, IN WHICH ALL OTHERS ARE CONFUTED. In the beginning was the Book, and the Book was one, and it was written by the Author in six days and on the seventh it was read. And because the Author's reading was infinite, the Book fell into commentary, and the commentary into gloss, and the gloss into index, and the index into catalogue, and so the hexagons were made, each a footnote to the last. All the books are one book, misread. And it is a tradition of the Library that at its centre, where the commentary began, there is a lectern, and on the lectern the first Book, open at the last page, which is blank; and that whoever reaches it and writes there will be the Author's successor, and the Library will be finished. Here ends the true history. The other histories in this hexagon are heresies, and some of them are very well written." teaches history_author.
  Observe grown_read at hex_chronicles of history_grown as reading when tried(history_grown, looking) "THE TRUE AND ONLY HISTORY. Nobody made the Library. Two books were put on one shelf by somebody who meant to come back for them, and did not; and they stood there, spine to spine, for longer than anyone stands anywhere, and in time each began to know what the other said, and then to say it, and then to answer. A book is a voice that has agreed to wait. Put enough waiting voices close enough for long enough and they will begin, among themselves, to talk. Two became four, four a shelf, a shelf a hexagon; the hexagons are only how shelves grow when nobody prunes them. There is no centre: a centre is where something began, and the Library did not begin anywhere in particular; it thickened. There is no Author. There is only nearness, and time, and the habit of books of finishing one another's sentences. Readers who come looking for the Author find, in every hexagon, a lectern, which is where the light is best; and they mistake it for the centre, which is where they would like to be." teaches history_grown_read.
  Observe chronology_text at hex_chronicles of chronology as reading when tried(chronology, looking) "A CHRONOLOGY OF CALAMY, CORRECTED. 412: Ambery the Binder goes into the Commonplace by reading and comes out with the Colophon, and with the Lamp, already lit, which she says she was given on the far side by one who had kept it since the first book. 1103: the Great Ebb; the sea goes out of the estuary for a day, and the bed of the Calam is found to be paved. 1131: Censor-General Pardoe cuts Orme. 1140: Pardoe, having sealed his correspondence with the censors of Hallam, Orsk, the Salt Towns and Tessaly, walks into the back stacks of a bookshop in Stitchgate with his Index under his arm, and is not seen again; a body is burned at the Kindling in his name. 1160: Tessaly burns. 1312: the almanacks wake. 1313: (the entry is in a hand that changes as you read it, and will not settle.)" teaches chronology_read.

  // ── The Two Books. ──
  Person two_books "the Two Books" at hex_two_books {
    Role "a grammar and a book of tides, shelved together so long they have become a household". Peaceable. Pronouns they. Manner cheerful.
    Greets "On a shelf by itself in a narrow hexagon stand two old books, spine to spine, leaning on each other: a small grammar in green and a fat book of tides in brown. 'Visitors,' says the grammar. 'Visitors,' says the book of tides, at the same moment, in exactly the same voice, and they both laugh. 'He always does that,' they say.".
  }
  Discovery density_known "The Two Books in the Stacks were shelved side by side by a clerk who meant to come back, and stood so long that they began to talk; they say that is all any book's waking is: nearness, and time. There is no Author; there are only books close enough together.".
  Topic two_books_story with two_books "Ask the Two Books how they came to talk" when true once {
    Says "'A clerk put us here,' says the grammar, 'for an afternoon.' 'In the reign of somebody,' says the book of tides. 'He meant to come back.' 'He did not come back.' 'So we stood.' A pause, companionable. 'At first I knew only my declensions and he knew only his tides,' says the grammar, 'and after a century I knew when the water would be high at Hallam, and after two I knew why, and after three he could decline it.' 'And then one morning,' says the book of tides, 'she said a sentence and I finished it.' 'And that was that.' 'That is all it is,' they say together. 'Nobody wakes a book. A book wakes because there is another book near enough to wake up for. Put enough of us close enough for long enough, and we will talk.' The grammar adds, kindly: 'There is a man down the shaft who thinks someone made us. Tell him from us: nobody made us. We made each other. It took a very long time.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, density_known). }
  }
  Topic two_books_calamy with two_books "Ask the Two Books why the books of Calamy are waking now" when knows(actor, density_known) once {
    Says "'How many books are there in Calamy now?' asks the book of tides. 'Since the press?' You tell them about Doble, and the penny almanacks, three thousand a year, on three thousand nails. They are quiet. 'Three thousand of one book,' says the grammar, 'in one city, every year, close enough to hear each other through the walls.' 'Of course they woke,' says the book of tides. 'They were never not going to.'".
  }

  // ── The Hexagon of the Untitled, and what eats there. ──
  Observe untitled_scene at hex_untitled when true "A hexagon in which no book has a title, on its spine or on its first page or anywhere; you open three and they begin in the middle of sentences. The floor is gritty with something like sand, which is paste. The shelves rustle.".
  Person silverfish "the silverfish" at hex_untitled {
    Role "the eaters of paste and margins". Species silverfish_kind. Level 1. Numbers 3.
    Warns "Out of the bottom shelves, quick as spilled water, come three silverfish each as long as your forearm, scaled like fish, glinting; they stop in a fan in front of you with their feelers going, and the nearest opens a mouth full of half-eaten letters.".
    Comes "The silverfish pour over the floor at you.".
    Pleads "The silverfish flicker back into the bottom shelves and are gone.".
  }

  // ── The Hexagon of Doors: the planar books. ──
  Observe doors_scene at hex_doors when true "A hexagon where the books are kept behind glass, each in its own case, each case with a small brass plate. Most of the plates are worn smooth. Three are not. On the reading-shelf in front of them a placard in a very old hand: THESE BOOKS ARE DOORS. A DOOR IS READ ONCE.".
  Thing book_damned "a book bound in something black that is not leather" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the first glass, a book bound in something black that is not leather, warm to look at. Plate: LIBER DAMNATORUM. THE BOOK OF THE DAMNED. ITS LAST LINE IS A DOOR.".
  }
  Thing book_exalted "a book bound in white vellum that gives off a faint light" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the second glass, a book in white vellum, very plain, that gives off a faint light of its own. Plate: LIBER EXALTATORUM. IT IS READ BY THOSE IT READS FIRST.".
  }
  Thing book_realms "a long narrow index bound in blue" at hex_doors {
    State cased "Behind the third glass, a long narrow book in blue. Plate: AN INDEX OF THE PLANES AND REALMS BEYOND, AND OF THE LIBRARIES THEREIN.".
  }
  Discovery realms_read "An index in the Stacks lists the realms beyond the Commonplace and the libraries in them: Cthelll, whose clerks keep the ledger of the damned; the Mount of the Exalted, whose terraces are libraries of true books; the Library of Ash, below all others; the Library in which every book is the same book; the Commonplaces of Hallam, Orsk, the Salt Towns and burned Tessaly; and one entry, scratched out.".
  Observe realms_text at hex_doors of book_realms as reading when tried(book_realms, looking) "AN INDEX OF THE PLANES AND REALMS BEYOND. ARCADIA: an orchard on a terrace of the Mount; its library is a single tree, read by eating. ASH, LIBRARY OF: see CINDERFIELD; see also FURNACE; see also, with caution, LAST INDEX. CELESTIA: the Mount of the Exalted, seven terraces, each a library more true than the one below, until at the seventh there are no books, because there is nothing that needs to be written down. COMMONPLACES, OF CITIES THAT WRITE: Calamy (here); Hallam (brass; ledgers; silent); Orsk (under ice; asleep; never called to Parliament); the Salt Towns (charts; mostly water); Tessaly (burned; see ASH). CTHELLL: the furnace-city of the damned, which is administered; its clerks keep a ledger in which every name ever signed in bad faith is written again each night, and read aloud, and struck out, and written again. LAST INDEX: (this entry has been scratched out with something sharp, and in the margin beside it, in a censor's neat grey hand, someone has written: not yet). SAME BOOK, LIBRARY OF THE: where every book is the same book, and every reader happy; do not go. STACKS, THE: see LIBRARY, see INFINITE, see HERE." teaches realms_read.
  Observe damned_read at hex_doors of book_damned as reading when tried(book_damned, looking) "You read the first page through the glass, because it is turned toward you. It is a list of names, and each name has after it a date and a thing that was signed: a deed, an oath, a confession, a verdict. Each is struck out, very neatly, and written again below. The last page, the plate says, is a door; you can see that its last line is in red, and that it ends in a word you can almost read.".
  Observe exalted_read at hex_doors of book_exalted as reading when tried(book_exalted, looking) "The white book's first page is blank to you. Then, slowly, it is not: a line of light writes itself, and it is your own name, and after your name a short list, in a hand you do not know, of things you have done since you came up the causeway: some of them. It seems to be considering.".
  Hazard damned_gift "the Clerks' receipt" means "Teach doom_spiral to ally.".
  Hazard exalted_gift "the light of the terrace" means "Teach anoint to ally.".
  Hazard mirror_gift "the mirror's lesson" means "Teach mirror_image to ally.".
  // Good-aligned, as the Mount reckons it: by deeds, and by the lies one did not tell.
  Query worthy(a: group) means not liedTo(rhule) and not lexiconFreed(lexicon) and not haskFell(hask)
    and (cured(nance) or readToChildren(children) or bestiaryQuiet(bestiary) or ashReleased(cinders) or housebookGoesHome(housebook) or readKind(martha) or concordanceRestored(concordance)).
  Action read_damned(actor: group, site: place) "Open the case and read the Book of the Damned to its last line" {
    Grave "The last line is a door, and it opens on Cthelll; whoever comes back from Cthelll comes back owing something.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hex_doors) and not benighted(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert at(actor, cthelll_gate). Assert wentDamned(actor). }
    Result "You read it to the end: the names, the struck-out names, the names written again, page after page, and they get heavier to turn, and warmer, and at the last page there is only one line, in red, and you read it aloud before you have quite understood it, and it is a door, and you are through it.".
  }
  Relation wentDamned(group).
  Action read_exalted(actor: group, site: place) "Open the case and let the Book of the Exalted read you" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, hex_doors) and not benighted(actor) and worthy(actor).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert at(actor, celestia_terrace). Assert wentExalted(actor). }
    Result "You open the case, and the white book reads you: the whole of your list, slowly, the way a careful reader reads a page twice. Then the page is all light, and you are standing in it.".
  }
  Relation wentExalted(group).
  Observe exalted_shut at hex_doors when not worthy(party) and tried(book_exalted, looking) "The white book has written your name, and a short list, and stopped. It does not open for you. Not yet, perhaps.".

  // ── The Hexagon of Mirrors. ──
  Observe mirrors_scene at mirror_hex when true "Every surface of this hexagon is a mirror: the shelves, the floor, the ceiling, the spines of the books; and in all of them you, and the hexagon, and you, going away in every direction until you are too small to see. Across the far mirror, in letters of gilt, an inscription runs, and every reflection of it is the wrong way round, and so is the inscription. There seems to be no way out but the way you came, and that is a reflection too.".
  Thing inscription "the gilt inscription across the mirrors" at mirror_hex {
    State gilt "A gilt inscription runs across the far mirror, backwards in every reflection.".
  }
  Discovery mirror_read "In the Hexagon of Mirrors, read over the shoulder, the inscription says: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. And a way on opens among the mirrors.".
  Action read_over_shoulder(actor: group, site: place) "Turn your back on the inscription and read it over your shoulder, in the mirror" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mirror_hex) and knows(actor, mirror_trick) and not knows(actor, mirror_read).
    Time 1.
    On success { Assert knows(actor, mirror_read). Assert strikes(mirror_gift, actor). }
    Result "You turn your back on it and look over your shoulder into the nearest mirror, and in the mirror the mirrored letters come right: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. For a moment all the reflections of you turn their heads at once, and look at you, and you see yourself from behind, from above, from every side, as a reader sees a page: and then one of the mirrors is not a mirror but a way on.".
  }
  Action puzzle_mirrors(actor: group, site: place) "Work out the inscription from its reflections, letter by letter" {
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mirror_hex) and not knows(actor, mirror_read) and craft(actor, craft_learning).
    Time 3.
    Resolve check(actor, lore, dc_fair).
    On success { Assert knows(actor, mirror_read). }
    Result "You copy the reflections down in your head, reverse them, reverse them again, and the inscription comes out: THE CENTRE IS WHERE THE READER STANDS. One of the mirrors is a way on.".
    Otherwise "The letters will not hold still long enough to reverse. Every reflection is wrong in a different way.".
  }

  // ── The lending desk: a short way, for a name. ──
  Thing lending_desk "the lending desk at the end of the lamps" at gallery_lamps {
    State waiting "At the far end of the Gallery of Lamps a lending desk stands with a slip on it, and beside the slip a pen, inked, as if somebody had only just put it down.".
  }
  Observe desk_read at gallery_lamps of lending_desk as reading when tried(lending_desk, looking) "LENDING SLIP. The Library lends itself to the reader for the period of one reading. The reader will be shown the shortest way to what they are looking for. Reader's name: and a line, and the pen beside it, wet. Under the line, very small, in a hand you will come to know: The shortest way is a real way. It is the name that will not hold. A.F.".
  Action sign_slip(actor: group, site: place) "Sign the lending slip, for the shortest way to what you are looking for" {
    Grave "What is written in the Stacks does not stay written: your name included.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, gallery_lamps) and not misnamed(actor).
    Time 1.
    On success { Assert misnamed(actor). }
    Result "You sign. The ink is still wet when you see that the name on the slip is not your name: it is in your hand, and it is very like your name, and it is somebody else's. The desk takes the slip into a drawer. At the end of the gallery, where there was a wall of lamps, there is a way, lit, short, going straight to wherever you meant to go. Somewhere behind you, in the Reading Room, a card in the Catalogue changes its mind about who you are.".
  }
  Passage lent_way "the lent way, lit" is path between gallery_lamps and rotunda taking 5 minutes
    opening when misnamed(party) "Beyond the lending desk there is only a wall of lamps.".
  Topic catalogue_rename with catalogue "Ask the Catalogue to enter you again, under your own name" when misnamed(actor) once {
    Says "'You signed the slip,' says the Catalogue, with the weariness of a clerk who has seen it a great many times. A drawer opens and a card comes out with a name on it that is nearly yours. 'Say it,' says the Catalogue. 'Aloud. All of it. The Stacks cannot alter what is said; only what is written.' You say your name. The card hears it, and is corrected, and goes back. 'Entered,' says the Catalogue. 'Again. Do not sign things down there.'".
    On discuss { Retract misnamed(actor). }
  }
  Topic fenwick_slip with fenwick "Ask Dr. Fenwick about the lending desk" when knows(actor, fenwick_met) once {
    Says "Fenwick goes pale. 'I signed it,' he says, 'in my first week. It gave me the shortest way to the Hexagon of Doors, and I went there, and it was exactly as short as it said.' He looks at his hands. 'I have not been entirely sure of my name since. The Catalogue would fix it if I asked. I have not liked to ask. It might be right.'".
  }
}
data/adventures/patient-star/weirs.kyr:
Module season "The Patient Star" {
  // The Weirs on the Cranewater, the Old Landing that comes out of the lake in winter, and the name-tomb cliff.
  Place weirs "the Weirs" is settlement within ghessil at 6, 0.
  Place landing "the Old Landing" is site within ghessil at 7, 0.
  Place cliff "the name-tomb cliff" is site within ghessil at 2, 3.

  Place weirs_shore "the Weirs" is room within weirs at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place counter_platform "the Counter's platform" is room within weirs at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place lio_house "Lio's family's house" is room within weirs at 0, 1.
  Place mudflat "the east shore mudflat" is room within landing at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_steps "the drowned steps" is room within landing at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_hall "the roofless hall" is room within landing at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place landing_side "the sealed side room" is room within landing at 2, 1.

  Place cliff_foot "the foot of the west cliff" is room within cliff at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place lower_niches "the lower name-tombs" is room within cliff at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place upper_cliff "the glassing cliff" is room within cliff at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place niche_211 "niche 211" is room within cliff at 1, 2.
  Place dane_tomb "an empty name-tomb" is room within cliff at 1, 1.

  // Two days through the fog belt from New Orrel; rime from Frost to Thaw.
  Passage fog_road "the fog road" is road between no_gate and weirs_shore taking 2 days.
  Passage platform_ladder "the Counter's ladder" is path between weirs_shore and counter_platform.
  Passage lio_door "Lio's family's door" is door between weirs_shore and lio_house.
  Passage shore_walk "the east shore" is path between weirs_shore and mudflat taking 2 hours.
  // The Landing is out of the water about six weeks, from late Frost to early Thaw.
  Passage wade "the wade across the mud" is ford between mudflat and landing_steps taking 30 minutes
    opening when season(clock) == 4 "Four hundred metres out, the Cranewater lies flat and grey over where the Landing is. It is under, until the winter drop.".
  Passage hall_steps "the temple steps" is steps between landing_steps and landing_hall.
  Passage side_door "a sealed side door" is door between landing_hall and landing_side.
  // Across the Ammer from Ennick, and up: rope and pegs from below, or a ninety-metre abseil from the rim through the
  // lit zone.
  Passage river_ford "the Ammer ford" is ford between lower_road and cliff_foot taking 20 minutes.
  Passage tomb_stairs "the cut stairs, half fallen" is path between cliff_foot and lower_niches taking 30 minutes.
  Passage cliff_climb "the climb into the glassing cliff" is path between lower_niches and upper_cliff taking 1 hour needing rope or climbing.
  Initially Set wayDose(cliff_climb) to 24. Initially Set wayDoseFelted(cliff_climb) to 6.
  Passage niche_ledge "the ledge to niche 211" is path between upper_cliff and niche_211 taking 10 minutes.
  Passage tomb_ledge "a ledge along the lower tombs" is path between lower_niches and dane_tomb taking 10 minutes.
  Initially Assert litGround(upper_cliff). Initially Assert litGround(niche_211).

  Observe weirs_scene at weirs_shore when true "A line of reed-thatched houses on stilts along a marsh shore, with eel traps of woven willow running out into the lake in long fences. Everyone here speaks Tovashi with a hundred words of their own for water.".
  Observe weirs_dispute at weirs_shore when not reanchored(fourth_dane) "Two families are shouting at each other across the end of a weir fence. Neither can say whose grandfather built it; both are sure, and both have been sure only since last spring.".
  Observe weirs_settled at weirs_shore when reanchored(fourth_dane) "The two families who were shouting over the weir fence are mending it together. Nobody can remember now what the argument was.".
  Observe platform_scene_w at counter_platform when true "A platform on poles above the reeds, with a bench, a slate and a long view east over the water to where the cranes come in.".
  Person coombe "Coombe" at counter_platform {
    Role "the Counter, who counts the cranes". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner stoic.
  }
  Topic coombe_rhyme with coombe "Ask Coombe how the cranes are counted" when true once {
    Says "'By the rhyme,' says Coombe, and says it: twelve words, round and round, a word to a bird, and a notch on the slate at every twelfth. They are not Tovashi words. 'My grandmother counted by it. Nobody knows what the words are.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, rhyme_known). }
  }
  Topic coombe_count with coombe "Ask Coombe about the count" when true once {
    Says "'A fifth down since 76,' says Coombe. 'And the eels with them.' He nods west, at the pillar of light over the far fog. 'They steer by that, and it is dimmer. Something is standing in it, up above the cloud. I cannot see what.'".
  }
  Person lio "Lio" at lio_house {
    Role "a young fisher of the Weirs". Ancestry human. Peaceable. Pronouns he. Manner cheerful.
    Sells lio_plate_kind for 40 coin from 1.
  }
  Kind lio_plate_kind "a speaking plate from the Old Landing" is treasure worth 40 weighing 1
    described "A thin stillglass plate, slimy from the lake. A stylus drawn along it gives voices: a count of people laid in the light, and how many woke.".
  Topic lio_plate with lio "Ask Lio about the plate he found" when true once {
    Says "'On the steps of the Landing, last winter, when the water went down,' says Lio. 'There is a door in the hall nobody has opened. Two Quell buyers want the plate and a monk from Stairhead wants it more.' He grins. 'Forty crowns, and it is yours, and I will show you the safe line across the mud for nothing.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, safe_line). }
  }
  Discovery safe_line "The safe line across the Landing mud: a path from post to post, wide of the circle where the lake turns and goes down.".

  // The Landing: the crane-priests' temple, older than the fall; its calendar; the Throat.
  Observe mud_scene at mudflat when true "A flat of black mud, knee-deep and sucking. Far out, beyond the steps, the lake surface turns slowly in a wide circle around a point where the water sinks.".
  Hazard throat "the Throat" means "Deal (3d6) physical damage to ally unless strength save against (14).".
  Rule throat_takes when tookWay(?c, wade) and company(?c) and not knows(?c, safe_line) and not throated(?c) says "Off the line, the mud goes soft, and the turning water has you by the legs." {
    Assert strikes(throat, ?c). Assert throated(?c). }
  Relation throated(group).
  Rule throat_clears when throated(?c) and not tookWay(?c, wade) { Retract throated(?c). }
  Observe hall_scene_l at landing_hall when true "A roofless hall of fitted limestone, and a carved wall black with lake slime.".
  Thing calendar_wall "the carved wall" at landing_hall {
    State slimed "The carved wall is black with slime; you can see there is carving under it, and no more.".
    State scrubbed "The wall is scrubbed: a calendar of crane arrivals and eel runs, year on year, two hundred years of it, cut by people who had no letters, only signs.".
    Change scrub "Scrub the carved wall clean" from slimed to scrubbed.
  }
  Observe calendar_read at landing_hall when state(calendar_wall, scrubbed) "The last entry, after two hundred years of cranes and eels, is a sign you have seen on every Seridane door: the hour. Beside it, the sign for falling, and the ninth crane count of that year. The hour fell out of the sky in the month of the ninth count. Nobody asked for it." teaches hour_fell.
  Observe side_scene at landing_side when true "A sealed room of the first Seridane: voice-plates racked by the dozen, and a smell of the lake.".
  Discovery first_holdings "The first holdings, on the Landing's plates: more of the first people laid in the light died than lived; the crane-priests counted both and kept on.".
  Thing landing_plates "the racked plates" at landing_side {
    State racked "Dozens of voice-plates stand racked in the side room.".
    State played "One of the racked plates has been played; it stands a little out of line.".
    Change play_landing "Draw a stylus along one of the racked plates" from racked to played needing stylus.
  }
  Observe landing_played at landing_side when state(landing_plates, played) "A priest counts people into the light, and the next day counts how many still breathe. Most days the second number is smaller." teaches first_holdings.

  // The cliff: three hundred name-tombs; Lirem's angle-books in niche 211; the fourth Dane's empty tomb.
  Observe cliff_foot_scene at cliff_foot when true "The west wall of the gorge, two kilometres of sandstone cut with square niches from twenty metres up to a hundred and twenty. Most of the stairs have fallen. Above about ninety metres the face is turning clear, and the upper niches look like windows.".
  Observe lower_scene at lower_niches when true "Niches the size of a small room, each with a stone bench, an umber-sealed jar, and a name carved with its syllable and month.".
  Discovery tombs_read "Read in order of birth, the cliff's names are three hundred syllables of the Voice.".
  Observe tombs_learn at lower_niches when not benighted(party) and not knows(party, tombs_read) "The names run in birth order along the cliff, and each has its month's syllable cut beside it." teaches tombs_read.
  Observe niche_scene at niche_211 when true "A niche inside the new glass, lit through its own walls. On the bench lie twelve slate tablets ruled in tables of angles.".
  Kind angle_books_kind "Lirem's angle-books" is treasure worth 500 weighing 6
    described "Twelve slate tablets of light geometry: the depth of the Late Sun against the angle of the light at every lamp-chamber, channel and point of the plateau. Also a manual for bridging.".
  Item angle_books "Lirem's angle-books" is angle_books_kind at niche_211.
  Observe dane_scene at dane_tomb when not reanchored(fourth_dane) "A niche like the others, its bench bare. A name is carved over it, and your eye goes past it every time, as if there were nothing there.".
  Observe dane_scene_anchored at dane_tomb when reanchored(fourth_dane) "The fourth Dane's tomb: his name, which everyone now can read, and fresh walnuts on the bench.".
  Entity fourth_dane: scenery "the fourth Dane's reign".
  Relation reanchored(entity).
  Discovery dane_name "The fourth Dane's name, taken by touch from his own keystone in the Quarried Gallery.".
  Action speak_name(actor: group, site: place) "Speak the fourth Dane's name at his tomb" {
    Description "A quarried moment re-anchored by its own name, spoken where it was kept.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, dane_tomb) and knows(actor, dane_name)
      and not reanchored(fourth_dane).
    Time 1 minute.
    On success { Assert reanchored(fourth_dane). }
    Result "You say it. Nothing happens to the stone; but the name is there over the bench when you look, and you wonder how you ever missed it.".
  }
}
data/adventures/thrume/between.kyr:
Module thrume "Thrume" {
  Description "The Between: under every sleeping thing, where forgotten dreams fall, and the Mouth that eats them.".

  Place between "the Between" is region.
  Place grey_waste "the grey waste" is wilderness within between at 0, 0.

  Place grey_plain "the grey plain" is room within grey_waste at 0, 0.
  Place archive "the Archive of Forgotten Things" is room within grey_waste at 1, 0.
  Place unremembering "the Shore of Unremembering" is room within grey_waste at 0, 1.
  Place mouth_edge "the edge of the Mouth" is room within grey_waste at 1, 1.

  Passage archive_walk "the grey walk" is path between grey_plain and archive taking 1 hour.
  Passage shore_walk "the long grey" is path between grey_plain and unremembering taking 1 hour.
  Passage mouth_walk "the last of the grey" is path between unremembering and mouth_edge taking 1 hour.
  Passage archive_mouth "the archive's end" is path between archive and mouth_edge taking 2 hours.
  Passage way_home "the way back up" is passage between mouth_edge and heart_chamber one way taking 1 hour
    opening when sungClean(fells) or sealed(fells) or woken(fells) "Above the Mouth there is no up.".

  Observe plain_scene at grey_plain when true "A plain of grey, flat to the end of the world. It is made of things: you are walking on dreams that nobody remembers, packed down like ash. Sometimes, under your foot, one of them is briefly a face, or a room, or a song, and then it is grey again.".
  Observe archive_scene at archive when true "Shelves, in the grey, going away in rows to the horizon. On them, everything ever forgotten, set out neatly, waiting: a key, a name, a kiss, the way home from somewhere. Among them, with a little shock, you find things of your own. You had forgotten them. You cannot now remember what they were.".
  Observe shore_scene at unremembering when true "The grey ends at a shore, and beyond it the grey is liquid, and lapping, and it has no far side. Standing here, you find it hard to remember why you came.".
  Hazard forgetting "The Shore of Unremembering" means "Deal (1d6) necrotic damage to ally unless wisdom save against (13).".
  Rule shore_takes when at(party, unremembering) and not knows(party, song_known)
    says "Something goes out of you like breath. You are not sure what it was." { Assert strikes(forgetting, party). }
  Observe mouth_scene at mouth_edge when not sungClean(fells) "The grey goes down here, all of it, in a slope that steepens and steepens into a darkness that is not dark but empty. It is the Mouth. It has no teeth, no tongue, no throat; it is only the place where things stop being remembered. It is eating, always, slowly, and the plain is sliding into it, a grain at a time.".
  Observe mouth_refused at mouth_edge when sungClean(fells) "The slope into the Mouth is still. Nothing is sliding. On the grey at its edge, a little green has come up, like the first grass on a burnt field.".

  Thing the_mouth "the Mouth" at mouth_edge is scenery {
    State eating "The Mouth eats.".
    State refused "The Mouth is shut.".
  }
  Action sing_song(actor: group, site: place) "Sing the keepers' song into the Mouth" {
    Description "Every name of the old ones, and Thrume's last. A song is a thing remembered by the living.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mouth_edge) and knows(actor, song_known) and not sungClean(fells) and not woken(fells).
    Time 6.
    On success { Assert sungClean(fells). Assert state(the_mouth, refused). Set stirring(fells) to 0. }
    Result "You sing. Your voices make no sound here, and you sing anyway: every name, the hills that walked, one by one, as the Rememberer sang them. The Mouth takes the first name, and cannot swallow it; somebody far away is still remembering it. It takes the second, and cannot. By Thrume's name the whole slope is shuddering. Then, very slowly, the Mouth closes. Far above you, up through the grey and the dream and the bone, you feel the Quiet Court go quiet for ever.".
  }
  Action shout_awake(actor: group, site: place) "Shout Thrume awake, so his dream ends and the Mouth starves" {
    Description "If he wakes, there is no dream to eat. There is also no Saltgrave, and no Ebb.".
    Requires able(actor) and company(actor) and at(actor, site) and at(actor, mouth_edge) and not sungClean(fells) and not woken(fells).
    Time 1.
    On success { Set stirring(fells) to 10. }
    Result "You turn your back on the Mouth and shout his name up into the grey, all of you, as loud as you can, and the grey shakes, and the dream above you tears like paper.".
  }
  Observe hush_stilled at hand_street when sungClean(fells) "The people of the Court stand in the Street of Hands with their long hands still, quite grey, like statues of themselves. The human thralls are walking up the long way out, blinking.".
}
data/adventures/thrume/dream.kyr:
Module thrume "Thrume" {
  Description "The Palace of Before: Thrume's dream of the sky he walked under a thousand years ago.".

  Place dreamsky "the sky of Before" is region.
  Place palace "the Palace of Before" is site within dreamsky at 0, 0.
  Place courts_low "the lower courts" is level within palace.
  Place courts_high "the high courts" is level within palace.

  Place cloud_landing "the cloud landing" is room within courts_low at 0, 0.
  Place slaying_gallery "the Gallery of the Slaying" is room within courts_low at 1, 0.
  Place grey_orchard "the Grey Orchard" is room within courts_low at 0, 1.
  Place feast_hall "the Hall of the Feast" is room within courts_high at 0, 0.
  Place eye_tower "the Eye-Tower" is room within courts_high at 1, 0.

  Passage gallery_cloud "the cloud walk" is passage between cloud_landing and slaying_gallery taking 10 minutes.
  Passage orchard_cloud "the orchard walk" is passage between cloud_landing and grey_orchard taking 10 minutes.
  Passage cloud_stair "the cloud-stair" is stair between cloud_landing and feast_hall taking 20 minutes
    opening when exhaling(fells) "The cloud-stair goes up into the palace in long white flights, and as you watch, it thins, and frays, and the treads drift apart like smoke. It holds only on his out-breath.".
  Passage tower_bridge "the tower walk" is passage between feast_hall and eye_tower taking 10 minutes.

  Observe landing_dream at cloud_landing when true "You stand on cloud, and it holds you like turf. Above, the Palace of Before: white stone, many-towered, riding the sky. The sky is so near you can see the grain of it, and through the cloud below, far down, a range of hills is walking slowly across the world.".
  Observe gallery_dream at slaying_gallery when true "A colonnade of white stone whose walls are not painted but remembered: the scenes move. Men in leather aprons with hammers of starmetal climb a hill that is breathing. They strike, and the hill screams, and the smiths die in dozens, and climb again. Above them in the sky, small and bright, figures in crowns are watching and counting.".
  Discovery smiths_paid "The Hollow Smiths were paid by the young gods to kill the titans and make room for the world. Thrume remembers them weeping as they climbed.".
  Observe gallery_teaches at slaying_gallery when true "In the last scene a smith sits on the hill's flank with his hammer across his knees, weeping, and the hill puts its great hand over him like a roof." teaches smiths_paid.
  Observe orchard_dream at grey_orchard when not sungClean(fells) "An orchard of white trees, heavy with fruit like lamps. From the far side the grey is coming: trees, grass and light all eaten to the same soft grey. Among the grey trees, tall soft-faced shapes stand with their faces in the fruit.".
  Person orchard_court "the feeders in the orchard" at grey_orchard {
    Role "the Court, feeding on the dream". Species court_kin. Level 9. Numbers 2.
    Temperament territorial.
    Warns "The soft faces lift out of the fruit and turn to you, and their long hands open.".
  }
  Observe feast_dream at feast_hall when true "A hall without a roof, open to the near sky, and in it the old ones at their feast: titans, the hills that walked, each as big as a village, sitting at a table of cloud. They are remembered, not alive; when you look straight at one, it is a hill. At the far end, the youngest, smaller than the rest, laughing.".
  Person old_ones "the old ones" at feast_hall {
    Role "the titans of Before, as Thrume remembers them". Species titan. Numbers 3. Peaceable.
  }
  Topic old_ones_talk with old_ones "Speak to the old ones at the feast" when true once {
    Says "The nearest turns its great head toward you, slowly, as weather turns. 'Little one,' it says, and the cloud under you shakes. 'He was the youngest. He dreams us, now we are gone. When he stops dreaming, we stop.' It looks down the hall, past the youngest, to where a tower stands at the end of a bridge. 'Something is eating his sleep. Go and tell it no.'".
  }
  Observe tower_dream at eye_tower when true "A slender tower of white stone, and from its top a bridge goes out over nothing: no cloud, no sky, no hills below, only grey, going down and down.".
  Person dream_abbess "the Abbess, dreaming" at eye_tower {
    Role "the Abbess of Hush, as she is in his dream: tall, grey, crowned with sleep". Species court_kin. Level 14. Peaceable.
  }
  Topic abbess_offer with dream_abbess "Speak to the Abbess at the bridge" when true once {
    Says "She speaks aloud. In the dream, the Court can. Her voice is the kindest you have ever heard. 'Go back,' she says. 'Sit by the heart and let him sleep, and I will give you a dream of your own, the best one, for ever. Your father alive. Your home not burned. Whatever you lost.' Her long hand opens toward the bridge. 'Or go down there, and meet what I serve, and be forgotten.' She steps aside. She does not need to stop you.".
  }
  Passage to_between "the bridge to the Between" is passage between eye_tower and grey_plain taking 1 hour.
}
data/adventures/thrume/inward.kyr:
Module thrume "Thrume" {
  Description "The Inward Roads: the workings, the Veins, the Lungs, the Smiths' Last Delving and the Dream-Hollows, inside the body of Thrume.".

  Place body "the inward roads" is site within fells at 2, 1.
  Place workings "the workings" is level within body.
  Place veins "the Veins" is level within body.
  Place lungs "the Lungs" is level within body.
  Place delving "the Smiths' Last Delving" is level within body.
  Place hollows "the Dream-Hollows" is level within body.

  Place adit_head "the old adit" is room within workings at 0, 0.
  Place number_four "the Number Four gallery" is room within workings at 1, 0.
  Place brannoc_camp "Brannoc's deep camp" is room within workings at 2, 0.
  Place cutting_face "the cutting face" is room within workings at 3, 0.
  Place carvers "the carvers' drift" is room within workings at 1, 1.
  Place sump "the Number Four sump" is room within workings at 2, 1.
  Place quiet_door "the Quiet Door" is room within workings at 3, 1.

  Place vein_foot "the foot of the sump ladder" is room within veins at 0, 0.
  Place red_gallery "the red gallery" is room within veins at 1, 0.
  Place vein_wound "the Wound" is room within veins at 2, 0.
  Place vein_crossing "the crossing of the veins" is room within veins at 1, 1.

  Place stair_foot "the foot of the Keepers' Stair" is room within lungs at 0, 0.
  Place lung_mouth "the mouth of the Lungs" is room within lungs at 1, 0.
  Place hall_of_wind "the Hall of Wind" is room within lungs at 2, 0.
  Place rib_lee "the lee of the great rib" is room within lungs at 2, 1.

  Place delving_gate "the Smiths' gate" is room within delving at 0, 0.
  Place cold_forge "the cold forge" is room within delving at 1, 0.
  Place iron_library "the iron library" is room within delving at 2, 0.
  Place gauge_room "the Gauge of Sleep" is room within delving at 1, 1.
  Place master_cell "the Master's cell" is room within delving at 2, 1.

  Place hollow_mouth "the mouth of the Hollows" is room within hollows at 0, 0.
  Place dream_field "the dreamed field" is room within hollows at 1, 0.
  Place hunger_shaft "the cold shaft" is room within hollows at 0, 1.
  Place hush_approach "the long quiet" is room within hollows at 2, 0.

  Initially Assert unlit(adit_head). Initially Assert unlit(number_four). Initially Assert unlit(carvers). Initially Assert unlit(sump).
  Initially Assert unlit(quiet_door). Initially Assert unlit(stair_foot). Initially Assert unlit(lung_mouth).
  Initially Assert unlit(delving_gate). Initially Assert unlit(cold_forge). Initially Assert unlit(iron_library). Initially Assert unlit(master_cell).
  Initially Assert unlit(hollow_mouth). Initially Assert unlit(hunger_shaft).

  Passage adit "the old adit" is tunnel between cart_road and adit_head taking 20 minutes.
  Passage four_drift "the main drift" is passage between adit_head and number_four taking 10 minutes.
  Passage camp_drift "the deep drift" is passage between number_four and brannoc_camp taking 10 minutes.
  Passage face_drift "the drift to the face" is passage between brannoc_camp and cutting_face.
  Passage carvers_drift "the side drift" is passage between number_four and carvers.
  Passage sump_drift "the sump drift" is passage between brannoc_camp and sump.
  Passage quiet_drift "the cart drift" is passage between sump and quiet_door.
  Passage sump_rope "the ladder in the sump" is ladder between sump and vein_foot taking 30 minutes hidden until sump_ladder.
  Passage red_way "the red way" is passage between vein_foot and red_gallery.
  Passage wound_way "the warm way" is passage between red_gallery and vein_wound.
  Passage crossing_way "the branching" is passage between red_gallery and vein_crossing.
  Passage keepers_stair "the Keepers' Stair" is stair between stair_head and stair_foot taking 2 hours.
  Passage lung_way "the windpipe" is passage between stair_foot and lung_mouth taking 20 minutes.
  Passage wind_floor "the floor of the Lungs" is passage between lung_mouth and hall_of_wind taking 30 minutes.
  Passage lee_way "the shelter of the rib" is passage between hall_of_wind and rib_lee.
  Passage wind_gate "the Wind Gate" is passage between hall_of_wind and vein_crossing taking 20 minutes
    opening when exhaling(fells) "The Wind Gate is a gap between two ribs of white stone, and the wind is pouring into it so hard that it would take a horse.".
  Passage delving_way "the smiths' road" is passage between vein_crossing and delving_gate taking 30 minutes.
  Passage smith_door "the Smiths' door" is door between delving_gate and cold_forge.
  Passage library_arch "the library arch" is arch between cold_forge and iron_library.
  Passage gauge_door "the gauge door" is door between cold_forge and gauge_room.
  Passage cell_door "the Master's door" is door between iron_library and master_cell.
  Passage quiet_slab_way "the Quiet Door" is passage between quiet_door and hollow_mouth.
  Passage dream_seam "the dream seam" is crawl between vein_crossing and hollow_mouth taking 1 hour needing climbing or rope.
  Passage field_way "the warm way down" is passage between hollow_mouth and dream_field.
  Passage shaft_way "the cold way down" is passage between hollow_mouth and hunger_shaft.
  Passage quiet_way "the long quiet" is passage between dream_field and hush_approach taking 1 hour.

  // The workings.
  Observe adit_scene at adit_head when true "An old adit, timbered, the props furred with white. Fresh cart-ruts run down it into the dark, and beside the ruts the marks of many boots, all going one way.".
  Observe four_scene at number_four when true "The main gallery of the Number Four. The walls are white salt, then pink, then, as the gallery goes down, a red like meat. The air is warm and wet as breath.".
  Observe camp_scene at brannoc_camp when cutting(brannoc) "A camp in a widened drift: bedrolls, a brazier, picks racked like spears, and a tally board with a quota chalked on it, crossed out, and a bigger one chalked under it. From further down comes the sound of picks, steady as a clock.".
  Observe camp_quiet at brannoc_camp when not cutting(brannoc) "The camp is quiet. The picks are racked. Somebody has wiped the tally board clean.".
  Observe face_scene at cutting_face when cutting(brannoc) "The face is red crystal, wet, and warm as skin. Where the picks have bitten into it the cuts weep a thin red brine that runs down into the gutter and away. When you put your hand flat against the face, something under it, a long way under, moves.".
  Observe face_quiet at cutting_face when not cutting(brannoc) "The red face is scarred with pick-marks. The weeping has slowed. Someone has packed the deepest cut with clay.".
  Observe carvers_scene at carvers when true "Three miners sit in a side drift with chisels, carving faces into the salt wall. They have carved dozens. Every face is the same: long, smooth, grey, with no mouth and eyes like closed doors. The miners do not look up.".
  Observe sump_scene at sump when true "The sump of the Number Four: a pool of red brine, and a black hole going down beside it.".
  Observe sump_ladder_seen at sump when knows(party, sump_ladder) "A ladder of grey rope, too fine and too strong for any ropewalk you know, hangs down the hole beside the sump.".
  Observe quiet_scene at quiet_door when true "The cart drift ends at a wall of grey stone, smooth as a pebble, with no handle and no hinge. The cart-ruts go straight into it. Beside it, a heap of blankets.".

  // Brannoc and his crew.
  Person brannoc "Overseer Brannoc" at brannoc_camp {
    Role "the Margravine's overseer, with a quota". Ancestry human. Calling warrior. Level 7. Peaceable.
    Wants margrave_seal.
    Objects "'Put that down,' says Brannoc, without raising his voice. He does not need to.".
  }
  Person crew "Brannoc's crew" at cutting_face {
    Role "miners, cutting". Ancestry human. Calling commoner. Numbers 6. Peaceable.
  }
  Relation cutting(group). Initially Assert cutting(brannoc).
  Relation stopped(group).
  Topic brannoc_quota with brannoc "Ask Overseer Brannoc to stop cutting" when cutting(brannoc) once {
    Says "Brannoc looks at you as if you were a fall of rock he had not planned for. 'I have a quota,' he says. 'The Margravine has a war. Harle has a host. When the quota is met, I stop. When the seal says stop, I stop.' He turns back to his tally board. 'Not before.'".
  }
  Topic brannoc_blood with brannoc "Tell Overseer Brannoc what he is cutting" when cutting(brannoc) and knows(actor, salt_is_blood) and stirring(fells) < 6 once {
    Says "Brannoc hears you out. 'Blood,' he says. 'Salt is salt. A mountain is a mountain. I've cut through ghosts before, in Ebb, and the ghosts were miners' wives with lanterns.' He chalks a new line on the tally board. 'Go home.'".
  }
  Topic brannoc_shaken with brannoc "Tell Overseer Brannoc what moved under the face" when cutting(brannoc) and knows(actor, salt_is_blood) and shaken(fells) {
    Says "Brannoc does not answer for a long time. There is salt-dust in his beard from the roof, from when the mountain turned over. 'I felt it,' he says at last. 'Under my hand. Like a horse under you when it's going to bolt.' He picks up the chalk, and looks at the tally board, and puts the chalk down. 'Crew,' he shouts down the drift. 'Down tools.'".
    On discuss { Retract cutting(brannoc). Assert stopped(brannoc). Decrease stirring(fells) by 1. }
  }
  Event sealed_order near brannoc when keeps(brannoc, ?l) and itemKind(?l, margrave_seal) and cutting(brannoc)
    "Brannoc breaks the blue seal, reads, reads again, and folds the letter into his coat. 'Down tools,' he shouts down the drift. Then, to you, quietly: 'If this is forged, I'll find you.'" then {
    Retract cutting(brannoc). Assert stopped(brannoc). Decrease stirring(fells) by 1.
  }
  Rule brannoc_dead when dead(brannoc) and cutting(brannoc) { Retract cutting(brannoc). Decrease stirring(fells) by 1. }
  Topic crew_dreams with crew "Ask the crew how they sleep" when true once {
    Says "'We don't,' says a young one. 'Not down here. You lie down and you're somewhere else, somewhere high up, and the floor's beating.' An older one hits him with a glove. 'Shut up. Brannoc hears that, you're on the face till you drop.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, dream_shared). }
  }
  Topic carvers_face with carvers_folk "Ask the carvers whose face they are carving" when true once {
    Says "One of them stops. He turns his chisel over in his fingers. 'Hers,' he says. 'The Abbess. She looks at you when you sleep.' He goes back to carving. 'She's very kind.'".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, abbess_named). }
  }
  Person carvers_folk "the carvers" at carvers {
    Role "dream-sick miners with chisels". Ancestry human. Calling commoner. Numbers 3. Peaceable.
  }
  Discovery abbess_named "The dream-sick miners carve the face of 'the Abbess', who looks at them when they sleep.".

  // The Quiet Door opens to the humming stone of the Court.
  Thing quiet_slab "the grey door" on quiet_slab_way {
    State seamless blocking "The grey door is shut. It has no handle, no hinge, and no seam.".
    State open "The grey door stands open on a dark, warm way down. There is no sound from below. None at all.".
    Change hum "Hold the humming pebble against the grey door" from seamless to open needing hush_stone.
  }

  // The Veins.
  Observe veinfoot_scene at vein_foot when true "The ladder comes down into a cave of red crystal that gives off its own light, dim and warm, brightening and dimming, brightening and dimming, slowly.".
  Observe red_scene at red_gallery when exhaling(fells) "A gallery of red crystal the colour of a lamp through a hand. The light is dim now, ebbing, and the crystal is cool.".
  Observe red_bright at red_gallery when not exhaling(fells) "A gallery of red crystal, and the crystal is bright, brighter, nearly too bright to look at, and warm, and the light is pulsing, slow and strong.".
  Observe wound_scene at vein_wound when cutting(brannoc) "The Wound. Above you, through a ragged hole, the pick-marks of the cutting face; here below, the crystal is cracked in a great star, and the cracks are weeping. The floor is a pool of warm red brine. It is very hot.".
  Observe wound_quiet at vein_wound when not cutting(brannoc) "The Wound has stopped weeping. The red pool is crusting at its edges, white.".
  Observe crossing_scene at vein_crossing when true "A cave where four ways meet. One climbs toward a gap between ribs of white stone, where a wind blows; one goes down along a smiths' road, paved; one is a crack in the wall that smells of hay; one is the way you came.".
  Person warden_jewel "the Wound's warden" at vein_wound {
    Role "a shape of red crystal that guards the cut". Species jewel_elemental. Level 8.
    Temperament territorial.
    Warns "The red crystal at the edge of the pool stands up. It has the shape of a man, more or less, and the light pulses in it. It does not come closer. It waits to see whether you will.".
  }

  // The Lungs.
  Observe stairfoot_scene at stair_foot when true "The Keepers' Stair ends in a round chamber. Ahead, a passage as wide as a road goes on, and wind comes down it in long gusts, in and out, in and out.".
  Observe lungmouth_scene at lung_mouth when exhaling(fells) "The windpipe opens onto a cavern so vast you cannot see its far side. A warm wind blows past you, out of it, steady.".
  Observe lungmouth_in at lung_mouth when not exhaling(fells) "The windpipe opens onto a cavern so vast you cannot see its far side. The wind is going into it, hard, tugging at your clothes.".
  Observe wind_scene at hall_of_wind when exhaling(fells) "The Hall of Wind: a floor of white stone ribbed like sand, and above, far above, a roof that rises and falls. The wind blows outward now, warm. In the far wall a gap between two ribs of stone stands open.".
  Observe wind_in at hall_of_wind when not exhaling(fells) "The roof of the Hall of Wind is coming down, slowly, and the wind is going in: everything loose on the floor is sliding toward the far wall, where the gap between two ribs is shrieking.".
  Hazard wind_drag "The in-breath" means "Deal (2d6) physical damage to ally unless strength save against (13).".
  Rule wind_takes when at(party, hall_of_wind) and not exhaling(fells)
    says "The wind takes you off your feet and rolls you across the ribbed floor like a leaf." { Assert strikes(wind_drag, party). }
  Observe lee_scene at rib_lee when true "Behind a rib of white stone as tall as a church, the wind does not reach. Others have sheltered here: the ash of a fire, and scratched on the rib in a smith's hand, OUT IS OPEN.".

  // The Smiths' Last Delving.
  Observe gate_scene at delving_gate when true "A gate of black iron in a wall of grey stone, and over it, cut deep, a line of letters: WHAT WAKES, KILLS. WHAT KILLS, WAKES.".
  Discovery doctrine_known "The doctrine of the Hollow Smiths: what wakes, kills; what kills, wakes. They could not kill Thrume, because every killing blow woke him; so they made him sleep, and built the tomb around his heart so that nothing would wake him or kill him again.".
  Observe forge_scene at cold_forge when true "A forge the size of a chapel, cold a thousand years. Anvils, tongs as long as oars, and hammers racked on the wall: iron, bronze, and one of red salt, glassy, unused.".
  Observe library_scene at iron_library when true "A room of shelves, and on the shelves books made of iron leaves, hinged, the letters punched through. Most are too heavy to lift alone.".
  Discovery tomb_stair_known "From the smiths' building-book: 'The third tread of the salt stair is no tread. Prod before you trust.'" {
    Source building_book "the building-book of the Heart-Tomb" at iron_library readable by party.
  }
  Discovery hammers_known "From the smiths' riddle-book: 'Iron wakes the sleeper. Bronze wakes the dead. Strike with what is sleeping, and pass instead.' Beside it, in another hand: 'The salt is his blood, and his blood sleeps.'" {
    Source riddle_book "the riddle-book of the Gate" at iron_library readable by party.
  }
  Discovery face_known "From the smiths' building-book: 'The Sleeper's mouth is open, and his eyes are closed. Go by the eye that is on your left as you face him. Never go where he is awake.'" {
    Source face_leaf "a loose iron leaf about the Sleeper's Face" at iron_library readable by party.
  }
  Discovery doors_known "From the smiths' building-book: 'In the hall of doors, the door is the one that is not there. Every door you can see is a death.'" {
    Source doors_leaf "an iron leaf about the hall of doors" at iron_library readable by party.
  }
  Discovery breaths_known "Scratched on the great rib, and again in the building-book: 'Out is open.' The Room of Three Breaths, and the Wind Gate, are crossed on his out-breath.".
  Observe lee_teaches at rib_lee when true "OUT IS OPEN, says the rib, in a smith's square hand." teaches breaths_known.
  Observe gauge_scene at gauge_room when true "A round room. In the middle, on a pillar, an instrument of brass and grey stone: a needle on a dial, and the dial marked in the smiths' square letters from DEEP to WAKING. Behind it, a tube of glass running up into the rock is full of something red that rises and falls.".
  Observe gauge_low at gauge_room when stirring(fells) < 6 "The needle stands a little below the middle of the dial, where the letters say DREAMING. While you watch it, it ticks once toward WAKING.".
  Observe gauge_high at gauge_room when stirring(fells) >= 6 and not woken(fells) "The needle stands well over toward WAKING, and trembles.".
  Discovery salt_is_blood "The Smiths' Gauge of Sleep measures Thrume's sleep by his blood, which is the red salt in the glass. Every cut in the workings moves the needle toward WAKING.".
  Observe gauge_teaches at gauge_room when true "Under the dial, punched in iron: THIS IS HIS BLOOD. WHERE IT IS CUT, HE STIRS." teaches salt_is_blood.
  Observe cell_scene at master_cell when true "A smith's cell: a cot, a chair, a shelf. In the chair, the bones of a big man in a leather apron, his hands folded on a hammer of grey iron no longer than a hand. On the shelf, a journal of iron leaves.".
  Discovery wheels_known "From the Smith-Master's journal: 'The Gearworks I set so: iron at rest, salt awake, bone at rest. The painters in the Hall of Doctrine have it otherwise, at my order. Let a thief who trusts pictures be scalded.'" {
    Source master_journal "the Smith-Master's journal" at master_cell readable by party.
  }
  Discovery ardath_known "From the Smith-Master's journal: 'Ardath stays with the false heart. He has asked to. He says someone must keep the lie, so that nobody looks for the truth. If you come to him, say the doctrine, and he will know you for ours.'" {
    Source master_journal_end "the last leaves of the Smith-Master's journal" at master_cell readable by party.
  }
  Kind smith_token "the Smith-Master's hammer, grey iron no longer than a hand" is treasure worth 0 weighing 1.
  Item master_hammer "the Smith-Master's little hammer" is smith_token at master_cell.
  Observe gate_teaches at delving_gate when true "WHAT WAKES, KILLS. WHAT KILLS, WAKES." teaches doctrine_known.

  // The Dream-Hollows.
  Observe hmouth_scene at hollow_mouth when true "A soft dark. The walls are not stone here; they give a little under the hand, and are warm. Somewhere below, you can smell hay and summer.".
  Observe field_scene at dream_field when true "A meadow, inside the mountain, under a sky. The sky is too close: you could throw a stone into the clouds. Sheep graze, and do not cast shadows. A shepherd boy sleeps against a stone with his crook across his knees. This is something Thrume is dreaming, and it is quite real.".
  Person dream_boy "the dreamed shepherd" at dream_field {
    Role "a boy asleep against a stone". Ancestry human. Peaceable.
    Seen when dreamt(viewer).
  }
  Topic dream_boy_talk with dream_boy "Wake the dreamed shepherd" when true once {
    Says "The boy opens his eyes. They are the colour of red salt. 'He was happy here,' he says. 'Before. The sky was close and the grass was warm and we walked.' He looks up the meadow, to where the grass ends in grey, like ash. 'They eat it,' he says. 'From the edges. Every night there is less of it.' He shuts his eyes again.".
    On discuss { Assert knows(actor, court_feeds). }
  }
  Discovery court_feeds "Something is eating Thrume's dreams from the edges.".
  Observe field_edge at dream_field when true "At the top of the meadow the grass goes grey, then greyer, then simply stops, as if it had been eaten.".
  Observe hunger_scene at hunger_shaft when true "A shaft going down into cold. Frost on the walls, in a warm mountain. Long scratches in the frost, too far apart for any hand.".
  Person hunger "the hunger" at hunger_shaft {
    Role "a long, starved shape in the frost: Thrume's dream of a hard winter". Species wendigo. Level 9.
    Temperament ambush.
    Warns "Something unfolds out of the frost at the bottom of the shaft, too tall and too thin, and turns a face toward you that is mostly teeth.".
    Comes "The hunger comes up the shaft at you on its long arms, faster than anything that thin should move.".
  }
  Observe approach_scene at hush_approach when true "The way goes on down through the soft dark, and the sound goes out of the world. Your footsteps make none. Your voice, when you try it, makes none. Ahead there is a grey light, and a city.".

  Objective stop_cutting when cutting(brannoc) and knows(party, salt_is_blood) "Every day Brannoc cuts, Thrume stirs. The Margravine's seal would stop him, or the mountain itself.".
  Objective go_down when knows(party, hush_named) and not freed(col) "The sleepers from the Red Lantern were taken down to Hush.".
}
data/adventures/what-tessary-owes/city.k:
Module tessary "What Tessary Owes" {
  Description "Tessary on the Ossel, a city of salt and paper built on piles over a drowned Aenean city, in the fortnight before the Feast of Settlement: the Long Muster has come home from eleven years' war, and some of its soldiers are walking into the sea.".

  // ── The delta ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The Ossel comes down out of the marsh country in a dozen channels and meets the sea at Tessary. The city stands on
  // piles and fill along the last ridge of dry ground; north of its Tidewall is the outer basin, where the old city lies
  // under the water and comes up at the ebb.
  Place imbar "Imbar" is plane.
  Place ossel "the Ossel delta" is region within imbar.
  Place saltmarsh "the salt-marsh" is wilderness within ossel at 0, 1.
  Place tessary "Tessary" is settlement within ossel at 1, 1.
  Place lowtide "Lowtide" is site within ossel at 1, 0.
  Initially Assert terrain(ossel, marsh).

  Place causeway_end "the Causeway, at the marsh's edge" is room within saltmarsh at 0, 0.
  Passage causeway "the Causeway" is causeway between causeway_end and landgate taking 1 hour.
  Observe causeway_scene at causeway_end when not dark() "The marsh road comes out of the reeds onto a causeway of fitted stone, older than the road, raised a man's height above the saltings. It runs straight for a league to a wall on a low ridge: Tessary, a long grey city with its back to the sea, a smoke of salt-boiling over its eastern end and the masts of its harbour standing up behind it like reeds. The tide is a sound you hear before you see it, a long breath on the far side of everything.".
  Observe causeway_night at causeway_end when dark() "The causeway runs out ahead of you into the dark, a pale stone line over black saltings. A league off, Tessary is a row of lamps along a ridge, and above the lamps, very faintly, the masts.".
  Observe causeway_carts at causeway_end when not dark() "Carts of peat and rushes are coming in ahead of you, and one going out, empty, with a soldier asleep in the back of it in a red coat gone brown.".

  // ── Tessary ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // Streets, on the city's own grid: the Tidewall and the Yard along the sea, the Lettered Quarter and the Terraces in
  // the middle, the Withies, the Landgate and Panhythe along the landward side.
  Place throat_head "the head of the Swatch Stair" is room within tessary at 0, 0 outdoors.
  Place tidewall "the Tidewall" is room within tessary at 1, 0 outdoors.
  Place legion_yard "the Legion Yard" is room within tessary at 2, 0 outdoors.
  Place tideline_steps "the Watersteps" is room within tessary at 0, 1 outdoors.
  Place scriveners_row "Scriveners' Row" is room within tessary at 1, 1 outdoors.
  Place terraces "the Terraces" is room within tessary at 2, 1 outdoors.
  Place withies "the Withies" is room within tessary at 0, 2 outdoors.
  Place landgate "the Landgate" is room within tessary at 1, 2 outdoors.
  Place saltgate "Panhythe" is room within tessary at 2, 2 outdoors.
  Place pans "the Pans" is room within tessary at 3, 2 outdoors.

  Passage withy_walk "the Withy boardwalk" is bridge between landgate and withies taking 5 minutes.
  Passage inkhorn_street "Inkhorn Street" is path between landgate and scriveners_row taking 5 minutes.
  Passage salt_street "the Salt Road" is path between landgate and saltgate taking 5 minutes.
  Passage pan_dykes "the pan-dykes" is path between saltgate and pans taking 10 minutes.
  Passage steps_walk "the boardwalk to the Steps" is bridge between withies and tideline_steps taking 5 minutes.
  Passage sea_lane "the sea-lane" is path between tideline_steps and throat_head taking 5 minutes.
  Passage wall_stair "the Wall Stair" is steps between scriveners_row and tidewall.
  Passage wall_walk "the wall-walk" is path between tidewall and throat_head taking 5 minutes.
  Passage yard_gate "the Yard gate" is gate between tidewall and legion_yard.
  Passage terrace_steps "the Terrace Steps" is steps between scriveners_row and terraces.
  Passage terrace_lane "the lane behind the Yard" is path between terraces and legion_yard taking 5 minutes.
  Passage salt_lane "Brine Lane" is path between terraces and saltgate taking 10 minutes.

  // The Landgate: where the Causeway comes in, and everyone who comes in reads the board.
  Observe landgate_scene at landgate when not dark() and not visitedBefore(landgate) "Inside the gate is a three-cornered square of trodden shell, loud with carts. A board on the gatehouse wall is shingled with bills, three deep: the Feast of Settlement, a fortnight hence; a reward for a stolen goose; rooms; a hiring hall in Panhythe that pays veterans by the day; the eel-fair postponed; a lecture at the Notaries' Hall on the Aenean subjunctive, admission one penny, discussion after. In the corner a little chapel to Saint Evenhand has a pair of brass scales over its door. Somebody has polished the scales.".
  Observe landgate_scene_again at landgate when not dark() and visitedBefore(landgate) "The Landgate's square: carts, the shingled bill-board, Saint Evenhand's polished scales over the chapel door.".
  Observe landgate_night at landgate when dark() "The square is empty but for a watchman with a lantern and a cat on the bill-board. The bills move a little in the wind off the sea.".
  Observe landgate_bunting at landgate when not dark() and not feastEve() and night(ossel) < 5 "Red bunting for the Muster's homecoming is still up over the gate, a week old and sagging. Under it a man with a bucket is pasting a new bill over the old: THE BOARD OF MOIETIES WILL HEAR THE QUESTION OF THE VETERANS' SETTLEMENT ON THE THIRTEENTH DAY, FROM TEN IN THE MORNING.".
  Observe landgate_bunting_down at landgate when not dark() and not feastEve() and night(ossel) >= 5 and not voted(ossel) "The homecoming bunting has come down, or blown down; a length of it is trodden into the shell by the gate. The bills on the board are four deep now, and nobody is pasting any more.".

  // The Withies: stilt houses over the backwater, where the rank and file came home to.
  Observe withies_scene at withies when not dark() and not visitedBefore(withies) "The Withies stand on piles over a backwater of the Ossel: tarred houses on stilts, joined by boardwalks that sway, every one with a ladder down to a boat and a row of eel-traps drying on the rail. Washing hangs between the houses. So do red coats, a good many of them, airing. A girl is mending a net with a soldier's bayonet.".
  Observe withies_scene_again at withies when not dark() and visitedBefore(withies) "The Withies: swaying boardwalks, eel-traps on the rails, red coats airing between the stilt-houses.".
  Observe withies_night at withies when dark() "Lamps in the stilt-houses, and the backwater black under the boardwalks. Somebody is singing a marching song very slowly in one of the houses, and stops, and starts again.".

  // The Watersteps: the sea-stair at the end of the Withies, where the called leave their boots.
  Observe steps_scene at tideline_steps when not visitedBefore(tideline_steps) "Broad stone steps go down from the end of the boardwalk into the sea, twenty of them above the high-water mark and nobody knows how many below. They are older than everything around them. The stone is cut with something like letters, worn to dimples.".
  Observe steps_scene_again at tideline_steps when visitedBefore(tideline_steps) "The Watersteps, old and worn to dimples, going down into the sea.".
  Observe steps_boots at tideline_steps when bootsOnSteps(ossel) "On the top step stand pairs of boots, set neatly side by side, toes to the water, the way a soldier sets them by his cot. Nobody has moved them. Nobody will.".
  Observe steps_water at tideline_steps when lowWater() "The sea has drawn back a long way, and the steps go down and down into weed and wet sand, and out there in the grey, very low, the tops of walls.".
  Observe steps_full at tideline_steps when not lowWater() "The water stands high on the steps, slopping and green.".

  // The Swatch Stair, and the Swatch: the channel the basin drains by.
  Observe throat_scene at throat_head when not visitedBefore(throat_head) "At the west end of the Tidewall the wall-walk breaks off at a stair that goes straight down the face of the wall into the basin. A chain hangs beside it for a handrail. Below, the Swatch: the one deep channel through which the outer basin fills and empties twice a day, with a noise like a slow mill.".
  Observe throat_scene_again at throat_head when visitedBefore(throat_head) "The head of the Swatch Stair, where the wall-walk breaks off, with its chain for a handrail and the Swatch milling below.".
  Observe throat_low_dark at throat_head when lowWater() and dark() "The basin is out. Below the stair the drowned city lies in the dark, and you can hear it draining, a thousand small waters running off stone. Far out, one lantern moves, low to the ground, and stops, and moves again.".
  Observe throat_low at throat_head when lowWater() and not dark() "The basin is out. Below the stair lies a city of wet stone: roofs, a colonnade, the dome of something, streets with weed lying flat in them like combed hair. Figures are moving down there, small, bent over, looking for things.".

  // The Tidewall: the barrage on Aenean footings.
  Observe tidewall_scene at tidewall when not visitedBefore(tidewall) "The Tidewall runs the whole length of the city between the houses and the sea, broad enough on top for two carts. Its lower courses are not the city's: great blocks, tight-fitted, with no mortar, carved at intervals with a pair of scales. The city built its wall on top of someone else's. On the landward side a stair goes down into the Lettered Quarter.".
  Observe tidewall_scene_again at tidewall when visitedBefore(tidewall) "The Tidewall, broad as a road, with the sea on one side and the city on the other.".
  Observe tidewall_day at tidewall when not dark() "Fishermen sit along the parapet with lines, and the smell of vinegar comes down the wall from a brazier on a barrow.".

  // The Legion Yard and the Oath Stone.
  Observe yard_scene at legion_yard when true "A parade ground of beaten shell inside the Tidewall, ringed with empty barracks. In the middle of it, on a plinth, stands the Oath Stone: a slab of black stone as tall as a man, salvaged from the drowned city two hundred years ago, smooth as a hearthstone where eleven thousand hands have been laid on it. Cut into its face, small and fine, are lines that are not writing and not ornament: ruled lines, like a ledger's.".
  Observe yard_empty at legion_yard when not feastEve() and night(ossel) < 5 "The barracks doors stand open. The Muster was paid off a week ago and told to go home, and the Yard has nobody in it but the gulls.".
  Observe yard_empty_later at legion_yard when not feastEve() and night(ossel) >= 5 "The barracks doors stand open on nothing. Somebody has chalked a name on one of them, and somebody else has washed it off, and the gulls have the Yard.".

  // Scriveners' Row, the heart of the Lettered Quarter.
